## 0.3 Define generic helper functions
```{r}
# Helper function to quote arguments (similar to Perl's qw)
qw <- function(...) {
  sapply(match.call()[-1], deparse)
}

# Create an empty data frame with specified dimensions and column names
createEmptyDf = function( nrow, ncol, colnames = c() ){
  data.frame( matrix( vector(), nrow, ncol, dimnames = list( c(), colnames ) ) )
}

# Generate a distance dataframe from a distance matrix and a label
make_dist_dataframe<-function(fn_dist,fn_name){ # distance matrix, name tag
  fn_cbs<-attr(fn_dist, "Labels") # Extract labels from the distance matrix
  fn_cbpairs<-carbon_pairs %>% select(carbon1,carbon2,key) # Select key columns from the reference carbon_pairs dataframe
  fn_tmp1<-dist_long(fn_dist) # Transform distance matrix to long format
  fn_tmp2<-data.frame(rows=fn_cbs,cols=fn_cbs,distance=0) # Create self-to-self distance (distance = 0)
  fn_tmp3<-fn_tmp1 %>% select(cols,rows,distance) %>% rename(rows="cols",cols="rows") # Create mirrored pairs to ensure bidirectional coverage
  fn_tmp<-bind_rows(fn_tmp1,fn_tmp2,fn_tmp3) # Combine all distance entries
  # fn_tmp<-bind_rows(fn_tmp,fn_tmp3) # Combine all distance entries
  colnames(fn_tmp)<-c("carbon1","carbon2",paste("dist",fn_name,sep="_"))
  fn_cbpairs<-left_join(fn_cbpairs,fn_tmp,by=c("carbon1","carbon2")) # Join with the reference dataframe
  return(fn_cbpairs)
}

# Generate ggplot2-style colors using HCL scales
ggColorHue <- function(n, l=65) {
  hues <- seq(15, 375, length=n+1)
  hcl(h=hues, l=l, c=100)[1:n]
}

# Calculate distance based on Spearman's rank correlation (1 - rho)
spearman_dist <- function(x) {
  # Use 1 - correlation as distance
  as.dist(1 - cor(x, method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs"))
}

Sys.time()
```

# 1 Carbon sources
## 1.1 Load carbon source metadata and define categories
```{r}
# Define metabolic categories
carbon_categories<-c("Upper Glycolysis","Lower Glycolysis","Pentose Phosphate","TCA cycle","Entner Doudoroff","Amino acid-derived TCA input")
# Load carbon source mapping (Abbreviations and Categories)
carbon_names<-paste(getwd(),"Carbon_Info","Carbon_name.csv",sep="/") %>% read_csv()
# Assign colors to each metabolic category using a named vector for efficiency
category_colors <- c(
  "Upper Glycolysis" = "#0072B2",
  "Lower Glycolysis" = "#E69F00",
  "Pentose Phosphate" = "#56B4E9",
  "TCA cycle" = "#009E73",
  "Entner Doudoroff" = "#CC79A7",
  "Amino acid-derived TCA input" = "#8FD926"
)

# Map category colors back to the main dataframe
carbon_names$Category_col <- category_colors[carbon_names$Category]

# Generate all possible carbon source pairs for matrix operations
# upper triangle (pairwise combinations)
df_upper <- combn(carbon_names$Abb, 2) %>% t() %>% as.data.frame()
colnames(df_upper) <- qw(carbon1, carbon2)
df_upper$key <- "upper"

# diagonal (self-to-self)
df_diag <- data.frame(carbon1 = carbon_names$Abb, carbon2 = carbon_names$Abb, key = "diag")

# lower triangle (mirrored)
df_lower <- df_upper %>% rename(carbon1 = "carbon2", carbon2 = "carbon1")
df_lower$key <- "lower"

# Combine into a comprehensive pairs dataframe
carbon_pairs_pre <- bind_rows(df_upper, df_diag, df_lower)

# Join category information for both carbons in a pair
carbon_pairs_pre <- carbon_pairs_pre %>%
  left_join(carbon_names %>% select(carbon1 = Abb, category1 = Category), by = "carbon1") %>%
  left_join(carbon_names %>% select(carbon2 = Abb, category2 = Category), by = "carbon2")

# Determine if the pair belongs to the same category or is a "between-category" pair
carbon_pairs_pre <- carbon_pairs_pre %>%
  mutate(pair_category = ifelse(category1 == category2, category1, "between"))

# Assign colors to the pair categories
carbon_pairs_pre <- carbon_pairs_pre %>%
  left_join(
    data.frame(pair_category = c(names(category_colors), "between"),
               category_col = c(as.character(category_colors), "black")),
    by = "pair_category"
  )

Sys.time()
```

## 1.3 Essentiality-based Metabolic Distance from 7 GEMs and iML1515 (OLD VERSION)
### 1.3.1 Load essential reactions defined by genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs)
```{r, fig.height=8,fig.width=10, dpi=300}
# Function to read essential reaction data and calculate pairwise distances
calculate_gem_distances <- function(csv_filename, strain_id) {
  # Load mapping for carbon abbreviations
  carbon_map <- read_csv(file.path(getwd(), "FBA","growth_media", "Abb_carbon.csv"))
  
  # Load essential reaction list for the specific strain
  ess_data <- read_csv(file.path(getwd(), "FBA", "output_rev10", "essential_by_species", csv_filename))
  
  # Join with mapping and filter out unassigned carbons
  ess_data <- ess_data %>%
    left_join(carbon_map, by = "carbon") %>%
    filter(!is.na(Abb))
  
  # Identify unique reactions and carbons
  unique_reactions <- unique(ess_data$reaction_id)
  unique_carbons <- unique(ess_data$Abb)
  
  # Create a binary matrix (Carbon x Reaction)
  # Initialize with zeros
  binary_mat <- matrix(0, 
                       nrow = length(unique_carbons), 
                       ncol = length(unique_reactions),
                       dimnames = list(unique_carbons, unique_reactions))
  
  # Fill the matrix: Set 1 if the reaction is essential for that carbon source
  for (carbon in unique_carbons) {
    active_rxns <- ess_data$reaction_id[ess_data$Abb == carbon]
    binary_mat[carbon, colnames(binary_mat) %in% active_rxns] <- 1
  }
  
  # Calculate pairwise Manhattan distances between carbon sources
  dist_mat <- as.matrix(dist(binary_mat, method = "manhattan"))
  
  # Convert to long format for easier merging
  dist_df <- reshape2::melt(dist_mat)
  colnames(dist_df) <- c("carbon1", "carbon2", paste0("rxndiff_", strain_id))
  
  return(dist_df)
}

# Define filenames and corresponding strain names
model_files <- c("iML1515__essential_only.csv", "ECOR11__essential_only.csv",
                 "ECOR31__essential_only.csv", "ECOR32__essential_only.csv",
                 "ECOR38__essential_only.csv", "ECOR50__essential_only.csv",
                 "ECOR55__essential_only.csv", "ECOR71__essential_only.csv")

strain_names <- c("MG1655", "ECOR11", "ECOR31", "ECOR32", "ECOR38", "ECOR50", "ECOR55", "ECOR71")

# Iteratively load data and merge into a single dataframe
combined_dist_df <- NULL

for (i in seq_along(model_files)) {
  temp_dist <- calculate_gem_distances(model_files[i], strain_names[i])
  
  if (is.null(combined_dist_df)) {
    combined_dist_df <- temp_dist
  } else {
    combined_dist_df <- left_join(combined_dist_df, temp_dist, by = c("carbon1", "carbon2"))
  }
}

# Calculate median distance across all models (excluding the reference MG1655)
# This provides a robust representative metabolic distance
median_calculation_df <- combined_dist_df %>% select(-carbon1, -carbon2, -rxndiff_MG1655)
combined_dist_df$rxndiff_median <- apply(as.matrix(median_calculation_df), 1, median, na.rm = TRUE)

# Merge back with the primary carbon_pairs dataset
carbon_pairs_pre_cols <- colnames(carbon_pairs_pre)
carbon_pairs_updated <- left_join(carbon_pairs_pre, combined_dist_df, by = c("carbon1", "carbon2"))

## --- Visualization: Correlation between models ---
# Plot a pair-panel to check consistency of metabolic distances across different models
# Only using 'upper' triangle pairs to avoid redundancy
carbon_pairs_updated %>%
  filter(key == "upper") %>%
  select(starts_with("rxndiff_")) %>%
  psych::pairs.panels(method = "spearman", 
                      line.col = "red", 
                      pch = 21, 
                      main = "Consistency of Metabolic Distances across GEMs")

# Finalize the carbon_pairs dataframe for subsequent analysis
carbon_pairs <- carbon_pairs_updated %>%
  select(all_of(carbon_pairs_pre_cols), rxndiff_median, rxndiff_MG1655)


# Essentiality-based metabolic distance matrix derived from iML1515
carbon_matrix_iml<-carbon_pairs %>%
  select(carbon1,carbon2,rxndiff_MG1655) %>%
  filter(!is.na(rxndiff_MG1655)) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon2,values_from = rxndiff_MG1655) %>%
  column_to_rownames("carbon1") %>%
  as.matrix()
my_ins<-colnames(carbon_matrix_iml)
my_ins<-my_ins[order(my_ins)]
carbon_matrix_iml<-carbon_matrix_iml[my_ins,my_ins]

Sys.time()
```

### 1.3.3 Construction of the integrated essential reaction matrix (Supplementary Data)
```{r, message=FALSE}
# Function to generate a binary essentiality matrix for a specific GEM
generate_essential_matrix <- function(csv_filename, strain_id) {
  # Load carbon abbreviation mapping
  carbon_map <- read_csv(file.path(getwd(), "FBA", "growth_media","Abb_carbon.csv"))
  
  # Load raw essentiality data
  raw_data <- read_csv(file.path(getwd(), "FBA", "output_rev10", "essential_by_species", csv_filename))
  
  # Join and filter valid carbon sources
  processed_data <- raw_data %>%
    left_join(carbon_map, by = "carbon") %>%
    filter(!is.na(Abb))
  
  # Get unique reactions and carbons to define matrix dimensions
  unique_rxns <- unique(processed_data$reaction_id)
  unique_abbs <- unique(processed_data$Abb)
  
  # Initialize the binary matrix with zeros
  # Using strain_id as a grouping column for the final integrated table
  essential_mat <- matrix(0, 
                          nrow = length(unique_abbs), 
                          ncol = length(unique_rxns),
                          dimnames = list(unique_abbs, unique_rxns))
  
  # Fill the matrix (1: Essential, 0: Non-essential)
  for (carbon in unique_abbs) {
    active_rxns <- processed_data$reaction_id[processed_data$Abb == carbon]
    essential_mat[carbon, colnames(essential_mat) %in% active_rxns] <- 1
  }
  
  # Convert to a dataframe and add strain identification
  essential_df <- as.data.frame(essential_mat) %>%
    rownames_to_column("carbon_name") %>%
    mutate(strain = strain_id) %>%
    select(strain, carbon_name, everything())
  
  return(essential_df)
}

# Integrate all models into a single master matrix
integrated_ess_mat <- NULL

for (i in seq_along(model_files)) {
  temp_df <- generate_essential_matrix(model_files[i], strain_names[i])
  
  if (is.null(integrated_ess_mat)) {
    integrated_ess_mat <- temp_df
  } else {
    # bind_rows automatically handles cases where reaction sets (columns) differ between models,
    # filling missing entries with NA.
    integrated_ess_mat <- bind_rows(integrated_ess_mat, temp_df)
  }
}

# Handle NAs: Reactions absent in a specific model are treated as non-essential (0)
# This ensures a complete binary matrix for the supplementary material
integrated_ess_mat[is.na(integrated_ess_mat)] <- 0

# Define carbon sources to exclude from global statistics
excluded_carbons <- qw(Glu, Ser, Cit, Arg, His, Lys, Thr, Arab)

# Final output object
ess_rxn_mat_all <- integrated_ess_mat %>% 
  filter(carbon_name %nin% excluded_carbons)

Sys.time()
```

### 1.3.5 Venn Diagram: Overlap of Essential Reactions
```{r, fig.height=3, fig.width=3, dpi=300}
# Define representative carbon sources
carbon_reps <- qw(Glc, Succ, Lac)

# Filter the integrated essential reaction matrix for a specific strain (e.g., ECOR11)
# Transform to long format to identify presence/absence of each reaction
ess_rxn_long <- ess_rxn_mat_all %>% 
  filter(strain == "ECOR11" & carbon_name %in% carbon_reps) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = -c(strain, carbon_name), names_to = "rxn", values_to = "is_essential")

# Create a list where each element contains the names of essential reactions for that carbon source
venn_list <- list(
  Glc= ess_rxn_long$rxn[ess_rxn_long$carbon_name == "Glc" & ess_rxn_long$is_essential == 1],
  Succ = ess_rxn_long$rxn[ess_rxn_long$carbon_name == "Succ" & ess_rxn_long$is_essential == 1],
  Lac = ess_rxn_long$rxn[ess_rxn_long$carbon_name == "Lac" & ess_rxn_long$is_essential == 1]
)

# Generate the Venn diagram
# Note: venn.diagram returns a gList object that needs to be drawn via grid.draw
venn_plot <- venn.diagram(
  x = venn_list,
  filename = NULL,         # Do not save to file, return as an object
  disable.logging = TRUE,  # Suppress log files in the working directory
  fill = c("#0072B2", "#009E73", "#E69F00"), # Colors for Glc, Succ, Lac
  alpha = 0.6,             # Transparency for overlapping regions
  lty = "blank",           # Remove borders for a cleaner look
  cat.cex = 1.2,           # Category label size
  cex = 1.2,               # Numerical label size
  main = "Essential Reaction Overlap (ECOR11)"
)

# Draw the Venn diagram using the grid package
grid::grid.newpage()
grid::grid.draw(venn_plot)

# Data Inspection: Identify reactions essential for Glucose but NOT for Succinate
# Using basic set logic (setdiff) which is standard in R
glc_unique_to_succ <- setdiff(venn_list$Glucose, venn_list$Succinate)
print("Reactions essential for Glucose but not for Succinate:")
print(glc_unique_to_succ)

Sys.time()

```
### 1.3.6 Summary Statistics of Essential Reactions
```{r}
# Define carbon sources to exclude from global statistics
excluded_carbons <- qw(Glu, Ser, Cit, Arg, His, Lys, Thr, Arab)

# Filter dataset: Focus on 7 ECOR strains and representative carbon sources
ess_stats_mat <- ess_rxn_mat_all %>% 
  filter(strain != "MG1655" & !(carbon_name %in% excluded_carbons)) %>% 
  select(-strain, -carbon_name) %>% 
  as.matrix()

# 1. Distribution of the number of essential reactions per condition
# (Each row represents a specific strain on a specific carbon source)
essential_counts <- rowSums(ess_stats_mat)
print("Summary of the number of essential reactions per condition:")
print(summary(essential_counts))

# 2. Number of "Core" essential reactions
# Reactions that are essential across ALL tested strains and ALL carbon sources
# Using colAlls from matrixStats for efficiency, or a simple logical check
core_reactions_n <- sum(colSums(ess_stats_mat) == nrow(ess_stats_mat))
cat("# of core reactions (essential in all conditions):", core_reactions_n, "\n")

# 3. Number of "Pan" essential reactions
# Reactions that are essential in at least ONE condition (strain or carbon source)
pan_reactions_n <- sum(colSums(ess_stats_mat) > 0)
cat("# of pan reactions (essential in at least one condition):", pan_reactions_n, "\n")

# 4. List of carbon sources included in this statistical summary
included_carbons <- ess_rxn_mat_all %>% 
  filter(strain != "MG1655" & !(carbon_name %in% excluded_carbons)) %>% 
  pull(carbon_name) %>% 
  unique()

print("Carbon sources analyzed in this summary:")
print(included_carbons)

Sys.time()
```
### 1.3.7 Elbow & Scree (iML1515) (Fig. S9i)
```{r, fig.height=4,fig.width=5}
# 1. Perform hierarchical clustering (Ward's method)
my_ins<-sort(ecor_carbons)
dist_theory<-carbon_matrix_iml[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------ essentiality-based distance (70 gem)
# Hierarchical clustering using Ward's D2 method
hc_result <- hclust(dist_theory, method = cl_method)
plot(hc_result)

# 2. Calculate WSS (within-cluster sum of squares) for k = 1 to 10
k_range <- 1:10
wss_values <- sapply(k_range, function(k) {
  # Get cluster assignments for each object
  ct <- cutree(hc_result, k = k)
  
  # Sum the squared distances from the centroid within each cluster
  sum(sapply(unique(ct), function(cluster) {
    # Subset of the distance matrix for data belonging to the current cluster
    sub_dist <- as.matrix(carbon_matrix_iml)[ct == cluster, ct == cluster, drop = FALSE]
    # Calculate within-cluster sum of squares (WSS) from the distance matrix
    sum(sub_dist^2) / (2 * nrow(sub_dist))
  }))
})

# 3. Create a data frame for plotting
elbow_df <- data.frame(k = k_range, wss = wss_values)

# 4. Plot the elbow diagram with ggplot2
# Elbow Method for Optimal Number of Clusters
p_elbow <- ggplot(elbow_df, aes(x = k, y = wss)) +
  geom_line(color = "black", size = 1.5) +
  geom_point(color = "black", size = 4) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 2, linetype = 2, color = "red") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = k_range) + 
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,6000),breaks = get_breaks(from = 0,to = 6000,by = 2000))+
  theme_pubr(base_size = 20) +
  font("xy.text",size=26)+
  font("xylab",size=26)+
  labs(
    x = "Number of clusters",
    y = "Total within-cluster\n sum of squares"
  )

print(p_elbow)



# 1. Create a data frame for plotting from the fusion height data
# hc_result$height stores the height (dissimilarity) at which clusters are merged, in ascending order
# k corresponds to [2, 3, 4, ..., total number of data points]
n <- length(hc_result$order)
height_df <- data.frame(
```

## 1.4 Essentiality-based distance derived from 70 EOCR strains
### 1.4.1 Load essential reactions defined by genome-scale metabolic models
```{r, fig.height=8,fig.width=12, dpi=300}
# Function to read essential reaction data and calculate pairwise distances
calculate_gem_distances_all <- function(csv_filename, strain_id) {
  # Load mapping for carbon abbreviations
  carbon_map <- read_csv(file.path(getwd(), "FBA","growth_media", "Abb_carbon.csv"))
  
  # Load essential reaction list for the specific strain
  ess_data <- read_csv(file.path(getwd(), "FBA", "output_rev10", "essential_by_species", csv_filename))
  
  # Join with mapping and filter out unassigned carbons
  ess_data <- ess_data %>%
    left_join(carbon_map, by = "carbon") %>%
    filter(!is.na(Abb))
  
  # Identify unique reactions and carbons
  unique_reactions <- unique(ess_data$reaction_id)
  unique_carbons <- unique(ess_data$Abb)
  
  # Create a binary matrix (Carbon x Reaction)
  # Initialize with zeros
  binary_mat <- matrix(0, 
                       nrow = length(unique_carbons), 
                       ncol = length(unique_reactions),
                       dimnames = list(unique_carbons, unique_reactions))
  
  # Fill the matrix: Set 1 if the reaction is essential for that carbon source
  for (carbon in unique_carbons) {
    active_rxns <- ess_data$reaction_id[ess_data$Abb == carbon]
    binary_mat[carbon, colnames(binary_mat) %in% active_rxns] <- 1
  }
  
  # Calculate pairwise Manhattan distances between carbon sources
  dist_mat <- as.matrix(dist(binary_mat, method = "manhattan"))
  
  # Convert to long format for easier merging
  dist_df <- reshape2::melt(dist_mat)
  colnames(dist_df) <- c("carbon1", "carbon2", paste0("rxndiff_", strain_id))
  
  return(dist_df)
}

# Define filenames and corresponding strain names
# 1. Generate sequential numbers from 01 to 72, excluding 29 and 52
nums <- sprintf("%02d", setdiff(1:72, c(29, 52)))

# 2. Create a list of model names combining iML1515 and ECORXX
model_names_all <- c("iML1515", paste0("ECOR", nums))

# 3. Append the common suffix to complete the file name list (71 files in total)
model_files_all <- paste0(model_names_all, "__essential_only.csv")

strain_names_all <- model_names_all
strain_names_all[1]<-"MG1655"

# Iteratively load data and merge into a single dataframe
combined_dist_df_all <- NULL

for (i in seq_along(model_files_all)) {
  temp_dist <- calculate_gem_distances_all(model_files_all[i], strain_names_all[i])
  
  if (is.null(combined_dist_df_all)) {
    combined_dist_df_all <- temp_dist
  } else {
    combined_dist_df_all <- left_join(combined_dist_df_all, temp_dist, by = c("carbon1", "carbon2"))
  }
}

# Calculate median distance across all models (excluding the reference MG1655)

median_calculation_df_all <- combined_dist_df_all %>% select(-carbon1, -carbon2, -rxndiff_MG1655)
combined_dist_df_all$rxndiff_median <- apply(as.matrix(median_calculation_df_all), 1, median, na.rm = TRUE)
combined_dist_df_all$rxndiff_mean <- apply(as.matrix(median_calculation_df_all), 1, mean, na.rm = TRUE)

# Merge back with the primary carbon_pairs dataset
carbon_pairs_pre_cols <- colnames(carbon_pairs_pre)
carbon_pairs_updated_all <- left_join(carbon_pairs_pre, combined_dist_df_all, by = c("carbon1", "carbon2"))

## --- Visualization: Correlation between models ---
```

### 1.4.2 Construction of the integrated essential reaction matrix (Supplementary Data) for all 70 models
```{r, message=FALSE}
# Function to generate a binary essentiality matrix for a specific GEM
generate_essential_matrix_70gems <- function(csv_filename, strain_id) {
  # Load carbon abbreviation mapping
  carbon_map <- read_csv(file.path(getwd(), "FBA", "growth_media","Abb_carbon.csv"))
  
  # Load raw essentiality data
  raw_data <- read_csv(file.path(getwd(), "FBA", "output_rev10", "essential_by_species", csv_filename))
  
  # Join and filter valid carbon sources
  processed_data <- raw_data %>%
    left_join(carbon_map, by = "carbon") %>%
    filter(!is.na(Abb))
  
  # Get unique reactions and carbons to define matrix dimensions
  unique_rxns <- unique(processed_data$reaction_id)
  unique_abbs <- unique(processed_data$Abb)
  
  # Initialize the binary matrix with zeros
  # Using strain_id as a grouping column for the final integrated table
  essential_mat <- matrix(0, 
                          nrow = length(unique_abbs), 
                          ncol = length(unique_rxns),
                          dimnames = list(unique_abbs, unique_rxns))
  
  # Fill the matrix (1: Essential, 0: Non-essential)
  for (carbon in unique_abbs) {
    active_rxns <- processed_data$reaction_id[processed_data$Abb == carbon]
    essential_mat[carbon, colnames(essential_mat) %in% active_rxns] <- 1
  }
  
  # Convert to a dataframe and add strain identification
  essential_df <- as.data.frame(essential_mat) %>%
    rownames_to_column("carbon_name") %>%
    mutate(strain = strain_id) %>%
    select(strain, carbon_name, everything())
  
  return(essential_df)
}

# Integrate all models into a single master matrix
integrated_ess_mat_70gems <- NULL

for (i in seq_along(model_files_all)) {
  temp_df <- generate_essential_matrix_70gems(model_files_all[i], strain_names_all[i])
  
  if (is.null(integrated_ess_mat_70gems)) {
    integrated_ess_mat_70gems <- temp_df
  } else {
    # bind_rows automatically handles cases where reaction sets (columns) differ between models,
    # filling missing entries with NA.
    integrated_ess_mat_70gems <- bind_rows(integrated_ess_mat_70gems, temp_df)
  }
}

# Handle NAs: Reactions absent in a specific model are treated as non-essential (0)
# This ensures a complete binary matrix for the supplementary material
# integrated_ess_mat_70gems[is.na(integrated_ess_mat_70gems)] <- 0

# Define carbon sources to exclude from global statistics
excluded_carbons <- qw(Glu, Ser, Cit, Arg, His, Lys, Thr, Arab)

# Final output object
ess_rxn_mat_all_70gems <- integrated_ess_mat_70gems %>% 
  filter(carbon_name %nin% excluded_carbons)

Sys.time()
```

### 1.4.10 Clustering
```{r,fig.width=4,fig.height=3,dpi=300}
# 1. Clustering based on experimental evolutionary distances
# Define the number of theoretical clusters (k)
k_val <- 2

my_ins<-sort(ecor_carbons)
dist_theory<-carbon_matrix_70gem[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------ essentiality-based distance (70 gem)
# Hierarchical clustering using Ward's D2 method
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = cl_method)
cluster_theory    <- cutree(hc_theory, k = k_val)

# Create a mapping table for carbon sources and their assigned clusters
my_tmp<-data.frame(carbon=names(cluster_theory),theory=cluster_theory)
carbon_clust_tbl<-my_tmp
my_tmp1<-my_tmp %>% rename(carbon1=carbon,theory1=theory)
my_tmp2<-my_tmp %>% rename(carbon2=carbon,theory2=theory)

# Print carbon sources belonging to each cluster for inspection
for(i in 1:k_val){
  paste("cluster ",i,": ",paste(my_tmp[my_tmp$exp==i,]$carbon,collapse = ","),sep="") %>% print()
}

# 2. Data Integration
# Focus on unique pairs (upper triangle) and join with cluster assignments
my_map<-carbon_pairs_all %>%
  select(carbon1,carbon2,key,category1,category2,pair_category,category_col)
my_dist_df<-carbon_matrix_70gem[my_ins,my_ins] %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("carbon1") %>%
  pivot_longer(-carbon1,names_to = "carbon2",values_to = "rxndiff_median") %>%
  left_join(my_map,by=c("carbon1","carbon2"))%>%
  left_join(my_tmp1,by="carbon1") %>%
  left_join(my_tmp2,by="carbon2") %>%
  filter(key=="upper")


my_clstrs<-seq(1,k_val)

# ==========================================
# 3. Data reshaping: automatically determine cluster numbers based on Upper Glycolysis count
# ==========================================
# Count the number of Upper Glycolysis pairs within each cluster based on the original assignments (theory1=1, theory2=2, etc.)
cluster_counts <- my_dist_df %>%
  mutate(pair_type_raw = case_when(
    theory1 == 1 & theory2 == 1 ~ "C1",
    theory1 == 2 & theory2 == 2 ~ "C2",
    TRUE                  ~ "Between"
  )) %>%
  # Extract within-cluster pairs and tally the Upper Glycolysis count for each cluster
  filter(pair_type_raw %in% c("C1", "C2")) %>%
  group_by(pair_type_raw) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(upper_glyco_count = sum(pair_category == "Upper Glycolysis", na.rm = TRUE))

# Identify the original cluster name containing more Upper Glycolysis pairs
# (In case of a tie, the original C1 is given priority)
target_raw_c1 <- cluster_counts$pair_type_raw[which.max(cluster_counts$upper_glyco_count)]

# Define new cluster names based on the result above (assign Cluster 1 to the cluster with more Upper Glycolysis pairs)
plot_df <- my_dist_df %>%
  mutate(
    pair_type = case_when(
      theory1 == 1 & theory2 == 1 ~ if_else(target_raw_c1 == "C1", "Cluster 1", "Cluster 2"),
      theory1 == 2 & theory2 == 2 ~ if_else(target_raw_c1 == "C2", "Cluster 1", "Cluster 2"),
      TRUE                  ~ "Between"
    )
  ) %>%
  # Fix the display and test order to "Cluster 1, Cluster 2, Between"
  mutate(pair_type = factor(pair_type, levels = c("Cluster 1", "Cluster 2", "Between")))

# Print to console which cluster was assigned as the new Cluster 1
print(paste("The cluster with more Upper Glycolysis pairs was assigned as Cluster 1. Original cluster:", target_raw_c1))


# ==========================================
# 4. Visualization and statistical testing (error-safe version)
# ==========================================
# Embedding wilcox.test directly within ggboxplot reliably avoids mapping errors
p_integrated <- ggboxplot(
  plot_df,
  x = "pair_type", 
  y = "rxndiff_median",
  ylab = "Evolutionary correlation [-]", 
  xlab = "",
  add = "jitter", 
  add.params = list(alpha = 0.4, size = 1.5), 
  theme = theme_pubr(base_size = 20)
) +
  font("xy.text", size = 22) +
  font("ylab", size = 22) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 40, by = 10), limits = c(0, 40)) +
  # Run the test directly inside stat_pwc to avoid errors
  stat_pwc(
    method = "wilcox.test",
    ref.group = "Between",      # Use "Between" as the reference group
    p.adjust.method = "BH",     # Multiple testing correction (Benjamini-Hochberg method)
    label = "p.adj.signif",     # Display significance as stars (*, **, ***)
    tip.length = 0,
    bracket.nudge.y = 0.05, 
    hide.ns = TRUE              # Hide non-significant results
  )

print(p_integrated)


# ==========================================
# 5. (Verification) Output detailed statistical results as text
# ==========================================
stat_test <- plot_df %>%
  wilcox_test(
```

### 1.4.12 Elbow plot (Fig. S9f)
```{r, fig.height=4,fig.width=5}
# 1. Perform hierarchical clustering (Ward's method)
my_ins<-sort(ecor_carbons)
dist_theory<-carbon_matrix_70gem[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------ essentiality-based distance (70 gem)
# Hierarchical clustering using Ward's D2 method
hc_result <- hclust(dist_theory, method = cl_method)
plot(hc_theory)

# 2. Calculate WSS (within-cluster sum of squares) for k = 1 to 10
k_range <- 1:10
wss_values <- sapply(k_range, function(k) {
  # Get cluster assignments for each object
  ct <- cutree(hc_result, k = k)
  
  # Sum the squared distances from the centroid within each cluster
  sum(sapply(unique(ct), function(cluster) {
    # Subset of the distance matrix for data belonging to the current cluster
    sub_dist <- as.matrix(carbon_matrix_70gem)[ct == cluster, ct == cluster, drop = FALSE]
    # Calculate within-cluster sum of squares (WSS) from the distance matrix
    sum(sub_dist^2) / (2 * nrow(sub_dist))
  }))
})

# 3. Create a data frame for plotting
elbow_df <- data.frame(k = k_range, wss = wss_values)

# 4. Plot the elbow diagram with ggplot2
# Elbow Method for Optimal Number of Clusters
p_elbow <- ggplot(elbow_df, aes(x = k, y = wss)) +
  geom_line(color = "black", size = 1.5) +
  geom_point(color = "black", size = 4) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 2, linetype = 2, color = "red") +
```

### 1.4.13 Exchange reactions removed
```{r, message=FALSE}
# Function to read essential reaction data and calculate pairwise distances
calculate_gem_distances_all_exrmvd <- function(csv_filename, strain_id) {
  # Load mapping for carbon abbreviations
  carbon_map <- read_csv(file.path(getwd(), "FBA", "growth_media", "Abb_carbon.csv"))
  
  # Load essential reaction list for the specific strain
  ess_data <- read_csv(file.path(getwd(), "FBA", "output_rev10", "essential_by_species", csv_filename))
  
  # Join with mapping, filter out unassigned carbons, and remove Exchange reactions ("EX_")
  ess_data <- ess_data %>%
    left_join(carbon_map, by = "carbon") %>%
    filter(!is.na(Abb)) %>%
    filter(!grepl("EX_", reaction_id))
  
  # Identify unique reactions and carbons
  unique_reactions <- unique(ess_data$reaction_id)
  unique_carbons <- unique(ess_data$Abb)
  
  # Create a binary matrix (Carbon x Reaction)
  binary_mat <- matrix(0, 
                       nrow = length(unique_carbons), 
                       ncol = length(unique_reactions),
                       dimnames = list(unique_carbons, unique_reactions))
  
  # Fill the matrix: Set 1 if the reaction is essential for that carbon source
  for (carbon in unique_carbons) {
    active_rxns <- ess_data$reaction_id[ess_data$Abb == carbon]
    binary_mat[carbon, colnames(binary_mat) %in% active_rxns] <- 1
  }
  
  # Calculate pairwise Manhattan distances between carbon sources
  dist_mat <- as.matrix(dist(binary_mat, method = "manhattan"))
  
  # Convert to long format for easier merging
  dist_df <- reshape2::melt(dist_mat)
  colnames(dist_df) <- c("carbon1", "carbon2", paste0("rxndiff_exrmvd_", strain_id))
  
  return(dist_df)
}

# Define filenames and corresponding strain names
nums <- sprintf("%02d", setdiff(1:72, c(29, 52)))
model_names_all <- c("iML1515", paste0("ECOR", nums))
model_files_all <- paste0(model_names_all, "__essential_only.csv")

strain_names_all <- model_names_all
strain_names_all[1] <- "MG1655"

# Iteratively load data and merge into a single dataframe
combined_dist_df_all_exrmvd <- NULL

for (i in seq_along(model_files_all)) {
  temp_dist <- calculate_gem_distances_all_exrmvd(model_files_all[i], strain_names_all[i])
  
  if (is.null(combined_dist_df_all_exrmvd)) {
    combined_dist_df_all_exrmvd <- temp_dist
  } else {
    combined_dist_df_all_exrmvd <- left_join(combined_dist_df_all_exrmvd, temp_dist, by = c("carbon1", "carbon2"))
  }
}

# Calculate median distance across all models (excluding the reference MG1655)
median_calculation_df_all_exrmvd <- combined_dist_df_all_exrmvd %>% select(-carbon1, -carbon2, -rxndiff_exrmvd_MG1655)

# Merge back with the primary carbon_pairs dataset
```

### 1.5.2 Load flux distributions computed for each strain
```{r,message=FALSE}
# Create a carbon source template
fba_carbon_map <- read_csv(file.path(getwd(), "FBA", "growth_media","Abb_carbon.csv"))
carbon_pairs_cos <- carbon_pairs
carbon_pairs_cos <- carbon_pairs_cos %>%
  filter(carbon1 %in% used_carbons) %>%
  filter(carbon2 %in% used_carbons)

# Model names used for pFBA
fba_all_strains<-sprintf("ECOR%02d", 1:72)
fba_all_strains<-fba_all_strains[fba_all_strains %nin% qw(ECOR29,ECOR52)] # Remove strains excluded from the analysis
fba_all_strains<-c(fba_all_strains,"iML1515") # Add iML1515

# Extract all flux distributions
flux_distr_list<-list()
i<-1
for(i in 1:length(fba_all_strains)){
  my_strain<-fba_all_strains[i]
  my_fdfile<-paste(my_strain,"__flux_matrix.csv",sep="")
  my_flux_dist<-paste(getwd(),"FBA","output_rev10","flux_distribution_by_species",my_fdfile,sep="/") %>%
    read_csv()
  
  # 1. Create a named vector for mapping (carbon column as original names, Abb column as new names)
  lookup_vector <- fba_carbon_map$Abb
  names(lookup_vector) <- fba_carbon_map$carbon
  
  # 2. Get the current column names
  current_names <- colnames(my_flux_dist)
  
  # 3. Replace only the column names present in the mapping table with their corresponding abbreviations
  # (Non-matching names such as reaction_id or lactic acid are kept as-is)
  matched_indices <- match(current_names, names(lookup_vector))
  new_names <- ifelse(!is.na(matched_indices), 
                      lookup_vector[matched_indices], 
                      current_names)
  
  # 4. Apply the new column names to the data frame
  colnames(my_flux_dist) <- new_names
  
  # 5. Select the carbon sources used in the analysis
  my_flux_dist<-my_flux_dist %>%
    select(c("reaction_id",used_carbons))
  
  # 6. Rename columns to strain_carbonAbb format
  new_names<-colnames(my_flux_dist[,2:ncol(my_flux_dist)])
  new_names<-paste(my_strain,new_names,sep="_")
  
  colnames(my_flux_dist) <- c("reaction_id",new_names)
  flux_distr_list[[i]]<-my_flux_dist
}

```
### 1.5.3 Construct a flux distribution from reactions common to all strains, excluding exchange reactions
```{r}
# 1. Retrieve the list of reaction_ids excluding exchange reactions (EX_) for each strain, then take their intersection
common_rxns <- flux_distr_list %>%
  purrr::map(~ .x %>% 
               dplyr::filter(!stringr::str_detect(reaction_id, "^EX_")) %>% 
               dplyr::pull(reaction_id)) %>%
  purrr::reduce(intersect)

message(sprintf("Number of internal metabolic reactions common to all strains (EX_ excluded): %d", length(common_rxns)))


# 2. Filter to reactions common to all strains and join into a single wide data frame
flux_matrix_df <- flux_distr_list %>%
  purrr::map(~ dplyr::filter(.x, reaction_id %in% common_rxns)) %>%
  purrr::reduce(dplyr::inner_join, by = "reaction_id")

# 3. Set reaction_id as row names and convert to a numeric matrix
flux_mat <- flux_matrix_df %>%
  tibble::column_to_rownames("reaction_id") %>%
  as.matrix()

# Replace any NA values with 0
flux_mat[is.na(flux_mat)] <- 0


# 4. Remove reactions (rows) that are zero across all conditions
# Retain rows whose sum of absolute values exceeds 1e-9 (i.e., reactions with non-zero flux in at least one condition)
# A threshold of 1e-9 is used instead of 0 to account for numerical precision errors
active_rxns <- rowSums(abs(flux_mat)) > 1e-9

# Filter the matrix
flux_mat <- flux_mat[active_rxns, ]

message(sprintf("Number of common reactions after excluding exchange reactions: %d", length(common_rxns)))
message(sprintf("Final number of reactions after removing all-zero reactions: %d", nrow(flux_mat)))
```

```{r}
# coop::cosine computes pairwise similarities between columns by default (same behavior as lsa)
cos_sim_matrix <- coop::cosine(flux_mat)

# 2. Convert to cosine distance (distance = 1 - cosine similarity)
cos_dist_matrix <- 1 - cos_sim_matrix

# 3. Create a distance matrix object (dist type)
cos_dist_obj <- as.dist(cos_dist_matrix)
```

### 1.5.6 Calculate average cosine distances across all strains
```{r}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Prerequisite: uses flux_mat constructed from the code above
# flux_mat rows: common_rxns (common reaction IDs)
# flux_mat columns: strain_carbon (e.g., "ECOR01_Ace", "ECOR01_Glc", "iML1515_Glc")
# -----------------------------------------------------------------

# 1. Compute pairwise cosine similarities across all strain-carbon conditions at once using coop::cosine
# Since flux_mat is (Rxn × condition), the result is a (condition × condition) cosine similarity matrix
all_pairs_cos_sim <- coop::cosine(flux_mat)
all_pairs_cos_dist <- 1 - all_pairs_cos_sim

# 2. Split condition names (column names) into strain and carbon source, and reshape into a data frame
# Data structure: strain1, carbon1, strain2, carbon2, distance
dist_long <- as.data.frame(as.table(all_pairs_cos_dist)) %>%
  setNames(c("cond1", "cond2", "cos_dist")) %>%
  mutate(
    strain1 = sub("^([^_]+)_.*$", "\\1", cond1),
    carbon1 = sub("^[^_]+_", "", cond1),
    strain2 = sub("^([^_]+)_.*$", "\\1", cond2),
    carbon2 = sub("^[^_]+_", "", cond2)
  )

# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Approach A: Calculate pairwise carbon source distances within each strain, then average and compute SD across 70 strains
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
within_strain_summary <- dist_long %>%
  # Filter to within-strain comparisons only
  filter(strain1 == strain2) %>%
  # Exclude the reference strain
  filter(strain1 %nin% "iML1515") %>%
  # Summarize by carbon source pair (carbon1, carbon2)
  group_by(carbon1, carbon2) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_cos_dist = mean(cos_dist, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_cos_dist=median(cos_dist, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_cos_dist   = sd(cos_dist, na.rm = TRUE),
    # Calculate the coefficient of variation (CV = SD / mean)
    # (Set to 0 when mean is 0 to avoid division by zero)
    cv_cos_dist   = ifelse(mean_cos_dist == 0, 0, sd_cos_dist / mean_cos_dist),
    n_strains     = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Reshape the mean distance across 70 strains into a matrix (carbon source × carbon source)
mean_carbon_dist_matrix <- within_strain_summary %>%
  select(carbon1, carbon2, mean_cos_dist) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon2, values_from = mean_cos_dist) %>%
  column_to_rownames("carbon1") %>%
  as.matrix()

median_carbon_dist_matrix <- within_strain_summary %>%
  select(carbon1, carbon2, median_cos_dist) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon2, values_from = median_cos_dist) %>%
  column_to_rownames("carbon1") %>%
  as.matrix()

# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Approach B: Ignore strain-level differences (genomic background) and compute pairwise carbon source distances across all conditions (all strains × all carbon sources)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
overall_carbon_summary <- dist_long %>%
  group_by(carbon1, carbon2) %>%
  summarise(
    overall_mean_dist = mean(cos_dist, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r,fig.width=4,fig.height=3,dpi=300}
# 1. Clustering based on experimental evolutionary distances
# Define the number of theoretical clusters (k)
k_val <- 2

my_ins<-sort(ecor_carbons)
dist_theory<-mean_carbon_dist_matrix[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------ cosine distance
# Hierarchical clustering using Ward's D2 method
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = cl_method)
cluster_theory    <- cutree(hc_theory, k = k_val)

# Create a mapping table for carbon sources and their assigned clusters
my_tmp<-data.frame(carbon=names(cluster_theory),theory=cluster_theory)
carbon_clust_tbl<-my_tmp
my_tmp1<-my_tmp %>% rename(carbon1=carbon,theory1=theory)
my_tmp2<-my_tmp %>% rename(carbon2=carbon,theory2=theory)

# Print carbon sources belonging to each cluster for inspection
for(i in 1:k_val){
  paste("cluster ",i,": ",paste(my_tmp[my_tmp$exp==i,]$carbon,collapse = ","),sep="") %>% print()
}

# 2. Data Integration
# Focus on unique pairs (upper triangle) and join with cluster assignments
my_map<-carbon_pairs_all %>%
  select(carbon1,carbon2,key,category1,category2,pair_category,category_col)
my_dist_df<-mean_carbon_dist_matrix[my_ins,my_ins] %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("carbon1") %>%
  pivot_longer(-carbon1,names_to = "carbon2",values_to = "mean_cos_dist") %>%
  left_join(my_map,by=c("carbon1","carbon2"))%>%
  left_join(my_tmp1,by="carbon1") %>%
  left_join(my_tmp2,by="carbon2") %>%
  filter(key=="upper")





my_clstrs<-seq(1,k_val)

# ==========================================
# 3. Data reshaping: automatically determine cluster numbers based on Upper Glycolysis count
# ==========================================
# Count the number of Upper Glycolysis pairs within each cluster based on the original assignments (theory1=1, theory2=2, etc.)
cluster_counts <- my_dist_df %>%
  mutate(pair_type_raw = case_when(
    theory1 == 1 & theory2 == 1 ~ "C1",
    theory1 == 2 & theory2 == 2 ~ "C2",
    TRUE                  ~ "Between"
  )) %>%
  # Extract within-cluster pairs and tally the Upper Glycolysis count for each cluster
  filter(pair_type_raw %in% c("C1", "C2")) %>%
  group_by(pair_type_raw) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(upper_glyco_count = sum(pair_category == "Upper Glycolysis", na.rm = TRUE))

# Identify the original cluster name containing more Upper Glycolysis pairs
# (In case of a tie, the original C1 is given priority)
target_raw_c1 <- cluster_counts$pair_type_raw[which.max(cluster_counts$upper_glyco_count)]

# Define new cluster names based on the result above (assign Cluster 1 to the cluster with more Upper Glycolysis pairs)
plot_df <- my_dist_df %>%
  mutate(
    pair_type = case_when(
      theory1 == 1 & theory2 == 1 ~ if_else(target_raw_c1 == "C1", "Cluster 1", "Cluster 2"),
      theory1 == 2 & theory2 == 2 ~ if_else(target_raw_c1 == "C2", "Cluster 1", "Cluster 2"),
      TRUE                  ~ "Between"
    )
  ) %>%
  # Fix the display and test order to "Cluster 1, Cluster 2, Between"
  mutate(pair_type = factor(pair_type, levels = c("Cluster 1", "Cluster 2", "Between")))

# Print to console which cluster was assigned as the new Cluster 1
print(paste("The cluster with more Upper Glycolysis pairs was assigned as Cluster 1. Original cluster:", target_raw_c1))


# ==========================================
# 4. Visualization and statistical testing (error-safe version)
# ==========================================
# Embedding wilcox.test directly within ggboxplot reliably avoids mapping errors
p_integrated <- ggboxplot(
  plot_df,
  x = "pair_type", 
  y = "mean_cos_dist",
  ylab = "Evolutionary correlation [-]", 
  xlab = "",
  add = "jitter", 
  add.params = list(alpha = 0.4, size = 1.5), 
  theme = theme_pubr(base_size = 20)
) +
  font("xy.text", size = 22) +
  font("ylab", size = 22) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 0.8, by = 0.2), limits = c(0, 0.8)) +
  # Run the test directly inside stat_pwc to avoid errors
  stat_pwc(
    method = "wilcox.test",
    ref.group = "Between",
    p.adjust.method = "BH",
    label = "p.adj.signif",
    tip.length = 0,
    bracket.nudge.y = 0.05, 
    hide.ns = TRUE
  )


print(p_integrated)


# ==========================================
# 5. (Verification) Output detailed statistical results as text
# ==========================================
stat_test <- plot_df %>%
  wilcox_test(
    formula = mean_cos_dist ~ pair_type,
    ref.group = "Between",
    p.adjust.method = "BH"
  )
print("Detailed adjusted p-values compared to Between:")
print(stat_test)

# Extract a mapping table of carbon sources to new cluster assignments (Cluster 1 / 2)
# from the plot_df finalized in the ECOR analysis above
# This ensures that the cluster definitions corrected by Upper Glycolysis count are carried over as-is
cbnclust_tbl_fluxbased <- plot_df %>%
  # Create a mapping from the carbon1 and carbon2 definitions so that each carbon source appears as a separate row
  select(carbon = carbon1, pair_type) %>%
  bind_rows(select(plot_df, carbon = carbon2, pair_type)) %>%
  filter(pair_type %in% c("Cluster 1", "Cluster 2")) %>%
  distinct(carbon, pair_type)


Sys.time()
```

## 1.6 Flux-based distance derived from iML1515
### 1.6.1 Visualization of cosine distances derived from iML1515
```{r,fig.height=3,fig.width=8, dpi=300}
# 1. Extract flux data for iML1515 (all reactions)
iml_cols <- grep("iML1515", colnames(flux_mat), value = TRUE)
iml_mat <- flux_mat[, iml_cols]

# 2. Remove reactions with no variation (reactions that are always zero)
active_mat <- iml_mat[apply(iml_mat, 1, var) > 1e-8, ]

# Calculate cosine similarity and cosine distance from the flux matrix (columns = carbon sources)
iml_cos_sim_matrix <- coop::cosine(active_mat) # Pairwise similarity between columns

cos_dist_matrix_iml<-1-iml_cos_sim_matrix
rownames(cos_dist_matrix_iml)<- sub("^[^_]*_", "", rownames(cos_dist_matrix_iml))
colnames(cos_dist_matrix_iml)<- sub("^[^_]*_", "", colnames(cos_dist_matrix_iml))
my_ins<-sort(rownames(cos_dist_matrix_iml))
cos_dist_matrix_iml<-cos_dist_matrix_iml[my_ins,my_ins]
  
iml_cos_dist <- as.dist(1 - iml_cos_sim_matrix)    # Convert to a distance object

# 2. Perform PCoA (Principal Coordinate Analysis / cmdscale)
pcoa_res <- cmdscale(iml_cos_dist, k = 2, eig = TRUE)

# Calculate the proportion of variance explained
eigen_vals <- pcoa_res$eig
pc1_var <- round(eigen_vals[1] / sum(eigen_vals[eigen_vals > 0]) * 100, 1)
pc2_var <- round(eigen_vals[2] / sum(eigen_vals[eigen_vals > 0]) * 100, 1)

# 3. Create a data frame for plotting
pcoa_df <- data.frame(
  ColName = rownames(pcoa_res$points),
  Carbon = sub("^[^_]*_", "", rownames(pcoa_res$points)),
  PCoA1 = pcoa_res$points[, 1],
  PCoA2 = pcoa_res$points[, 2]
) %>%
  left_join(carbon_names, by = c("Carbon"="Abb"))

# 4. Create a named color vector mapping categories to color codes
color_palette <- setNames(
  unique(carbon_names$Category_col), 
  unique(carbon_names$Category)
)

# 5. Simple visualization with ggscatter
ggscatter(
  pcoa_df,
  x = "PCoA1", y = "PCoA2",
  color = "Category",          # Color by category
  palette = color_palette,     # Apply the color palette derived from carbon_names
  label = "Carbon",            # Display label (abbreviation)
  repel = TRUE,                # Prevent label overlap
  label.select = NULL,
  point.size = 3.5,
  alpha = 0.8,
  xlab = paste0("PCoA1 (", pc1_var, "%)"),
  ylab = paste0("PCoA2 (", pc2_var, "%)"),
  # xlim =c(-40,20),
  title = "iML1515 pFBA Flux Cosine Distance PCoA",
  ggtheme = theme_bw(base_size = 14)
) +
  theme(
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "right"
  )
```

```{r}
# 1. Distance matrix
my_gr_mat<-mean_carbon_dist_matrix
my_rows<-rownames(my_gr_mat)
# 2. Theoretical distance matrix between carbon sources
my_cbdist_mat<-cos_dist_matrix_iml[my_rows,my_rows]

# 3. Mantel test
set.seed(123)
mantel_result <- mantel(
  xdis = as.dist(my_gr_mat),  # Growth-based correlation matrix
  ydis = as.dist(my_cbdist_mat), # Theoretical distance matrix
  method = "spearman",         # Rank correlation (change to "pearson" if needed)
  permutations = 999,          # Number of permutations to stabilize the result
  na.rm = TRUE                 # Handle diagonal elements and missing values (NA)
)

print(mantel_result)
Sys.time()
```

#### 1.8.3.3 Entanglement score with permutation test (Fig. S8d)
```{r, fig.width=1.5,fig.height=3.5,dpi=300}

my_mat<-iml_cos_sim_matrix
rownames(my_mat)<-sub("^[^_]*_", "", rownames(my_mat))
colnames(my_mat)<-sub("^[^_]*_", "", colnames(my_mat))

# Flux-based distance and Phenotypic distance from Growth rates
my_ins<-sort(ecor_carbons)
my_ins<-my_ins[my_ins %in% rownames(my_mat)]
dist_exp<-mean_carbon_dist_matrix[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------ 70 GEMs
dist_theory<-1-my_mat[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------iml1515

# Hierarchical clustering using Ward's D2 method
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = cl_method)
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method)

dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# 2. Untangle: Optimize the layout of the two dendrograms to minimize crossings
# Maintaining the topology while rotating branches for better visualization
dl <- dendlist(dend_theory, dend_exp)
dl_untangled <- dendextend::untangle(dl, method = "step2side")

dend_p <- dl_untangled[[1]] # Optimized iml
dend_t <- dl_untangled[[2]] # Optimized 70 GEMs


# 3. Create color vectors based on labels
# Retrieve current label order from the left (FBA) dendrogram
current_labels_p <- labels(dend_p)
# Map categories and colors to the current labels
groups_p <- carbon_labels_ordered_cos$Category[match(current_labels_p, carbon_labels_ordered_cos$label)]
col_vector_p <- carbon_labels_ordered_cos$Category_col[match(current_labels_p, carbon_labels_ordered_cos$label)]

# 4. Set label colors
dend_p <- dend_p %>% set("labels_colors", col_vector_p)

# Match Growth-based tree labels with the FBA-based tree's color vector
dend_t <- dend_t %>% 
  set("labels_colors", col_vector_p[match(labels(dend_t), current_labels_p)])

# 5. Draw Tanglegram
# Visualizing the structural similarity between metabolic theory and growth phenotype
tanglegram(dend_p, dend_t,
           common_subtrees_color_lines = FALSE, 
           highlight_distinct_edges = FALSE,
           highlight_branches_lwd = FALSE,
           color_lines = col_vector_p, 
           main_left = "iML1515",
           main_right = "70 GEMs",
           lab.cex = 1,
           lwd=2,
           columns_width = c(4, 1.5, 4),
           margin_inner = 3.5,
           margin_outer = 0.5,
           axes = FALSE)


# 6. Permutation Test for Entanglement Score
# Lower entanglement indicates higher structural similarity
actual_ent <- entanglement(dl_untangled) # Entanglement score after untangling

print(Sys.time())
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- if_else(iteration_scale=="large",1000,10)
perm_ent <- numeric(n_perm)

# Fixed theory-based labels
labels_theory <- labels(dend_p)

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # Copy the experimental dendrogram and shuffle labels
  shuffled_dend <- dend_t
  labels(shuffled_dend) <- sample(labels_theory)
  
  # Calculate entanglement for the shuffled pair after untangling
  perm_dends <- dendlist(dend_p, shuffled_dend) %>% 
    dendextend::untangle(method = "step2side")
  perm_ent[i] <- entanglement(perm_dends)
  
  # Progress monitoring
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# 7. Calculate P-value
# P-value = Probability that random entanglement is lower than the observed value
p_val_ent <- sum(perm_ent <= actual_ent) / n_perm

# 8. Visualization of results
hist(perm_ent, main="Permutation Test for Entanglement", 
     xlab="Entanglement Score", xlim=c(0, 1))
abline(v = actual_ent, col = "red", lwd = 2)
cat(sprintf("Actual Entanglement: %.3f\nP-value: %.4f\n", actual_ent, p_val_ent))

Sys.time()
```
#### 1.8.3.4 Cophenetic correlation with permutation test (Fig. S8d)
```{r}
# 1. Prepare distance matrices and initial dendrograms
my_mat<-iml_cos_sim_matrix
rownames(my_mat)<-sub("^[^_]*_", "", rownames(my_mat))
colnames(my_mat)<-sub("^[^_]*_", "", colnames(my_mat))

# Flux-based distance and Phenotypic distance from Growth rates
my_ins<-sort(ecor_carbons)
my_ins<-my_ins[my_ins %in% rownames(my_mat)]
dist_exp<-mean_carbon_dist_matrix[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------ 70 GEMs
dist_theory<-1-my_mat[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------iml1515

# Hierarchical clustering
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = cl_method)
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method)

dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# Calculate observed Cophenetic correlation (Spearman)
# This measures how well the tree structure reflects the original distance matrix
actual_cor <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_exp, method = "spearman")

# --- Permutation Test for Cophenetic Correlation ---
print(Sys.time())
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- 1000
perm_results <- data.frame(cor = numeric(n_perm))

# Get original labels (strain names) from the experimental distance matrix
exp_labels <- rownames(as.matrix(dist_exp))

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # 1. Shuffle labels while keeping the underlying matrix structure intact
  dist_shuffled <- dist_exp
  shuffled_labels <- sample(exp_labels)
  
  # Convert to matrix to reassign shuffled names
  temp_mat <- as.matrix(dist_shuffled)
  rownames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  colnames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  
  # 2. Reconstruct dendrogram from the shuffled distance matrix
  hc_shuffled <- hclust(as.dist(temp_mat), method = cl_method)
  dend_shuffled <- as.dendrogram(hc_shuffled)
  
  # 3. Calculate and store the correlation for this permutation
  perm_results$cor[i] <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_shuffled, method = "spearman")
  
  # Progress monitoring
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# --- Statistical Evaluation ---
# P-value: Proportion of permutations where correlation is equal to or greater than observed
p_val_cor <- sum(perm_results$cor >= actual_cor) / n_perm

cat("【Analysis Results】\n")
cat(sprintf("Cophenetic Cor (Spearman): %.3f (p = %.4f)\n", actual_cor, p_val_cor))

# --- Visualization: Cophenetic Correlation Bubble Plot ---
# 1. Prepare data and count overlapping points (ties) for bubble sizing
df_coph <- data.frame(
  Theory = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_theory)),
  Experiment = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_exp))
) %>%
  group_by(Theory, Experiment) %>%
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = 'drop') # 各座標の重複数をカウント

my_txt<-paste("R=",sprintf("%.3f",actual_cor),sep="")

# 2. Plotting with ggscatter
# Bubble size and color intensity are log2-scaled to visualize the density of distance pairs
ggscatter(df_coph, x = "Theory", y = "Experiment",
          size = "count",           # Map count to dot size
          fill = "count",           # Map count to fill color
          color = "black",          # Fix border color to black
          shape = 21,               # Use filled circles with borders
          alpha= 0.8,
          xlab = "Cophenetic distance (Theory)",
          ylab = "Cophenetic distance (Experiment)",
          title = "Cophenetic Correlation (Log-scaled Bubble Size)",
          ylim=c(0,3)) +
  # Apply log2 transformation to size and color to handle the wide range of counts
  scale_size_continuous(trans = "log2", range = c(1, 12), name = "Count (log2)") +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Greys", trans = "log2", direction = 1, name = "Count (log2)")+
  annotate("text", x = 0.2, y = 2.7, label = my_txt,)

Sys.time()
```

#### 1.8.4.3 Entanglement score with permutation test (Fig. S9h)
```{r, fig.width=1.5,fig.height=3.5,dpi=300}

my_ins<-ecor_carbons
# Flux-based distance and Phenotypic distance from Growth rates
dist_theory<-carbon_matrix_70gem[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------ 70 GEMs
dist_exp<-1- carbon_matrix_iml[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------iml1515

# Hierarchical clustering using Ward's D2 method
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = cl_method)
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method)

dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# 2. Untangle: Optimize the layout of the two dendrograms to minimize crossings
# Maintaining the topology while rotating branches for better visualization
dl <- dendlist(dend_theory, dend_exp)
dl_untangled <- dendextend::untangle(dl, method = "step2side")

dend_p <- dl_untangled[[1]] # Optimized 70 GEMs
dend_t <- dl_untangled[[2]] # Optimized iML1515


# 3. Create color vectors based on labels
# Retrieve current label order from the left (FBA) dendrogram
current_labels_p <- labels(dend_p)
# Map categories and colors to the current labels
groups_p <- carbon_labels_ordered_cos$Category[match(current_labels_p, carbon_labels_ordered_cos$label)]
col_vector_p <- carbon_labels_ordered_cos$Category_col[match(current_labels_p, carbon_labels_ordered_cos$label)]

# 4. Set label colors
dend_p <- dend_p %>% set("labels_colors", col_vector_p)

# Match Growth-based tree labels with the FBA-based tree's color vector
dend_t <- dend_t %>% 
  set("labels_colors", col_vector_p[match(labels(dend_t), current_labels_p)])

# 5. Draw Tanglegram
# Visualizing the structural similarity between metabolic theory and growth phenotype
tanglegram(dend_p, dend_t,
           common_subtrees_color_lines = FALSE, 
           highlight_distinct_edges = FALSE,
           highlight_branches_lwd = FALSE,
           color_lines = col_vector_p, 
           main_left = "70 GEMs",
           main_right = "iML1515",
           lab.cex = 1,
           lwd=2,
           columns_width = c(4, 1.5, 4),
           margin_inner = 3.5,
           margin_outer = 0.5,
           axes = FALSE)


# 6. Permutation Test for Entanglement Score
# Lower entanglement indicates higher structural similarity
actual_ent <- entanglement(dl_untangled) # Entanglement score after untangling

print(Sys.time())
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- if_else(iteration_scale=="large",1000,10)
perm_ent <- numeric(n_perm)

# Fixed theory-based labels
labels_theory <- labels(dend_p)

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # Copy the experimental dendrogram and shuffle labels
  shuffled_dend <- dend_t
  labels(shuffled_dend) <- sample(labels_theory)
  
  # Calculate entanglement for the shuffled pair after untangling
  perm_dends <- dendlist(dend_p, shuffled_dend) %>% 
    dendextend::untangle(method = "step2side")
  perm_ent[i] <- entanglement(perm_dends)
  
  # Progress monitoring
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# 7. Calculate P-value
# P-value = Probability that random entanglement is lower than the observed value
p_val_ent <- sum(perm_ent <= actual_ent) / n_perm

# 8. Visualization of results
hist(perm_ent, main="Permutation Test for Entanglement", 
     xlab="Entanglement Score", xlim=c(0, 1))
abline(v = actual_ent, col = "red", lwd = 2)
cat(sprintf("Actual Entanglement: %.3f\nP-value: %.4f\n", actual_ent, p_val_ent))

Sys.time()
```

```{r}

hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method)

dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# This measures how well the tree structure reflects the original distance matrix

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # 1. Shuffle labels while keeping the underlying matrix structure intact

  temp_mat <- as.matrix(dist_shuffled)
  rownames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  colnames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  
  # 2. Reconstruct dendrogram from the shuffled distance matrix
  hc_shuffled <- hclust(as.dist(temp_mat), method = cl_method)
  dend_shuffled <- as.dendrogram(hc_shuffled)
  
  # 3. Calculate and store the correlation for this permutation
  perm_results$cor[i] <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_shuffled, method = "spearman")
  
  # Progress monitoring
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# --- Statistical Evaluation ---
# P-value: Proportion of permutations where correlation is equal to or greater than observed
p_val_cor <- sum(perm_results$cor >= actual_cor) / n_perm

cat("【Analysis Results】\n")
cat(sprintf("Cophenetic Cor (Spearman): %.3f (p = %.4f)\n", actual_cor, p_val_cor))

# --- Visualization: Cophenetic Correlation Bubble Plot ---
# 1. Prepare data and count overlapping points (ties) for bubble sizing
df_coph <- data.frame(
  Theory = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_theory)),
  Experiment = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_exp))
) %>%
  group_by(Theory, Experiment) %>%
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = 'drop') 

my_txt<-paste("R=",sprintf("%.3f",actual_cor),sep="")

# 2. Plotting with ggscatter

          size = "count",           # Map count to dot size
          fill = "count",           # Map count to fill color
          color = "black",          # Fix border color to black
          shape = 21,               # Use filled circles with borders
          alpha= 0.8,
          xlab = "Cophenetic distance (Theory)",
          ylab = "Cophenetic distance (Experiment)",
          title = "Cophenetic Correlation (Log-scaled Bubble Size)",
          ylim=c(0,40)) +
  # Apply log2 transformation to size and color to handle the wide range of counts
  scale_size_continuous(trans = "log2", range = c(1, 12), name = "Count (log2)") +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Greys", trans = "log2", direction = 1, name = "Count (log2)")+
  annotate("text", x = 10, y = 2.7, label = my_txt,)

Sys.time()
```

### 1.8.7 Flux-based distance across metabolic pathway categories (Fig. 4c)
```{r,fig.height=2.5,fig.width=7, dpi=300}
my_palette<-c("#0072B2", "#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73", "#8FD926", "grey60", "grey30")

my_df1 <- carbon_dist_integrated_long %>%
  filter(
    carbon1 %in% ecor_carbons,
    carbon2 %in% ecor_carbons,
    key == "upper",
    pair_category != "between"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    xlab = case_when(
      pair_category == "Upper Glycolysis"            ~ "Upper\nGlycolysis",
      pair_category == "Lower Glycolysis"            ~ "Lower\nGlycolysis",
      pair_category == "Pentose Phosphate"           ~ "Pentose\nPhosphate",
      pair_category == "TCA cycle"                   ~ "TCA\ncycle",
      pair_category == "Amino acid-derived TCA input" ~ "Amino acid\nderived\nTCA input",
      TRUE                                           ~ as.character(pair_category)
    )
  )

my_df2 <- carbon_dist_integrated_long %>%
  filter(
    carbon1 %in% ecor_carbons,
    carbon2 %in% ecor_carbons,
    key == "upper"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    xlab = if_else(pair_category == "between", "Between", "Within")
  )

my_df<-bind_rows(my_df1,my_df2)
my_label<-c("Upper\nGlycolysis","Lower\nGlycolysis","Pentose\nPhosphate","TCA\ncycle","Amino acid\nderived\nTCA input","Between","Within")

my_df$xlab<-factor(my_df$xlab,levels = my_label)

# Wilcoxon test
my_df %>%
  wilcox_test(formula = mean_cos_dist ~ xlab,
              ref.group = "Between",
              p.adjust.method = "BH"
              )

# iML1515 based distance
ggboxplot(my_df,
          x="xlab",y="mean_cos_dist",
          ylab="Metabolic distance [-]",xlab="",
          add="jitter",add.params = list(alpha=0.5),
          color = "xlab",palette = my_palette,legend="")
Sys.time()
```


# 2 Phylogenetic tree of ECOR
## 2.1 load phylogenetic relationship based on core-genome SNP typing using Parsnp (Fig.1a)
```{r}
## Strain typing based on alignmrernt of core genome sequnces using Pansnp
## for Parsnp: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4262987/
## for EzClermont: https://github.com/nickp60/EzClermont/tree/master/docs/analysis

# Metadata validation and cleanup
ez_metadata <- read_csv(file.path(getwd(), "EzClermont", "validation_metadata.csv")) %>%
  mutate(simple = gsub("(.*?) (.*)", "\\1", reported_phylogroup)) %>%
  select(-dataset, -reported_phylogroup) %>%
  filter(accession != "")

# Load ezClermont results
ez_expdata <- read_delim(file.path(getwd(), "EzClermont", "2020-04-09-ezclermont.txt"), 
                         col_names = c("long_acc", "ezClermont_phylogroup")) %>%
  mutate(accession = gsub(".scaffold.fasta", "", 
                          gsub("(GCA_.*?\\.\\d)_(.*)", "\\1", long_acc)))

# Merge and validate consistency between reported and predicted phylogroups
ez_together <- left_join(ez_metadata, ez_expdata %>% select(-long_acc), by = "accession") %>%
  mutate(raw_match = (simple == ezClermont_phylogroup))

# Correct known mismatches for specific Clades/Cryptic lineages
ez_together <- ez_together %>%
  mutate(match = ifelse(grepl("Clade", simple) & grepl("cryptic", ezClermont_phylogroup) & !raw_match, 
                        TRUE, raw_match))

# Load ClermontTyping results for comparison
ez_expdata_ct <- read_delim(file.path(getwd(), "EzClermont", "2020-04-09-CT-results.txt"), 
                            col_names = c("accession", "alleles", "profile", "al", "ct_phylotype", "mashpath")) %>%
  mutate(accession = gsub(".scaffold.fasta", "", gsub("(.*?\\..)_(.*)", "\\1", accession)),
         ct_phylotype = gsub("(.*?) (.*)", "\\1", ct_phylotype)) %>%
  select(accession, ct_phylotype)

ez_together <- left_join(ez_together, ez_expdata_ct, by = "accession")

# 2.1.2 Phylogenetic Tree Construction and Visualization
# Load the Maximum Likelihood tree (Parsnp output)
ez_tree <- ape::read.tree(file.path(getwd(), "EzClermont", "parsnp.clean.phy_phyml_tree.txt"))

# Standardize tip labels to match accession formats
ez_tree$tip.label <- ifelse(!startsWith(ez_tree$tip.label, "0"),
                            paste0("ESC_", ez_tree$tip.label),
                            paste0("GCA_", ez_tree$tip.label))

# Prepare label dataframe for ggtree mapping
labdf <- data.frame(label = ez_tree$tip.label, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
  left_join(ez_together %>% mutate(label = substr(accession, 1, 13)), by = "label") %>%
  mutate(
    label2 = ifelse(match, strain, paste0("(", ezClermont_phylogroup, ") ", strain)),
    # Consolidate cryptic clades for visualization
    quardiplex_pcr_base_tidy = ifelse(grepl("lade", simple), "Cryptic", simple),
    ct_phylotype = ifelse(grepl("lade", ct_phylotype), "Cryptic", 
                          ifelse(grepl("Unknown", ct_phylotype), "U", ct_phylotype)),
    ezClermont_phylogroup = ifelse(grepl("cryptic", ezClermont_phylogroup), "Cryptic", ezClermont_phylogroup)
  )

# Define Phylogroup Color Palette
colors <- c(A="grey", B1="darkgreen", B2="purple", C="orange", 
            "Clade I"="yellow", "Cryptic"="yellow", "Clade II"="yellow", 
            "Clade IV"="yellow", "Clade V"="yellow", D="red", E="green", 
            F="steelblue", G="black", U="pink")

# Visualization: Circular tree with heatmaps and phylogroup highlights
tp <- gheatmap(
  ggtree(ape::root.phylo(ez_tree, node = 142), layout = "circular", branch.length = 'none') %<+% labdf +
    geom_hilight(node = 145, fill = colors['A'], alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_hilight(node = 179, fill = colors['B1'], alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_hilight(node = 218, fill = colors['B2'], alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_hilight(node = 199, fill = colors['C'], alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_hilight(node = 212, fill = colors['D'], alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_hilight(node = 202, fill = colors['E'], alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_hilight(node = 135, fill = colors['F'], alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_hilight(node = 132, fill = colors['G'], alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_tiplab2(aes(label = label2), size = 3, offset = 5) +
    scale_color_manual(values = colors) +
    theme(legend.position = "right"),
  data = labdf %>% select(label, Reported = quardiplex_pcr_base_tidy, ClermonTyping = ct_phylotype, EzClermont = ezClermont_phylogroup) %>%
    column_to_rownames("label"),
  colnames_position = "top", width = 0.2, font.size = 2
) + scale_fill_manual(values = colors)+ labs(fill="Phylogroup")
print(tp)


# 2.1.3 ECOR-specific Subtree Generation
# Filter for ECOR and K12-MG1655 strains
labdf_sub <- labdf %>% 
  filter(grepl("^ECOR", strain) | strain == "K12-MG1655") %>%
  rename(Phylogroup = ezClermont_phylogroup)

# Manual curation for specific strains (based on literature: doi:10.1099/acmi.0.000143)
labdf_sub$Phylogroup[labdf_sub$strain %in% c("ECOR44", "ECOR49")] <- "D"

# Extract and plot the subtree
sub_tree <- ape::keep.tip(ez_tree, labdf_sub$label)

my_outfile<-paste(getwd(),"Outputs_Main",sep="/")

# ggtree(sub_tree, layout="circular", branch.length="none") + geom_text(aes(label=node))
ggtree(sub_tree, layout = "circular") %<+% labdf_sub +
  geom_tiplab2(aes(label = strain), size = 3, offset = 0.001) +
  geom_tippoint(aes(color = Phylogroup), size = 2) +
  geom_hilight(node = 84, fill = pgPalette['A'], alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_hilight(node = 108, fill = pgPalette['B1'], alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_hilight(node = 131, fill = pgPalette['B2'], alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_hilight(node = 121, fill = pgPalette['C'], alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_hilight(node = 126, fill = pgPalette['D'], alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_hilight(node = 123, fill = pgPalette['E'], alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_hilight(node = 76, fill = pgPalette['F'], alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_treescale(x = 0.006, y = 71, offset = 1) +
  labs(title = "Phylogeny of ECOR strains and MG1655") +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
# TODO ggsave(file="Fig1a.pdf", path=my_outfile,dpi = 300, width = 6, height = 6,bg=NULL)

# Update
labdf_sub<-labdf_sub %>% 
  filter(grepl("^ECOR", strain)) # remove K12-MG1655

Sys.time()
```

## 2.1 Transforming Phylogenetic Distance Matrix to Long-format Dataframe
```{r}
# 1. Compute pairwise distances between tips based on the branch lengths (ML tree)
# cophenetic.phylo calculates the sum of the edge lengths between each pair of tips
phylo_dist_mat <- cophenetic.phylo(sub_tree)

# 2. Map accession labels back to strain names for better readability
# Ensure the mapping matches the current matrix order
strain_mapping <- labdf_sub$strain[match(rownames(phylo_dist_mat), labdf_sub$label)]
rownames(phylo_dist_mat) <- colnames(phylo_dist_mat) <- strain_mapping

# 3. Filter for ECOR strains only to create a focused distance matrix
ecor_indices <- grep("^ECOR", rownames(phylo_dist_mat))
phylo_dist_mat <- phylo_dist_mat[ecor_indices, ecor_indices]

# 4. Identify matrix positions (Upper triangle, Lower triangle, or Diagonal)
# This tagging is essential for downstream correlation analyses to avoid redundant pairs
n_strains <- nrow(phylo_dist_mat)
pos_tag_mat <- matrix("upper", n_strains, n_strains)
pos_tag_mat[lower.tri(pos_tag_mat)] <- "lower"
diag(pos_tag_mat) <- "diag"

# 5. Convert the distance matrix to a long-format dataframe
phylo_dist_df <- as.data.frame(as.table(phylo_dist_mat))
colnames(phylo_dist_df) <- c("strain1", "strain2", "phylo_dist")

# 6. Append the positional tags (flattening the tag matrix in the same order)
phylo_dist_df$Type  <- as.vector(pos_tag_mat)

# 7. Data Inspection
# Review the first few rows to ensure correct mapping
print("Preview of the phylogenetic distance dataframe:")
head(phylo_dist_df)
Sys.time()
```

### 3.1.2 Variance in growth rate across MA lineage (Two reps and Four reps)
```{r,fig.height=8,fig.width=6, dpi=300}
carbon<-dat$carbon %>% unique()
n_carbon<-carbon %>% length()
lineage<-dat$lineage %>% unique()
n_lineage<-lineage %>% length()
round<-dat$round %>% unique()
n_round<-round %>% unique()
anc_colony<-dat$Anc %>% unique()


i<-1
j<-1
for (i in 1:n_carbon){
  my_carbon<-carbon[i]
  my_dat<-dat %>%
    filter(carbon==my_carbon)
  my_dat[(my_dat$lineage %nin% c("lineage1","lineage5","lineage9"))&
           (my_dat$round==0),]$mu_max<-NA #<- remove overlapped anc data (use Anc data of lineages 1, 5, 9)
  my_dat[(my_dat$lineage %nin% c("lineage1","lineage5","lineage9"))&
           (my_dat$round==0),]$mu_max_allrep<-NA #<- remove overlapped anc data (use Anc data of lineages 1, 5, 9)
  my_df<-data.frame(round=round,carbon=my_carbon,
                    mean_mu=NA,sd_mu=NA,var_mu=NA,
                    mean_mu_allrep=NA,sd_mu_allrep=NA,var_mu_allrep=NA
                    )
  for (j in 1:nrow(my_df)){
    my_round<-my_df$round[j]
    my_df$mean_mu[j]<-my_dat[my_dat$round==my_round,]$mu_max %>% mean(na.rm = TRUE)
    my_df$sd_mu[j]<-my_dat[my_dat$round==my_round,]$mu_max %>% sd(na.rm = TRUE)
    my_df$var_mu[j]<-my_dat[my_dat$round==my_round,]$mu_max %>% var(na.rm = TRUE)
    my_df$mean_mu_allrep[j]<-my_dat[my_dat$round==my_round,]$mu_max_allrep %>% mean(na.rm = TRUE)
    my_df$sd_mu_allrep[j]<-my_dat[my_dat$round==my_round,]$mu_max_allrep %>% sd(na.rm = TRUE)
    my_df$var_mu_allrep[j]<-my_dat[my_dat$round==my_round,]$mu_max_allrep %>% var(na.rm = TRUE)
  }
  if(i==1){
    stat_df<-my_df
  }else{
    stat_df<-bind_rows(stat_df,my_df)
  }
}
stat_df$cv_mu<-stat_df$sd_mu/stat_df$mean_mu
stat_df$cv_mu_allrep<-stat_df$sd_mu_allrep/stat_df$mean_mu_allrep

# Two reps
g<-ggline(stat_df,x="round",y="cv_mu",numeric.x.axis = TRUE, alpha=0.5,ylab="Coefficient of variation [-]")
g<-ggpar(g, font.y = c(14, "black"))
facet(g,facet.by = "carbon")

g<-ggline(stat_df,x="round",y="var_mu",numeric.x.axis = TRUE, alpha=0.5)
facet(g,facet.by = "carbon")

# Four reps
g<-ggline(stat_df,x="round",y="cv_mu_allrep",numeric.x.axis = TRUE, alpha=0.5,ylab="Coefficient of variation [-]")
g<-ggpar(g, font.y = c(14, "black"))
facet(g,facet.by = "carbon")

Sys.time()
```
### 3.1.3 Calc. relative growth rate to anc (rel growth rate)
```{r}
gr_ma_df<-dat
# 2 representative replicates
gr_ma_df$rel_mu_max<-NA
i<-1
j<-1
for(i in 1:length(carbon)){
  my_carbon<-carbon[i]
  for(j in 1:length(anc_colony)){
    my_anc<-anc_colony[j]
    my_gr_anc<-gr_ma_df[(gr_ma_df$carbon==my_carbon)&
                       (gr_ma_df$Anc==my_anc)&
                       (gr_ma_df$round==0),]$mu_max %>% unique()
    gr_ma_df[(gr_ma_df$carbon==my_carbon)&
            (gr_ma_df$Anc==my_anc),]$rel_mu_max<-gr_ma_df[(gr_ma_df$carbon==my_carbon)&(gr_ma_df$Anc==my_anc),]$mu_max/my_gr_anc
  }
}

# all 4 replicates
gr_ma_df$rel_mu_max_allrep<-NA
i<-1
j<-1
for(i in 1:length(carbon)){
  my_carbon<-carbon[i]
  for(j in 1:length(anc_colony)){
    my_anc<-anc_colony[j]
    my_gr_anc<-gr_ma_df[(gr_ma_df$carbon==my_carbon)&
                       (gr_ma_df$Anc==my_anc)&
                       (gr_ma_df$round==0),]$mu_max_allrep %>% unique()
    gr_ma_df[(gr_ma_df$carbon==my_carbon)&
            (gr_ma_df$Anc==my_anc),]$rel_mu_max_allrep<-gr_ma_df[(gr_ma_df$carbon==my_carbon)&(gr_ma_df$Anc==my_anc),]$mu_max_allrep/my_gr_anc
  }
}

Sys.time()
```

### 3.2.2 Inter-sample correlation
```{r}
ma_pair_all<-carbon_dist_integrated_long
ma_pair_all<-ma_pair_all[(ma_pair_all$carbon1 %in% ma_carbons)&(ma_pair_all$carbon2 %in% ma_carbons),]
ma_pair_all$correlation<-NA
ma_pair_all$correlation_allrep<-NA
i<-1
for (i in 1:nrow(ma_pair_all)){
  my_carbon_1<-ma_pair_all$carbon1[i]
  my_carbon_2<-ma_pair_all$carbon2[i]
  my_df1<-gr_ma_df[gr_ma_df$carbon==my_carbon_1,]
  my_df1<-my_df1 %>% select(carbon,Anc,lineage,round,mu_max,rel_mu_max,mu_max_allrep,rel_mu_max_allrep) %>%
    rename(mu_max_1=mu_max,rel_mu_max_1=rel_mu_max,mu_max_allrep_1=mu_max_allrep,rel_mu_max_allrep_1=rel_mu_max_allrep)
  my_df2<-gr_ma_df[gr_ma_df$carbon==my_carbon_2,]
  my_df2<-my_df2 %>% select(carbon,Anc,lineage,round,mu_max,rel_mu_max,mu_max_allrep,rel_mu_max_allrep) %>%
    rename(mu_max_2=mu_max,rel_mu_max_2=rel_mu_max,mu_max_allrep_2=mu_max_allrep,rel_mu_max_allrep_2=rel_mu_max_allrep)
  my_df<-left_join(my_df1,my_df2,by=qw(Anc,lineage,round))
  my_df<-my_df[my_df$round>0,] #<------------------ Remove Anc
  my_res<-cor_test(my_df,vars = "rel_mu_max_1",vars2 = "rel_mu_max_2",method = "spearman")
  ma_pair_all$correlation[i]<-my_res$cor
  my_res<-cor_test(my_df,vars = "rel_mu_max_allrep_1",vars2 = "rel_mu_max_allrep_2",method = "spearman")
  ma_pair_all$correlation_allrep[i]<-my_res$cor
}

# Correlation matrix
ma_matrix <- ma_pair_all %>% select(carbon1,carbon2,correlation) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon2, values_from = correlation) %>%
  column_to_rownames("carbon1") %>%
  as.matrix()

# Sorting
target_order <- sort(rownames(ma_matrix))
ma_matrix <- ma_matrix[target_order, target_order]

# Distance matrix
ma_dist_matrix <- as.dist(1 - ma_matrix)
ma_dist_df<-make_dist_dataframe(ma_dist_matrix,"ma")

Sys.time()
```

### 3.3.2 Mantel test
#### 3.3.2.1 Flux-based (70 ECOR strains)
```{r}
my_gr_mat<-ma_matrix
my_rows<-rownames(my_gr_mat)
my_cbdist_mat<-mean_carbon_dist_matrix[my_rows,my_rows]

# Mantel test
set.seed(123)
mantel_result <- mantel(
  xdis = as.dist(1-my_gr_mat),  # Growth-based distance matrix 
  ydis = as.dist(my_cbdist_mat), # Theoretical distance matrix
  method = "spearman",         
  permutations = 999,          
  na.rm = TRUE                 
)
print(mantel_result)
```

```{r,fig.height=2.5,fig.width=6,dpi=300}
my_df1[my_df1$pair_category=="Lower Glycolysis",]$xlab<-"Lower\nGlycolysis"
```
