### 3.7.3 Elbow analysis
```{r, fig.height=4,fig.width=5}

hc_result <- hclust(ma_dist_matrix, method = cl_method)
k_range <- 1:10
wss_values <- sapply(k_range, function(k) {
  ct <- cutree(hc_result, k = k)
  sum(sapply(unique(ct), function(cluster) {
    sub_dist <- as.matrix(ma_dist_matrix)[ct == cluster, ct == cluster, drop = FALSE]
    sum(sub_dist^2) / (2 * nrow(sub_dist))
  }))
})

elbow_df <- data.frame(k = k_range, wss = wss_values)


# Elbow Method for Optimal Number of Clusters
p_elbow <- ggplot(elbow_df, aes(x = k, y = wss)) +
  geom_line(color = "black", size = 1.5) +
  geom_point(color = "black", size = 4) +
  # geom_vline(xintercept = 2, linetype = 2, color = "red") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = k_range) + 
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,7))+
  theme_pubr(base_size = 20) +
  font("xy.text",size=26)+
  font("xylab",size=26)+
  labs(
    x = "Number of clusters",
    y = "Total within-cluster\n sum of squares"
  )

print(p_elbow)
Sys.time()
```
## 3.8 Comparison of dendrograms between essentiality-based and growth-based distances
### 3.8.1 Seven GEMs
#### 3.8.1.1 Entanglement score with permutation test
```{r,fig.width=1.5,fig.height=3.5,dpi=300}
# Genetic distance from FBA (7 GEMs consensus) and Phenotypic distance from Growth rates
dist_exp<-as.dist(1 - ma_matrix)
my_ins<-rownames(ma_matrix)
# dist_theory<-carbon_matrix_pre[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------ iML1515
dist_theory<-carbon_matrix_7gem[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------ 7 GEMs

# Hierarchical clustering using Ward's D2 method
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = cl_method)
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method)

dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# 2. Untangle: Optimize the layout of the two dendrograms to minimize crossings
# Maintaining the topology while rotating branches for better visualization
dl <- dendlist(dend_theory, dend_exp)
dl_untangled <- dendextend::untangle(dl, method = "step2side")

dend_p <- dl_untangled[[1]] # Optimized FBA-based dendrogram
dend_t <- dl_untangled[[2]] # Optimized Growth-based dendrogram


# 3. Create color vectors based on labels
# Retrieve current label order from the left (FBA) dendrogram
current_labels_p <- labels(dend_p)
# Map categories and colors to the current labels
groups_p <- carbon_labels_ordered_7gem$Category[match(current_labels_p, carbon_labels_ordered_7gem$label)]
col_vector_p <- carbon_labels_ordered_7gem$Category_col[match(current_labels_p, carbon_labels_ordered_7gem$label)]

# 4. Set label colors
dend_p <- dend_p %>% set("labels_colors", col_vector_p)

# Match Growth-based tree labels with the FBA-based tree's color vector
dend_t <- dend_t %>% 
  set("labels_colors", col_vector_p[match(labels(dend_t), current_labels_p)])

# 5. Draw Tanglegram
# Visualizing the structural similarity between metabolic theory and growth phenotype
tanglegram(dend_p, dend_t,
           common_subtrees_color_lines = FALSE, 
           highlight_distinct_edges = FALSE,
           highlight_branches_lwd = FALSE,
           color_lines = col_vector_p, 
           main_left = "FBA-based",
           main_right = "Growth-based",
           lab.cex = 1,
           lwd=2,
           columns_width = c(4, 1.5, 4),
           margin_inner = 3.5,
           margin_outer = 0.5,
           axes = FALSE)


# 6. Permutation Test for Entanglement Score
# Lower entanglement indicates higher structural similarity
actual_ent <- entanglement(dl_untangled) # Entanglement score after untangling

print(Sys.time())
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- if_else(iteration_scale=="large",1000,10)
perm_ent <- numeric(n_perm)

# Fixed theory-based labels
labels_theory <- labels(dend_p)

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # Copy the experimental dendrogram and shuffle labels
  shuffled_dend <- dend_t
  labels(shuffled_dend) <- sample(labels_theory)
  
  # Calculate entanglement for the shuffled pair after untangling
  perm_dends <- dendlist(dend_p, shuffled_dend) %>% 
    dendextend::untangle(method = "step2side")
  perm_ent[i] <- entanglement(perm_dends)
  
  # Progress monitoring
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# 7. Calculate P-value
# P-value = Probability that random entanglement is lower than the observed value
p_val_ent <- sum(perm_ent <= actual_ent) / n_perm

# 8. Visualization of results
hist(perm_ent, main="Permutation Test for Entanglement", 
     xlab="Entanglement Score", xlim=c(0, 1))
abline(v = actual_ent, col = "red", lwd = 2)
cat(sprintf("Actual Entanglement: %.3f\nP-value: %.4f\n", actual_ent, p_val_ent))

Sys.time()
```
#### 3.8.1.2 Cophenetic correlation with permutation test
```{r}
# 1. Prepare distance matrices and initial dendrograms
dist_exp<-as.dist(1 - ma_matrix)
my_ins<-rownames(ma_matrix)

# Theoretical distance based on 7 GEMs consensus
# dist_theory<-carbon_matrix_pre[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------ iML1515
dist_theory<-carbon_matrix_7gem[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------ 7 GEMs

# Hierarchical clustering
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = cl_method)
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method)

dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# Calculate observed Cophenetic correlation (Spearman)
# This measures how well the tree structure reflects the original distance matrix
actual_cor <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_exp, method = "spearman")

# --- Permutation Test for Cophenetic Correlation ---
print(Sys.time())
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- 1000
perm_results <- data.frame(cor = numeric(n_perm))

# Get original labels (strain names) from the experimental distance matrix
exp_labels <- rownames(as.matrix(dist_exp))

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # 1. Shuffle labels while keeping the underlying matrix structure intact
  dist_shuffled <- dist_exp
  shuffled_labels <- sample(exp_labels)
  
  # Convert to matrix to reassign shuffled names
  temp_mat <- as.matrix(dist_shuffled)
  rownames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  colnames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  
  # 2. Reconstruct dendrogram from the shuffled distance matrix
  hc_shuffled <- hclust(as.dist(temp_mat), method = cl_method)
  dend_shuffled <- as.dendrogram(hc_shuffled)
  
  # 3. Calculate and store the correlation for this permutation
  perm_results$cor[i] <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_shuffled, method = "spearman")
  
  # Progress monitoring
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# --- Statistical Evaluation ---
# P-value: Proportion of permutations where correlation is equal to or greater than observed
p_val_cor <- sum(perm_results$cor >= actual_cor) / n_perm

cat("【Analysis Results】\n")
cat(sprintf("Cophenetic Cor (Spearman): %.3f (p = %.4f)\n", actual_cor, p_val_cor))

# --- Visualization: Cophenetic Correlation Bubble Plot ---
# 1. Prepare data and count overlapping points (ties) for bubble sizing
df_coph <- data.frame(
  Theory = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_theory)),
  Experiment = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_exp))
) %>%
  group_by(Theory, Experiment) %>%
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = 'drop') # 各座標の重複数をカウント

my_txt<-paste("R=",sprintf("%.3f",actual_cor),sep="")

# 2. Plotting with ggscatter
# Bubble size and color intensity are log2-scaled to visualize the density of distance pairs
ggscatter(df_coph, x = "Theory", y = "Experiment",
          size = "count",           # Map count to dot size
          fill = "count",           # Map count to fill color
          color = "black",          # Fix border color to black
          shape = 21,               # Use filled circles with borders
          alpha= 0.8,
          xlab = "Cophenetic distance (Theory)",
          ylab = "Cophenetic distance (Experiment)",
          title = "Cophenetic Correlation (Log-scaled Bubble Size)",
          ylim=c(0,3)) +
  # Apply log2 transformation to size and color to handle the wide range of counts
  scale_size_continuous(trans = "log2", range = c(1, 12), name = "Count (log2)") +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Greys", trans = "log2", direction = 1, name = "Count (log2)")+
  annotate("text", x = 10, y = 2.7, label = my_txt,)

Sys.time()
```

```{r}
# dist_theory<-carbon_matrix_pre[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------ iML1515
dist_theory<-carbon_matrix_7gem[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------ 7 GEMs
dist_theory<-mean_carbon_dist_matrix[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------ cosine distance

# Hierarchical clustering
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = cl_method)
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method)

dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# Calculate observed Cophenetic correlation (Spearman)
# This measures how well the tree structure reflects the original distance matrix
actual_cor <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_exp, method = "spearman")

# --- Permutation Test for Cophenetic Correlation ---
print(Sys.time())
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- 1000
perm_results <- data.frame(cor = numeric(n_perm))

# Get original labels (strain names) from the experimental distance matrix
exp_labels <- rownames(as.matrix(dist_exp))

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # 1. Shuffle labels while keeping the underlying matrix structure intact
  dist_shuffled <- dist_exp
  shuffled_labels <- sample(exp_labels)
  
  # Convert to matrix to reassign shuffled names
  temp_mat <- as.matrix(dist_shuffled)
  rownames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  colnames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  
  # 2. Reconstruct dendrogram from the shuffled distance matrix
  hc_shuffled <- hclust(as.dist(temp_mat), method = cl_method)
  dend_shuffled <- as.dendrogram(hc_shuffled)
  
  # 3. Calculate and store the correlation for this permutation
  perm_results$cor[i] <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_shuffled, method = "spearman")
  
  # Progress monitoring
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# --- Statistical Evaluation ---
# P-value: Proportion of permutations where correlation is equal to or greater than observed
p_val_cor <- sum(perm_results$cor >= actual_cor) / n_perm

cat("【Analysis Results】\n")
cat(sprintf("Cophenetic Cor (Spearman): %.3f (p = %.4f)\n", actual_cor, p_val_cor))

# --- Visualization: Cophenetic Correlation Bubble Plot ---
# 1. Prepare data and count overlapping points (ties) for bubble sizing
df_coph <- data.frame(
  Theory = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_theory)),
  Experiment = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_exp))
) %>%
  group_by(Theory, Experiment) %>%
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = 'drop') # 各座標の重複数をカウント

my_txt<-paste("R=",sprintf("%.3f",actual_cor),sep="")

# 2. Plotting with ggscatter
# Bubble size and color intensity are log2-scaled to visualize the density of distance pairs
ggscatter(df_coph, x = "Theory", y = "Experiment",
          size = "count",           # Map count to dot size
          fill = "count",           # Map count to fill color
          color = "black",          # Fix border color to black
          shape = 21,               # Use filled circles with borders
          alpha= 0.8,
          xlab = "Cophenetic distance (Theory)",
          ylab = "Cophenetic distance (Experiment)",
          title = "Cophenetic Correlation (Log-scaled Bubble Size)",
          ylim=c(0,3)) +
  # Apply log2 transformation to size and color to handle the wide range of counts
  scale_size_continuous(trans = "log2", range = c(1, 12), name = "Count (log2)") +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Greys", trans = "log2", direction = 1, name = "Count (log2)")+
  annotate("text", x = 1, y = 2.7, label = my_txt,)

Sys.time()
```

```{r}
my_gr_mat<-ma_matrix_allrep

# Mantel test
set.seed(123)
mantel_result <- mantel(
  xdis = as.dist(1-my_gr_mat),  # Growth-based distance matrix 
  ydis = as.dist(my_cbdist_mat), # Theoretical distance matrix
  method = "spearman",         
  permutations = 999,

)
```

### 3.10.6 Comparison of dendrograms between essentiality-based and growth-based distances
#### 3.10.6.1 Entanglement score with permutation test in MA
```{r, fig.width=1.5,fig.height=3.5,dpi=300}
# Genetic distance from FBA (70 GEMs consensus) and Phenotypic distance from Growth rates
dist_exp<-as.dist(1 - ma_matrix_allrep)
my_ins<-rownames(ma_matrix_allrep)
dist_theory<-carbon_matrix_70gem[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------ 70 GEMs

# Hierarchical clustering using Ward's D2 method
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = cl_method)
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method)

dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# 2. Untangle: Optimize the layout of the two dendrograms to minimize crossings
# Maintaining the topology while rotating branches for better visualization
dl <- dendlist(dend_theory, dend_exp)
dl_untangled <- dendextend::untangle(dl, method = "step2side")

dend_p <- dl_untangled[[1]] # Optimized FBA-based dendrogram
dend_t <- dl_untangled[[2]] # Optimized Growth-based dendrogram


# 3. Create color vectors based on labels
# Retrieve current label order from the left (FBA) dendrogram
current_labels_p <- labels(dend_p)
# Map categories and colors to the current labels
groups_p <- carbon_labels_ordered_7gem$Category[match(current_labels_p, carbon_labels_ordered_7gem$label)]
col_vector_p <- carbon_labels_ordered_7gem$Category_col[match(current_labels_p, carbon_labels_ordered_7gem$label)]

# 4. Set label colors
dend_p <- dend_p %>% set("labels_colors", col_vector_p)

# Match Growth-based tree labels with the FBA-based tree's color vector
dend_t <- dend_t %>% 
  set("labels_colors", col_vector_p[match(labels(dend_t), current_labels_p)])

# 5. Draw Tanglegram
# Visualizing the structural similarity between metabolic theory and growth phenotype
tanglegram(dend_p, dend_t,
           common_subtrees_color_lines = FALSE, 
           highlight_distinct_edges = FALSE,
           highlight_branches_lwd = FALSE,
           color_lines = col_vector_p, 
           main_left = "FBA-based",
           main_right = "Growth-based",
           lab.cex = 1,
           lwd=2,
           columns_width = c(4, 1.5, 4),
           margin_inner = 3.5,
           margin_outer = 0.5,
           axes = FALSE)


# 6. Permutation Test for Entanglement Score
# Lower entanglement indicates higher structural similarity
actual_ent <- entanglement(dl_untangled) # Entanglement score after untangling

print(Sys.time())
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- if_else(iteration_scale=="large",1000,10)
perm_ent <- numeric(n_perm)

# Fixed theory-based labels
labels_theory <- labels(dend_p)

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # Copy the experimental dendrogram and shuffle labels
  shuffled_dend <- dend_t
  labels(shuffled_dend) <- sample(labels_theory)
  
  # Calculate entanglement for the shuffled pair after untangling
  perm_dends <- dendlist(dend_p, shuffled_dend) %>% 
    dendextend::untangle(method = "step2side")
  perm_ent[i] <- entanglement(perm_dends)
  
  # Progress monitoring
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# 7. Calculate P-value
# P-value = Probability that random entanglement is lower than the observed value
p_val_ent <- sum(perm_ent <= actual_ent) / n_perm

# 8. Visualization of results
hist(perm_ent, main="Permutation Test for Entanglement", 
     xlab="Entanglement Score", xlim=c(0, 1))
abline(v = actual_ent, col = "red", lwd = 2)
cat(sprintf("Actual Entanglement: %.3f\nP-value: %.4f\n", actual_ent, p_val_ent))

Sys.time()
```

```{r}
# 1. Prepare distance matrices and initial dendrograms
dist_exp<-as.dist(1 - my_mat)

dist_theory<-mean_carbon_dist_matrix[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------ flux based distance

# Hierarchical clustering
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = cl_method)
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method)

dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# Calculate observed Cophenetic correlation (Spearman)
# This measures how well the tree structure reflects the original distance matrix
actual_cor <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_exp, method = "spearman")

# --- Permutation Test for Cophenetic Correlation ---
print(Sys.time())
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- 1000
perm_results <- data.frame(cor = numeric(n_perm))

# Get original labels (strain names) from the experimental distance matrix
exp_labels <- rownames(as.matrix(dist_exp))

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # 1. Shuffle labels while keeping the underlying matrix structure intact
  dist_shuffled <- dist_exp
  shuffled_labels <- sample(exp_labels)
  
  # Convert to matrix to reassign shuffled names
  temp_mat <- as.matrix(dist_shuffled)
  rownames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  colnames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  
  # 2. Reconstruct dendrogram from the shuffled distance matrix
  hc_shuffled <- hclust(as.dist(temp_mat), method = cl_method)
  dend_shuffled <- as.dendrogram(hc_shuffled)
  
  # 3. Calculate and store the correlation for this permutation
  perm_results$cor[i] <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_shuffled, method = "spearman")
  
  # Progress monitoring
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# --- Statistical Evaluation ---
# P-value: Proportion of permutations where correlation is equal to or greater than observed
p_val_cor <- sum(perm_results$cor >= actual_cor) / n_perm

cat("【Analysis Results】\n")
cat(sprintf("Cophenetic Cor (Spearman): %.3f (p = %.4f)\n", actual_cor, p_val_cor))

# --- Visualization: Cophenetic Correlation Bubble Plot ---
# 1. Prepare data and count overlapping points (ties) for bubble sizing
df_coph <- data.frame(
  Theory = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_theory)),
  Experiment = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_exp))
) %>%
  group_by(Theory, Experiment) %>%
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = 'drop') # 各座標の重複数をカウント

my_txt<-paste("R=",sprintf("%.3f",actual_cor),sep="")

# 2. Plotting with ggscatter
# Bubble size and color intensity are log2-scaled to visualize the density of distance pairs
ggscatter(df_coph, x = "Theory", y = "Experiment",
          size = "count",           # Map count to dot size
          fill = "count",           # Map count to fill color
          color = "black",          # Fix border color to black
          shape = 21,               # Use filled circles with borders
          alpha= 0.8,
          xlab = "Cophenetic distance (Theory)",
          ylab = "Cophenetic distance (Experiment)",
          title = "Cophenetic Correlation (Log-scaled Bubble Size)",
          ylim=c(0,3)) +
  # Apply log2 transformation to size and color to handle the wide range of counts
  scale_size_continuous(trans = "log2", range = c(1, 12), name = "Count (log2)") +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Greys", trans = "log2", direction = 1, name = "Count (log2)")+
  annotate("text", x = 0.2, y = 2.7, label = my_txt,)

Sys.time()
```

```{r, fig.height=10,fig.width=10,dpi=300}
# --- 1. Load and join data ---
my_dat <- paste(getwd(), "Preculture", "Output", "preculod_ma.csv", sep = "/") %>% 
  read_csv() %>% 
  select(colony_round, Abb, PreculOD) %>% 
  rename(carbon = Abb, precul_od = PreculOD)

my_df <- left_join(gr_ma_df, my_dat, by = c("colony_round", "carbon"))


# ==============================================================================
# Pattern A: Display p_adj at fixed coordinates (0.9, 0.4) on the mu_max plot
# ==============================================================================

# 1. Correlation analysis, BH correction, and specification of fixed label coordinates
cor_results_mu <- my_df %>% 
  filter(!is.na(precul_od) & !is.na(mu_max_allrep)) %>% 
  group_by(carbon) %>% 
  summarise(
    res = list(if(n() >= 3) cor.test(precul_od, mu_max_allrep, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE) else NULL)
  ) %>% 
  filter(!map_lgl(res, is.null)) %>% 
  mutate(
    rho = map_dbl(res, ~ .x$estimate),
    p_value = map_dbl(res, ~ .x$p.value)
  ) %>% 
  select(-res) %>% 
  mutate(
    p_adj = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH"),
    label = sprintf("R = %.2f\np.adj = %.2g", rho, p_adj),
    # --- Specify fixed label coordinates directly ---
    precul_od = 0.95, 
    mu_max_allrep = 0.4
  )

# 2. Draw the plot
p1 <- ggscatter(my_df, x = "precul_od", y = "mu_max_allrep", 
                color = "carbon", alpha = 0.2, legend = "none", 
                cor.coef = FALSE)

# Facet the plot and overlay text using the fixed-coordinate data above
p1 <- facet(p1, facet.by = "carbon") +
  geom_text(data = cor_results_mu, aes(label = label), color = "black", size = 3.5, hjust = 0.5)

print(p1)

# 3. Extract significant results (e.g., adjusted p-value < 0.05)
significant_results <- cor_results_mu %>%
  # Create a new column (p_adj_sig2) rounded to 2 significant figures
  mutate(p_adj_sig2 = signif(p_adj, digits = 2)) %>% 
  # Filter for rounded values below 0.05
  filter(p_adj_sig2 < 0.05) %>% 
  # Sort by the rounded values
  arrange(p_adj_sig2)

# Check the results (return a message if nothing is significant)
if (nrow(significant_results) == 0) {
  message("No significant correlations found for mu_max after BH correction for multiple testing.")
} else {
  print(significant_results)
}

    p_adj = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH"),

    # --- Specify fixed label coordinates directly ---
    precul_od = 0.95, 
    rel_mu_max_allrep = 2.3
  )

# 2. Draw the plot
p3 <- ggscatter(my_df, x = "precul_od", y = "rel_mu_max_allrep", 
                color = "carbon", alpha = 0.2, legend = "none", 
                cor.coef = FALSE)

# Facet the plot and overlay text using the fixed-coordinate data above
p3 <- facet(p3, facet.by = "carbon") +
  geom_text(data = cor_results_relmu, aes(label = label), color = "black", size = 3.5, hjust = 0.5)

print(p3)

# 3. Extract significant results (e.g., adjusted p-value < 0.05)
significant_results <- cor_results_relmu %>%
  # Create a new column (p_adj_sig2) rounded to 2 significant figures
  mutate(p_adj_sig2 = signif(p_adj, digits = 2)) %>% 
  # Filter for rounded values below 0.05
  filter(p_adj_sig2 < 0.05) %>% 
  # Sort by the rounded values
  arrange(p_adj_sig2)

# Check the results (return a message if nothing is significant)
if (nrow(significant_results) == 0) {
  message("No significant correlations found for rel_mu after BH correction for multiple testing.")
} else {
  print(significant_results)
}


# Check for confounding
# ----------------------------------------------------
# 1. Reshape the data (extract strains with complete data across all carbon sources)
# ----------------------------------------------------
wide_mu <- my_df %>%
  dplyr::select(colony_round, carbon, rel_mu_max) %>%
  filter(!is.na(rel_mu_max)) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon, values_from = rel_mu_max)

wide_od <- my_df %>%
  dplyr::select(colony_round, carbon, precul_od) %>%
  filter(!is.na(precul_od)) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon, values_from = precul_od)

common_strains <- intersect(wide_mu$colony_round, wide_od$colony_round)

mat_mu <- wide_mu %>% 
  filter(colony_round %in% common_strains) %>% 
  arrange(colony_round) %>%
  filter(colony_round %nin% c("colony1@0","colony2@0","colony3@0")) %>%
  dplyr::select(-colony_round) %>% 
  as.matrix()

mat_od <- wide_od %>% 
  filter(colony_round %in% common_strains) %>% 
  arrange(colony_round) %>% 
  filter(colony_round %nin% c("colony1@0","colony2@0","colony3@0")) %>%
  dplyr::select(-colony_round) %>% 
  as.matrix()

all_carbons <- colnames(mat_mu)
carbon_pairs_tmp <- t(combn(all_carbons, 2)) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  rename(carbon_1 = V1, carbon_2 = V2)

# ----------------------------------------------------
# 2. Batch calculation of Spearman partial correlations using residuals (robust version)
# ----------------------------------------------------
analysis_results <- carbon_pairs_tmp %>%
  split(1:nrow(.)) %>% 
  map_dfr(function(pair) {
    c1 <- pair$carbon_1
    c2 <- pair$carbon_2
    
    y1 <- mat_mu[, c1]
    y2 <- mat_mu[, c2]
    z1 <- mat_od[, c1]
    z2 <- mat_od[, c2]
    
    # Standard correlation
    raw_cor <- cor.test(y1, y2, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)
    
    # Partial correlation: compute residuals after removing the effects of z1 and z2
    res_cor <- tryCatch({
      # Convert y1, y2, z1, z2 to ranks
      r_y1 <- rank(y1); r_y2 <- rank(y2); r_z1 <- rank(z1); r_z2 <- rank(z2)
      
      # Regress on control variables (z1, z2) and extract residuals (unexplained variation)
      fit1 <- lm(r_y1 ~ r_z1 + r_z2)
      fit2 <- lm(r_y2 ~ r_z1 + r_z2)
      
      # Calculate Spearman correlation between the residuals
      cor.test(residuals(fit1), residuals(fit2), method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)
    }, error = function(e) return(NULL))
    
    if (!is.null(res_cor)) {
      tibble(
        carbon_1   = c1,
        carbon_2   = c2,
        raw_rho    = raw_cor$estimate,
        raw_p      = raw_cor$p.value,
        pcor_rho   = res_cor$estimate,
        pcor_p     = res_cor$p.value
      )
    } else {
      NULL
    }
  })

# ----------------------------------------------------
# 3. Multiple testing correction (Benjamini-Hochberg method)
# ----------------------------------------------------
final_comparison <- analysis_results %>%
  mutate(
    raw_p_adj  = p.adjust(raw_p, method = "BH"),
    pcor_p_adj = p.adjust(pcor_p, method = "BH"),
    rho_drop   = raw_rho - pcor_rho
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(carbon_1, carbon_2, raw_rho, raw_p_adj, pcor_rho, pcor_p_adj, rho_drop)

# Check the results
print(head(final_comparison, 10))

ggscatter(final_comparison, x="raw_rho",y="pcor_rho",
          cor.coef = T,
          cor.coeff.args = list(method="spearman"))+
  geom_abline(slope = 1,intercept = 0,color="red")
  
Sys.time()
```

```{r,fig.width=5,fig.height=2.5, dpi=300}
# 1. Function to create a scatter plot comparing two carbon sources
plot_carbon_pair <- function(df, c1, c2, cor_args = list(method = "spearman"), y_scale = NULL) {
  
  # Extract data and rename columns simultaneously
  df1 <- df %>% filter(carbon == c1) %>% select(strain, mu_max_1 = mu_max_allrep)
  df2 <- df %>% filter(carbon == c2) %>% select(strain, mu_max_2 = mu_max_allrep)
  
  merged_df <- left_join(df1, df2, by = "strain")
  
  p <- ggscatter(
    merged_df, x = "mu_max_1", y = "mu_max_2", alpha = 0.5,
    cor.coef = TRUE, cor.coeff.args = cor_args
  ) +
    xlab(bquote(mu[max] ~ "on" ~ .(c1) ~ "[1/h]")) +
    ylab(bquote(mu[max] ~ "on" ~ .(c2) ~ "[1/h]"))
  
  # Apply a custom y-axis scale if provided (for Pair 2)
  if (!is.null(y_scale)) p <- p + y_scale
  
  return(p)
}

# 2. Run the function and combine the plots
p1 <- plot_carbon_pair(gr_ecor_df, "Glc", "Fru", cor_args = list(label.sep = "\n", method = "spearman"))
p2 <- plot_carbon_pair(gr_ecor_df, "Glc", "Fum", y_scale = scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 0.8, 0.4), limits = c(0, 0.8)))

p1 + p2
Sys.time()
```

## 4.4 Interstrain correlation
### 4.4.1. Calc. interstrain correlation (Two reps and Four reps)
```{r}
ecor_pair_all<-carbon_dist_integrated_long
ecor_pair_all<-ecor_pair_all %>%
  filter(carbon1 %in% ecor_carbons) %>%
  filter(carbon2 %in% ecor_carbons)

ecor_pair_all$correlation<-NA
ecor_pair_all$correlation_allrep<-NA
i<-1
for (i in 1:nrow(ecor_pair_all)){
  my_carbon_1<-ecor_pair_all$carbon1[i]
  my_carbon_2<-ecor_pair_all$carbon2[i]
  my_df1<-gr_ecor_df %>%
    filter(carbon==my_carbon_1) %>%
    select(strain,mu_max,mu_max_allrep) %>%
    rename(mu_max_1=mu_max,mu_max_allrep_1=mu_max_allrep)
  my_df2<-gr_ecor_df %>%
    filter(carbon==my_carbon_2) %>%
    select(strain,mu_max,mu_max_allrep) %>%
    rename(mu_max_2=mu_max,mu_max_allrep_2=mu_max_allrep)
  my_df<-left_join(my_df1,my_df2,by="strain")
  my_res<-cor_test(my_df,vars = "mu_max_1",vars2 = "mu_max_2",method = "spearman")
  ecor_pair_all$correlation[i]<-my_res$cor
  my_res<-cor_test(my_df,vars = "mu_max_allrep_1",vars2 = "mu_max_allrep_2",method = "spearman")
  ecor_pair_all$correlation_allrep[i]<-my_res$cor
}

  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon2, values_from = correlation) %>%
  column_to_rownames("carbon1") %>%

ecor_matrix_allrep <- ecor_matrix_allrep[target_order, target_order]
```

### 4.5.2 Mantel test
#### 4.5.2.1 Two reps
##### 4.5.2.1.1 Flux-based (70 ECOR strains)
```{r}
my_gr_mat<-ecor_matrix
my_rows<-rownames(my_gr_mat)
my_cbdist_mat<-mean_carbon_dist_matrix[my_rows,my_rows]

# Mantel test
set.seed(123)
mantel_result <- mantel(
  xdis = as.dist(1-my_gr_mat),  # Growth-based correlation matrix
  ydis = as.dist(my_cbdist_mat), # Theoretical distance matrix
  method = "spearman",         
  permutations = 999,          
  na.rm = TRUE                 
)

print(mantel_result)
```

## 4.6 Interstrain correlation across metabolic pathway categories
### 4.6.1 Comparison with global between-categories
```{r,fig.height=2.6,fig.width=7,dpi=300}
my_palette<-c("#0072B2", "#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73", "#8FD926", "grey70", "#000000")
my_df1<-ecor_pair_all[(ecor_pair_all$key=="upper")&(ecor_pair_all$pair_category!="between"),]
# my_df1$pair_category<-factor(my_df1$pair_category,levels = carbon_categories)
my_df1$xlab<-my_df1$pair_category %>% as.character()
my_df1[my_df1$pair_category=="Upper Glycolysis",]$xlab<-"Upper\nGlycolysis"
my_df1[my_df1$pair_category=="Lower Glycolysis",]$xlab<-"Lower\nGlycolysis"
my_df1[my_df1$pair_category=="Pentose Phosphate",]$xlab<-"Pentose\nPhosphate"
my_df1[my_df1$pair_category=="TCA cycle",]$xlab<-"TCA\ncycle"
my_df1[my_df1$pair_category=="Amino acid-derived TCA input",]$xlab<-"Amino acid\nderived\nTCA input"

my_df2<-ecor_pair_all[(ecor_pair_all$key=="upper"),]
my_df2$xlab<-my_df2$pair_category
my_df2[my_df2$xlab!="between",]$xlab<-"Within"
my_df2[my_df2$xlab=="between",]$xlab<-"Between"

my_df<-bind_rows(my_df1,my_df2)
my_label<-c("Upper\nGlycolysis","Lower\nGlycolysis","Pentose\nPhosphate","TCA\ncycle","Amino acid\nderived\nTCA input","Within","Between")
my_df$xlab<-factor(my_df$xlab,levels = my_label)

# Wilcoxon test
my_df %>%
  wilcox_test(formula = correlation ~ xlab,
              ref.group = "Between",
              p.adjust.method = "BH"
              )

# Two reps
ggboxplot(my_df,
          x="xlab",y="correlation",
          ylab="Interstrain correlation[-]",xlab="",
          add="jitter",add.params = list(alpha=0.5),
          color = "xlab",palette = my_palette,legend="")+
  stat_pwc(method = "wilcox.test",label = "p.adj.signif",
           ref.group = "Between",tip.length = 0,
    p.adjust.method = "BH",hide.ns = TRUE 
  )+
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = get_breaks(from = -0.4,to = 1.2,by = 0.4),limits = c(-0.4,1.4))

# Four reps
ggboxplot(my_df,
          x="xlab",y="correlation_allrep",
          ylab="Interstrain correlation[-]",xlab="",
          add="jitter",add.params = list(alpha=0.5),
          color = "xlab",palette = my_palette,legend="")+
  stat_pwc(method = "wilcox.test",label = "p.adj.signif",
           ref.group = "Between",tip.length = 0,
    p.adjust.method = "BH",hide.ns = TRUE 
  )+
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = get_breaks(from = -0.4,to = 1.2,by = 0.4),limits = c(-0.4,1.4))
Sys.time()
```
### 4.6.2 Comparison with local between-categories
#### 4.6.2.1 Two reps
##### 4.6.2.1.1 Statistical test
```{r,fig.width=1.7,fig.height=2,dpi=300}
my_palette<-c("#0072B2", "#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#CC79A7", "#009E73","#8FD926")
my_pathctgs<-c("Upper Glycolysis",
          "Lower Glycolysis",
          "Pentose Phosphate",
          "Entner Doudoroff",
          "TCA cycle",
          "Amino acid-derived TCA input")
pathctgs_df<-data.frame(category=my_pathctgs,
                        label=c("Upper\nGlycolysis",
          "Lower\nGlycolysis",
          "Pentose\nPhosphate",
          "Entner\nDoudoroff",
          "TCA\ncycle",
          "Amino acid-\nderived\nTCA input"),
                        color=my_palette)
  
my_df<-ecor_pair_all[ecor_pair_all$key=="upper",]
my_list<-list()
my_p_list<-list()
i<-6
for(i in 1:nrow(pathctgs_df)){
  my_cls<-pathctgs_df$category[i]
  my_dat<-my_df[(my_df$category1==my_cls)|(my_df$category2==my_cls),]
  n_cbn<-c(my_dat[my_dat$category1==my_cls,]$carbon1,my_dat[my_dat$category2==my_cls,]$carbon2) %>% unique() %>% length()
  if(n_cbn>1){
    my_dat$pair_mpc<-"Between"
    my_dat[my_dat$category1==my_dat$category2,]$pair_mpc<-pathctgs_df$label[i]
    my_dat$pair_mpc<-factor(my_dat$pair_mpc,levels=c(pathctgs_df$label[i],"Between"))
    my_dat$pair_category<-factor(my_dat$pair_category,levels=c(pathctgs_df$category[i],"between"))
    my_list[[i]]<-ggboxplot(my_dat,
            # x="pair_mpc",y="correlation",
            x="pair_category",y="correlation",
            ylab="Interstrain correlation [-]",xlab="",
            # color="pair_mpc",
            color="pair_category",
            add="jitter",add.params = list(alpha=0.5),
            palette = c(pathctgs_df$color[i],"grey60"),
            legend="")+
    stat_pwc(method = "wilcox.test",label = "p.adj.signif",
             # ref.group = "Between",
             ref.group = "between",
             tip.length = 0,
      p.adjust.method = "BH",hide.ns = TRUE)+
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-0.4, 0.8, by = 0.4), limits = c(-0.4, 1.2))
    # Wilcoxon test
    my_res<-my_dat %>%
      # wilcox_test(formula = correlation ~ pair_mpc,
      wilcox_test(formula = correlation ~ pair_category,
      # ref.group = "Between",
      ref.group = "between",
      p.adjust.method = "BH")
    my_p_list[[i]]<-my_res$p
  }
}
p.adjust(my_p_list%>% unlist(),method = "BH")
table(my_df$pair_category, useNA = "ifany")
my_list[[1]]
my_list[[2]]
my_list[[3]]
my_list[[4]]
my_list[[5]]
my_list[[6]]

sapply(pathctgs_df$category, function(cls) {
  sub_df <- my_df[(my_df$category1 == cls) | (my_df$category2 == cls), ]
  sum(sub_df$pair_category == "between", na.rm = TRUE)
})

Sys.time()
```
##### 4.6.2.1.2 Subsampling
```{r,fig.height=3,fig.width=3, dpi=300}
target_cls <- "Upper Glycolysis"
ug_dat <- my_df[(my_df$category1 == target_cls) | (my_df$category2 == target_cls), ]
ug_dat$pair_category <- factor(ug_dat$pair_category, levels = c(target_cls, "between"))

ug_within  <- ug_dat %>% filter(pair_category == target_cls)
ug_between <- ug_dat %>% filter(pair_category == "between")

cat("Original - Within:", nrow(ug_within), " / Between:", nrow(ug_between), "\n")

set.seed(123)
n_iter <- 1000
p_values <- numeric(n_iter)

for (k in 1:n_iter) {
  sampled_within <- ug_within %>% sample_n(size = 6, replace = FALSE)
  
  sub_dat <- bind_rows(sampled_within, ug_between)
  
  test_res <- sub_dat %>%
    wilcox_test(formula = correlation ~ pair_category,
                ref.group = "between")
  
  p_values[k] <- test_res$p
}


signif_ratio <- mean(p_values < 0.05)

cat("=== Sampling results (N=6, 1000 trials) ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Proportion significant (p < 0.05): %.1f%%\n", signif_ratio * 100))
cat(sprintf("Median p-value: %.4f (interquartile range: %.4f - %.4f)\n", 
            median(p_values), 
            quantile(p_values, 0.25), 
            quantile(p_values, 0.75)))


hist(p_values, breaks = 50, main = "p-value distribution (Upper Glycolysis: n=6)",
     xlab = "Wilcoxon test p-value", col = "skyblue", border = "white")
abline(v = 0.05, col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 2) 
Sys.time()
```
##### 4.6.2.1.3 Carbon source node-based subsampling validation (1000 trials)
```{r}
# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Approach B: Carbon source node-based subsampling validation (1000 trials)
# ---------------------------------------------------------

target_cls <- "Upper Glycolysis"

# 1. Extract pair data associated with Upper Glycolysis
# (pairs where either category1 or category2 is Upper Glycolysis)
ug_dat <- my_df[(my_df$category1 == target_cls) | (my_df$category2 == target_cls), ]

# Get the unique list of carbon sources belonging to Upper Glycolysis
ug_carbons <- unique(c(
  ug_dat[ug_dat$category1 == target_cls, ]$carbon1,
  ug_dat[ug_dat$category2 == target_cls, ]$carbon2
))

# Number of carbon source nodes to sample, matched to the comparison category
# (e.g., set to 4 if the comparison category has 4 carbon sources; TCA cycle has 4)
target_node_n <- 4

cat(sprintf("Total carbon sources in Upper Glycolysis: %d -> Nodes to sample: %d\n", 
            length(ug_carbons), target_node_n))

# 2. Run the node-sampling loop for 1000 iterations
set.seed(123) # Fix seed for reproducibility
n_iter <- 1000

p_values <- numeric(n_iter)
within_n_list <- numeric(n_iter)
between_n_list <- numeric(n_iter)

for (k in 1:n_iter) {
  # (1) Randomly sample target_node_n carbon sources from Upper Glycolysis
  sampled_nodes <- sample(ug_carbons, size = target_node_n, replace = FALSE)
  
  # (2) Create a subset restricted to the sampled carbon sources
  # - Within: both category1 and category2 are Upper Glycolysis and both carbon sources are in sampled_nodes
  # - Between: one side is Upper Glycolysis (and in sampled_nodes) while the other belongs to a different category
  sub_dat <- ug_dat %>%
    filter(
      (category1 == target_cls & category2 == target_cls & carbon1 %in% sampled_nodes & carbon2 %in% sampled_nodes) |
      (category1 == target_cls & category2 != target_cls & carbon1 %in% sampled_nodes) |
      (category1 != target_cls & category2 == target_cls & carbon2 %in% sampled_nodes)
    )
  
  # Set factor levels ("Upper Glycolysis" vs "between")
  sub_dat$pair_category <- factor(sub_dat$pair_category, levels = c(target_cls, "between"))
  
  # Record the number of pairs in each iteration
  within_n_list[k]  <- sum(sub_dat$pair_category == target_cls, na.rm = TRUE)
  between_n_list[k] <- sum(sub_dat$pair_category == "between", na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # (3) Run the Wilcoxon test
  test_res <- sub_dat %>%
    wilcox_test(formula = correlation ~ pair_category, ref.group = "between")
  
  p_values[k] <- test_res$p
}

# 3. Summarize and print results
signif_ratio <- mean(p_values < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)

cat("\n=== Node subsampling results (1000 trials) ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Mean number of pairs - Within: %.1f / Between: %.1f\n", 
            mean(within_n_list), mean(between_n_list)))
cat(sprintf("Proportion significant (p < 0.05): %.1f%%\n", signif_ratio * 100))
cat(sprintf("Median p-value: %.4f (interquartile range: %.4f - %.4f)\n", 
            median(p_values, na.rm = TRUE), 
            quantile(p_values, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE), 
            quantile(p_values, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)))

# 4. Visualize the p-value distribution as a histogram
hist(p_values, breaks = 50, 
     main = sprintf("p-value distribution (Node N=%d)", target_node_n),
     xlab = "Wilcoxon test p-value", col = "skyblue", border = "white")
abline(v = 0.05, col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 2)

Sys.time()
```

#### 4.7.1.3 pvclust
```{r}
# ==========================================
# 2. [NEW] Data reshaping and computation for pvclust
# ==========================================
message("Preparing data for pvclust...")

# Create a matrix from the raw data: rows = strain, columns = carbon, values = mu_max
# Restricted to the target carbon sources (ecor_carbons)
pv_raw_data <- gr_ecor_df %>%
  filter(carbon %in% ecor_carbons) %>%
  select(strain, carbon, mu_max) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon, values_from = mu_max) %>%
  column_to_rownames("strain") %>%
  as.matrix()

# Sort column names (carbon source names) to match the ordering of the upstream matrix
pv_raw_data <- pv_raw_data[, sort(colnames(pv_raw_data))]

# [IMPORTANT] Define a custom distance function based on Spearman correlation (1 - r)
# pvclust computes distances between "columns" internally, so cor(x, method="spearman") is used
dist.spearman <- function(x) {
  # Compute Spearman correlation coefficients between columns of x
  cor_matrix <- cor(x, method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
  # Convert to distance (1 - r) and return as a dist object
  return(as.dist(1 - cor_matrix))
}

message("Running bootstrap clustering with pvclust (Spearman correlation-based)...")

# Run pvclust
pv_result <- pvclust(
  data          = pv_raw_data,
  method.hclust = cl_method,
  method.dist   = dist.spearman, # Custom distance function defined above
  nboot         = 1000,
  parallel      = TRUE
)

# ==========================================
# 4. [NEW] Visualization of pvclust results (significant modules)
# ==========================================
# Draw the dendrogram with statistical support values
plot(pv_result, cex = 0.8, main = "Carbon source clustering (with bootstrap validation)")

# Highlight modules significant at the 95% level (AU >= 0.95) with red boxes
# These modules are robust enough to be considered non-random even accounting for variance
pvrect(pv_result, alpha = 0.95, stroke = 2, border = "red")
Sys.time()
```

```{r, fig.height=4,fig.width=5}

hc_result <- hclust(as.dist(ecor_dist_matrix), method = cl_method)
k_range <- 1:10
wss_values <- sapply(k_range, function(k) {
  ct <- cutree(hc_result, k = k)

  sum(sapply(unique(ct), function(cluster) {
    sub_dist <- as.matrix(ecor_dist_matrix)[ct == cluster, ct == cluster, drop = FALSE]
    sum(sub_dist^2) / (2 * nrow(sub_dist))
  }))
})

elbow_df <- data.frame(k = k_range, wss = wss_values)

# Elbow Method for Optimal Number of Clusters
p_elbow <- ggplot(elbow_df, aes(x = k, y = wss)) +
  geom_line(color = "black", size = 1.5) +
  geom_point(color = "black", size = 4) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 2, linetype = 2, color = "red") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = k_range) + 
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,7))+

  font("xy.text",size=26)+
  font("xylab",size=26)+

  )
```

#### 4.7.1.5 Interstrain correlation across clusters (k=2)
```{r,fig.width=4,fig.height=3,dpi=300}
# 1. Clustering based on experimental evolutionary distances
# Define the number of theoretical clusters (k)
k_val <- 2

dist_exp<-ecor_dist_matrix
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method)
cluster_exp    <- cutree(hc_exp, k = k_val)

# Create a mapping table for carbon sources and their assigned clusters
my_tmp<-data.frame(carbon=names(cluster_exp),exp=cluster_exp)
carbon_clust_tbl<-my_tmp


# Print carbon sources belonging to each cluster for inspection
for(i in 1:k_val){
  paste("cluster ",i,": ",paste(my_tmp[my_tmp$exp==i,]$carbon,collapse = ","),sep="") %>% print()
}

# 2. Data Integration
# Focus on unique pairs (upper triangle) and join with cluster assignments
my_df<-ecor_pair_all[ecor_pair_all$key=="upper",]
my_tmp1<-my_tmp %>% rename(carbon1=carbon,exp1=exp)
my_tmp2<-my_tmp %>% rename(carbon2=carbon,exp2=exp)
my_df<-left_join(my_df,my_tmp1,by="carbon1")
my_df<-left_join(my_df,my_tmp2,by="carbon2")

my_clstrs<-seq(1,k_val)

# ==========================================
# 3. Data reshaping: automatically determine cluster numbering
#    based on the count of Upper Glycolysis carbon sources per cluster
# ==========================================
# Count the number of Upper Glycolysis pairs in each cluster
# using the original assignments (exp=1, exp=2, etc.)
cluster_counts <- my_df %>%
  mutate(pair_type_raw = case_when(
    exp1 == 1 & exp2 == 1 ~ "C1",
    exp1 == 2 & exp2 == 2 ~ "C2",
    TRUE                  ~ "Between"
  )) %>%
  # Retain only within-cluster pairs and count Upper Glycolysis occurrences per cluster
  filter(pair_type_raw %in% c("C1", "C2")) %>%
  group_by(pair_type_raw) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(upper_glyco_count = sum(pair_category == "Upper Glycolysis", na.rm = TRUE))

# Identify the original cluster label that contains more Upper Glycolysis pairs
# (in case of a tie, C1 is given priority)
target_raw_c1 <- cluster_counts$pair_type_raw[which.max(cluster_counts$upper_glyco_count)]

# Based on the result above, assign new cluster labels
# (the cluster with more Upper Glycolysis pairs becomes new Cluster 1)
plot_df <- my_df %>%
  mutate(
    pair_type = case_when(
      exp1 == 1 & exp2 == 1 ~ if_else(target_raw_c1 == "C1", "Cluster 1", "Cluster 2"),
      exp1 == 2 & exp2 == 2 ~ if_else(target_raw_c1 == "C2", "Cluster 1", "Cluster 2"),
      TRUE                  ~ "Between"
    )
  ) %>%
  # Fix the order for plotting and testing to "Cluster 1, Cluster 2, Between"
  mutate(pair_type = factor(pair_type, levels = c("Cluster 1", "Cluster 2", "Between")))

# Print which original cluster was assigned as new Cluster 1
print(paste("The cluster with more Upper Glycolysis pairs was set as 'Cluster 1'. Original cluster:", target_raw_c1))


# ==========================================
# 4. Visualization and statistical testing (error-safe version)
# ==========================================
# Embed wilcox.test directly in ggboxplot to reliably avoid mapping errors
p_integrated <- ggboxplot(
  plot_df,
  x = "pair_type", 
  y = "correlation",
  ylab = "Interstrain correlation [-]", 
  xlab = "",
  add = "jitter", 
  add.params = list(alpha = 0.4, size = 1.5), 
  theme = theme_pubr(base_size = 20)
) +
  font("xy.text", size = 22) +
  font("ylab", size = 22) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-0.4, 1.0, by = 0.4), limits = c(-0.4, 1.3)) +
  stat_pwc(
    method = "wilcox.test",
    ref.group = "Between",      # Use "Between" as the reference group
    p.adjust.method = "BH",     
    label = "p.adj.signif",     
    tip.length = 0,
    bracket.nudge.y = 0.05, 
    hide.ns = TRUE              # Hide non-significant comparisons
  )

print(p_integrated)


# ==========================================
# 5. (For verification) Detailed statistical results in text form
# ==========================================
stat_test <- plot_df %>%
  wilcox_test(
    formula = correlation ~ pair_type,
    ref.group = "Between",
    p.adjust.method = "BH"
  )
print("Detailed adjusted p-values compared to Between:")
print(stat_test)

# Extract a mapping table of carbon sources to new cluster labels (Cluster 1 / 2)
# from the finalized plot_df of the ECOR analysis above
# This carries forward the cluster definitions corrected by Upper Glycolysis count
cbnclust_tbl_ecorbased <- plot_df %>%
  # Build the mapping from both carbon1 and carbon2 so each carbon source gets its own row
  select(carbon = carbon1, pair_type) %>%
  bind_rows(select(plot_df, carbon = carbon2, pair_type)) %>%
  filter(pair_type %in% c("Cluster 1", "Cluster 2")) %>%
  distinct(carbon, pair_type)

Sys.time()
```

```{r,fig.width=2.5,fig.height=2,dpi=300}
# 1. Clustering based on experimental evolutionary distances
# Define the number of theoretical clusters (k)
k_val <- 3

dist_exp<-ecor_dist_matrix
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method)
cluster_exp    <- cutree(hc_exp, k = k_val)

# Create a mapping table for carbon sources and their assigned clusters
my_tmp<-data.frame(carbon=names(cluster_exp),exp=cluster_exp)
carbon_clust_tbl<-my_tmp


# Print carbon sources belonging to each cluster for inspection
for(i in 1:k_val){
  paste("cluster ",i,": ",paste(my_tmp[my_tmp$exp==i,]$carbon,collapse = ","),sep="") %>% print()
}

# 2. Data Integration
# Focus on unique pairs (upper triangle) and join with cluster assignments
my_df<-ecor_pair_all[ecor_pair_all$key=="upper",]
my_tmp1<-my_tmp %>% rename(carbon1=carbon,exp1=exp)
my_tmp2<-my_tmp %>% rename(carbon2=carbon,exp2=exp)
my_df<-left_join(my_df,my_tmp1,by="carbon1")
my_df<-left_join(my_df,my_tmp2,by="carbon2")

my_clstrs<-seq(1,k_val)

# 3. Iterative Comparison: Within-cluster vs. Between-cluster Correlations
my_list<-list()
my_p_list<-list()
for(i in 1:length(my_clstrs)){
  my_cls<-my_clstrs[i]
  
  # Select pairs where at least one carbon source belongs to the target cluster
  my_dat<-my_df[(my_df$exp1==my_cls)|(my_df$exp2==my_cls),]
  n_cbn<-my_tmp[my_tmp$exp==my_cls,] %>% nrow()
  
  # Perform analysis only if the cluster contains more than one carbon source
  if(n_cbn>1){
    # Label pairs as either "Within" (the specific cluster number) or "Between"
    my_dat$pair_cluster_exp<-"Between"
    my_dat[my_dat$exp1==my_dat$exp2,]$pair_cluster_exp<-as.character(my_cls)
    
    # Set factor levels for consistent plotting order
    my_dat$pair_cluster_exp<-factor(my_dat$pair_cluster_exp,levels=c(as.character(my_cls), "Between"))
    
    # 4. Visualization: Boxplot with Jitter
    # Comparing evolutionary correlations within the cluster vs. with others
    my_list[[i]]<-ggboxplot(my_dat,
            x="pair_cluster_exp",y="correlation",
            ylab="Interstrain correlation [-]",xlab="",
            add="jitter",add.params = list(alpha=0.5),
            # palette = my_palette,
            legend="")+
      font("y.text",size=18)+
    stat_pwc(method = "wilcox.test",label = "p.adj.signif",
             ref.group = "Between",tip.length = 0,
      p.adjust.method = "BH",hide.ns = TRUE)+
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-0.4, 0.8, by = 0.4), limits = c(-0.4, 1.2))
    
    # 5. Statistical Testing: Wilcoxon Rank Sum Test
    my_res<-my_dat %>%
      wilcox_test(formula = correlation ~ pair_cluster_exp,
      ref.group = "Between",
      p.adjust.method = "BH")
    my_p_list[[i]]<-my_res$p
  }
}

# 6. Global P-value adjustment across all cluster comparisons
p_adjusted_all <- p.adjust(unlist(my_p_list), method = "BH")
print("Adjusted P-values for all clusters:")
print(p_adjusted_all)

# Output individual plots
my_list[[1]]
my_list[[2]]
my_list[[3]]

Sys.time()
```

#### 4.7.2.3 pvclust
```{r}
# ==========================================
# 2. [NEW] Data reshaping and computation for pvclust
# ==========================================
message("Preparing data for pvclust...")

# Create a matrix from the raw data: rows = strain, columns = carbon, values = mu_max_allrep
# Restricted to the target carbon sources (ecor_carbons)
pv_raw_data <- gr_ecor_df %>%
  filter(carbon %in% ecor_carbons) %>%
  select(strain, carbon, mu_max_allrep) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon, values_from = mu_max_allrep) %>%
  column_to_rownames("strain") %>%
  as.matrix()

# Sort column names (carbon source names) to match the ordering of the upstream matrix
pv_raw_data <- pv_raw_data[, sort(colnames(pv_raw_data))]

# [IMPORTANT] Define a custom distance function based on Spearman correlation (1 - r)
# pvclust computes distances between "columns" internally, so cor(x, method="spearman") is used
dist.spearman <- function(x) {
  # Compute Spearman correlation coefficients between columns of x
  cor_matrix <- cor(x, method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
  # Convert to distance (1 - r) and return as a dist object
  return(as.dist(1 - cor_matrix))
}

message("Running bootstrap clustering with pvclust (Spearman correlation-based)...")

# Run pvclust
pv_result <- pvclust(
  data          = pv_raw_data,
  method.hclust = cl_method,
  method.dist   = dist.spearman, # Custom distance function defined above
  nboot         = 1000,
  parallel      = TRUE
)

# ==========================================
# 4. [NEW] Visualization of pvclust results (significant modules)
# ==========================================
# Draw the dendrogram with statistical support values
plot(pv_result, cex = 0.8, main = "Carbon source clustering (with bootstrap validation)")

# Highlight modules significant at the 95% level (AU >= 0.95) with red boxes
# These modules are robust enough to be considered non-random even accounting for variance
pvrect(pv_result, alpha = 0.95, stroke = 2, border = "red")
Sys.time()
```

```{r,fig.height=5.5,fig.width=6.5}
  sum(sapply(unique(ct), function(cluster) {
    sub_dist <- as.matrix(ecor_dist_matrix_allrep)[ct == cluster, ct == cluster, drop = FALSE]
```

#### 4.7.2.5 Interstrain correlation across clusters (k=2) (Fig. 3f)
```{r,fig.width=6,fig.height=3,dpi=300}
# 1. Clustering based on experimental evolutionary distances
# Define the number of theoretical clusters (k)
k_val <- 2

dist_exp<-ecor_dist_matrix_allrep
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method)
cluster_exp    <- cutree(hc_exp, k = k_val)

# Create a mapping table for carbon sources and their assigned clusters
my_tmp<-data.frame(carbon=names(cluster_exp),exp=cluster_exp)
carbon_clust_tbl<-my_tmp


# Print carbon sources belonging to each cluster for inspection
for(i in 1:k_val){
  paste("cluster ",i,": ",paste(my_tmp[my_tmp$exp==i,]$carbon,collapse = ","),sep="") %>% print()
}

# 2. Data Integration
# Focus on unique pairs (upper triangle) and join with cluster assignments
my_df<-ecor_pair_all[ecor_pair_all$key=="upper",]
my_tmp1<-my_tmp %>% rename(carbon1=carbon,exp1=exp)
my_tmp2<-my_tmp %>% rename(carbon2=carbon,exp2=exp)
my_df<-left_join(my_df,my_tmp1,by="carbon1")
my_df<-left_join(my_df,my_tmp2,by="carbon2")

my_clstrs<-seq(1,k_val)

# ==========================================
# 3. Data reshaping: automatically determine cluster numbering
#    based on the count of Upper Glycolysis carbon sources per cluster
# ==========================================
# Count the number of Upper Glycolysis pairs in each cluster
# using the original assignments (exp=1, exp=2, etc.)
cluster_counts <- my_df %>%
  mutate(pair_type_raw = case_when(
    exp1 == 1 & exp2 == 1 ~ "C1",
    exp1 == 2 & exp2 == 2 ~ "C2",
    TRUE                  ~ "Between"
  )) %>%
  # Retain only within-cluster pairs and count Upper Glycolysis occurrences per cluster
  filter(pair_type_raw %in% c("C1", "C2")) %>%
  group_by(pair_type_raw) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(upper_glyco_count = sum(pair_category == "Upper Glycolysis", na.rm = TRUE))

# Identify the original cluster label that contains more Upper Glycolysis pairs
# (in case of a tie, C1 is given priority)
target_raw_c1 <- cluster_counts$pair_type_raw[which.max(cluster_counts$upper_glyco_count)]

# Based on the result above, assign new cluster labels
# (the cluster with more Upper Glycolysis pairs becomes new Cluster 1)
plot_df <- my_df %>%
  mutate(
    pair_type = case_when(
      exp1 == 1 & exp2 == 1 ~ if_else(target_raw_c1 == "C1", "Cluster 1", "Cluster 2"),
      exp1 == 2 & exp2 == 2 ~ if_else(target_raw_c1 == "C2", "Cluster 1", "Cluster 2"),
      TRUE                  ~ "Between"
    )
  ) %>%
  # Fix the order for plotting and testing to "Cluster 1, Cluster 2, Between"
  mutate(pair_type = factor(pair_type, levels = c("Cluster 1", "Cluster 2", "Between")))

# Print which original cluster was assigned as new Cluster 1
print(paste("The cluster with more Upper Glycolysis pairs was set as 'Cluster 1'. Original cluster:", target_raw_c1))


# ==========================================
# 4. Visualization and statistical testing (error-safe version)
# ==========================================
# Embed wilcox.test directly in ggboxplot to reliably avoid mapping errors
p_integrated <- ggboxplot(
  plot_df,
  x = "pair_type", 
  y = "correlation_allrep",
  ylab = "Interstrain correlation [-]", 
  xlab = "",
  add = "jitter", 
  add.params = list(alpha = 0.4, size = 1.5), 
  theme = theme_pubr(base_size = 20)
) +
  font("xy.text", size = 22) +
  font("ylab", size = 22) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-0.4, 1.0, by = 0.4), limits = c(-0.4, 1.3)) +
  stat_pwc(
    method = "wilcox.test",
    ref.group = "Between",      
    p.adjust.method = "BH",     
    label = "p.adj.signif",     
    tip.length = 0,
    bracket.nudge.y = 0.05, 
    hide.ns = TRUE              
  )

print(p_integrated)


# ==========================================
# 5. (For verification) Detailed statistical results in text form
# ==========================================
stat_test <- plot_df %>%
  wilcox_test(
    formula = correlation_allrep ~ pair_type,
    ref.group = "Between",
    p.adjust.method = "BH"
  )
print("Detailed adjusted p-values compared to Between:")
print(stat_test)

# Extract a mapping table of carbon sources to new cluster labels (Cluster 1 / 2)
# from the finalized plot_df of the ECOR analysis above
# This carries forward the cluster definitions corrected by Upper Glycolysis count
cbnclust_tbl_ecorbased_allrep <- plot_df %>%
  # Build the mapping from both carbon1 and carbon2 so each carbon source gets its own row
  select(carbon = carbon1, pair_type) %>%
  bind_rows(select(plot_df, carbon = carbon2, pair_type)) %>%
  filter(pair_type %in% c("Cluster 1", "Cluster 2")) %>%
  distinct(carbon, pair_type)


Sys.time()
```

```{r,fig.width=2.5,fig.height=2,dpi=300}
my_df<-left_join(my_df,my_tmp2,by="carbon2")

    my_list[[i]]<-ggboxplot(my_dat,

    stat_pwc(method = "wilcox.test",label = "p.adj.signif",
             ref.group = "Between",tip.length = 0,
      p.adjust.method = "BH",hide.ns = TRUE)+
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-0.4, 0.8, by = 0.4), limits = c(-0.4, 1.2))
    
    # 5. Statistical Testing: Wilcoxon Rank Sum Test
    my_res<-my_dat %>%
      wilcox_test(formula = correlation_allrep ~ pair_cluster_exp,
      ref.group = "Between",
      p.adjust.method = "BH")
    my_p_list[[i]]<-my_res$p
  }
}

# 6. Global P-value adjustment across all cluster comparisons
p_adjusted_all <- p.adjust(unlist(my_p_list), method = "BH")
print("Adjusted P-values for all clusters:")
print(p_adjusted_all)

# Output individual plots
my_list[[1]]
my_list[[2]]
my_list[[3]]
```

## 4.8 Comparison with flux-based distances
### 4.8.1 Two Reps
#### 4.8.1.1 Entanglement score with permutation test
```{r, fig.width=1.5,fig.height=3.5,dpi=300}
# Flux-based distance and Phenotypic distance from Growth rates
dist_exp<-as.dist(1 - ecor_matrix)
my_ins<-rownames(ecor_matrix)
dist_theory<-mean_carbon_dist_matrix[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------ cosine distance


# Hierarchical clustering using Ward's D2 method
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = cl_method)
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method)

dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# 2. Untangle: Optimize the layout of the two dendrograms to minimize crossings
# Maintaining the topology while rotating branches for better visualization
dl <- dendlist(dend_theory, dend_exp)
dl_untangled <- dendextend::untangle(dl, method = "step2side")

dend_p <- dl_untangled[[1]] # Optimized Flux-based dendrogram
dend_t <- dl_untangled[[2]] # Optimized Growth-based dendrogram


# 3. Create color vectors based on labels
# Retrieve current label order from the left (FBA) dendrogram
current_labels_p <- labels(dend_p)
# Map categories and colors to the current labels
groups_p <- carbon_labels_ordered_cos$Category[match(current_labels_p, carbon_labels_ordered_cos$label)]
col_vector_p <- carbon_labels_ordered_cos$Category_col[match(current_labels_p, carbon_labels_ordered_cos$label)]

# 4. Set label colors
dend_p <- dend_p %>% set("labels_colors", col_vector_p)

# Match Growth-based tree labels with the FBA-based tree's color vector
dend_t <- dend_t %>% 
  set("labels_colors", col_vector_p[match(labels(dend_t), current_labels_p)])

# 5. Draw Tanglegram
# Visualizing the structural similarity between metabolic theory and growth phenotype
tanglegram(dend_p, dend_t,
           common_subtrees_color_lines = FALSE, 
           highlight_distinct_edges = FALSE,
           highlight_branches_lwd = FALSE,
           color_lines = col_vector_p, 
           main_left = "Flux",
           main_right = "Growth",
           lab.cex = 1,
           lwd=2,
           columns_width = c(4, 1.5, 4),
           margin_inner = 3.5,
           margin_outer = 0.5,
           axes = FALSE)


# 6. Permutation Test for Entanglement Score
# Lower entanglement indicates higher structural similarity
actual_ent <- entanglement(dl_untangled) # Entanglement score after untangling

print(Sys.time())
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- if_else(iteration_scale=="large",1000,10)
perm_ent <- numeric(n_perm)

# Fixed theory-based labels
labels_theory <- labels(dend_p)

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # Copy the experimental dendrogram and shuffle labels
  shuffled_dend <- dend_t
  labels(shuffled_dend) <- sample(labels_theory)
  
  # Calculate entanglement for the shuffled pair after untangling
  perm_dends <- dendlist(dend_p, shuffled_dend) %>% 
    dendextend::untangle(method = "step2side")
  perm_ent[i] <- entanglement(perm_dends)
  
  # Progress monitoring
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# 7. Calculate P-value
# P-value = Probability that random entanglement is lower than the observed value
p_val_ent <- sum(perm_ent <= actual_ent) / n_perm

# 8. Visualization of results
hist(perm_ent, main="Permutation Test for Entanglement", 
     xlab="Entanglement Score", xlim=c(0, 1))
abline(v = actual_ent, col = "red", lwd = 2)
cat(sprintf("Actual Entanglement: %.3f\nP-value: %.4f\n", actual_ent, p_val_ent))

Sys.time()
```
#### 4.8.1.2 Cophenetic correlation with permutation test
```{r}
# 1. Prepare distance matrices and initial dendrograms
dist_exp<-as.dist(1 - ecor_matrix)
my_ins<-rownames(ecor_matrix)

# Flux-based metabolic distance
dist_theory<-mean_carbon_dist_matrix[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------ cosine distance

# Hierarchical clustering
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = cl_method)
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method)

dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# Calculate observed Cophenetic correlation (Spearman)
# This measures how well the tree structure reflects the original distance matrix
actual_cor <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_exp, method = "spearman")

# --- Permutation Test for Cophenetic Correlation ---
print(Sys.time())
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- 1000
perm_results <- data.frame(cor = numeric(n_perm))

# Get original labels (strain names) from the experimental distance matrix
exp_labels <- rownames(as.matrix(dist_exp))

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # 1. Shuffle labels while keeping the underlying matrix structure intact
  dist_shuffled <- dist_exp
  shuffled_labels <- sample(exp_labels)
  
  # Convert to matrix to reassign shuffled names
  temp_mat <- as.matrix(dist_shuffled)
  rownames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  colnames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  
  # 2. Reconstruct dendrogram from the shuffled distance matrix
  hc_shuffled <- hclust(as.dist(temp_mat), method = cl_method)
  dend_shuffled <- as.dendrogram(hc_shuffled)
  
  # 3. Calculate and store the correlation for this permutation
  perm_results$cor[i] <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_shuffled, method = "spearman")
  
  # Progress monitoring
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# --- Statistical Evaluation ---
# P-value: Proportion of permutations where correlation is equal to or greater than observed
p_val_cor <- sum(perm_results$cor >= actual_cor) / n_perm

cat("【Analysis Results】\n")
cat(sprintf("Cophenetic Cor (Spearman): %.3f (p = %.4f)\n", actual_cor, p_val_cor))

# --- Visualization: Cophenetic Correlation Bubble Plot ---
# 1. Prepare data and count overlapping points (ties) for bubble sizing
df_coph <- data.frame(
  Theory = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_theory)),
  Experiment = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_exp))
) %>%
  group_by(Theory, Experiment) %>%
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = 'drop') # 各座標の重複数をカウント

my_txt<-paste("R=",sprintf("%.3f",actual_cor),sep="")

# 2. Plotting with ggscatter
# Bubble size and color intensity are log2-scaled to visualize the density of distance pairs
ggscatter(df_coph, x = "Theory", y = "Experiment",
          size = "count",           # Map count to dot size
          fill = "count",           # Map count to fill color
          color = "black",          # Fix border color to black
          shape = 21,               # Use filled circles with borders
          alpha= 0.8,
          xlab = "Cophenetic distance (Theory)",
          ylab = "Cophenetic distance (Experiment)",
          title = "Cophenetic Correlation (Log-scaled Bubble Size)",
          ylim=c(0,3)) +
  # Apply log2 transformation to size and color to handle the wide range of counts
  scale_size_continuous(trans = "log2", range = c(1, 12), name = "Count (log2)") +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Greys", trans = "log2", direction = 1, name = "Count (log2)")+
  annotate("text", x = 0.2, y = 2.7, label = my_txt,)

Sys.time()
```
#### 4.8.1.3 Baker's Gamma Index for Topological Similarity
```{r}
# 1. Prepare distance matrices and initial dendrograms for ECOR
dist_exp<-as.dist(1 - ecor_matrix)
my_ins<-rownames(ecor_matrix)
dist_theory<-mean_carbon_dist_matrix[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------ cosine distance

# Hierarchical clustering using Ward's D2 method
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = cl_method)
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method)

dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# 2. Calculate Observed Baker's Gamma Index
# Baker's Gamma measures the rank correlation between the stages at which 
# pairs of objects combine in each dendrogram.
actual_gamma <- cor_bakers_gamma(dend_theory, dend_exp)
cat(sprintf("Actual Baker's Gammer: %.3f\n", actual_gamma))

# 3. Permutation Test (1,000 iterations)
# Building a null distribution by randomly shuffling labels to assess significance
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- 1000
perm_gammas <- numeric(n_perm)

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # Randomly shuffle the labels of one dendrogram while preserving its structure
  perm_dend <- sample.dendrogram(dend_theory, replace = FALSE)
  # Compute Baker's Gamma for the shuffled pair
  perm_gammas[i] <- cor_bakers_gamma(perm_dend, dend_exp)
}

# 4. Calculate P-value
# P-value: The probability of obtaining a Gamma value as high as observed by chance
p_value <- sum(perm_gammas >= actual_gamma) / n_perm

print(Sys.time())
cat(sprintf("P-value: %.4f\n", p_value))
```
#### 4.8.1.4 Entanglement score with permutation test (without upper glycolysis carbons)
```{r, fig.width=1.8,fig.height=2.5,dpi=300}
# Flux-based distance and Phenotypic distance from Growth rates
my_mat<-ecor_matrix
my_ins<-carbon_names %>%
  filter(Abb %in% rownames(my_mat)) %>%
  filter(Category %nin% "Upper Glycolysis") %>%
  pull(Abb) %>%
  sort()
dist_exp<-as.dist(1 - my_mat[my_ins,my_ins])
dist_theory<-mean_carbon_dist_matrix[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------ cosine distance


# Hierarchical clustering using Ward's D2 method
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = cl_method)
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method)

dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# 2. Untangle: Optimize the layout of the two dendrograms to minimize crossings
# Maintaining the topology while rotating branches for better visualization
dl <- dendlist(dend_theory, dend_exp)
dl_untangled <- dendextend::untangle(dl, method = "step2side")

dend_p <- dl_untangled[[1]] # Optimized Flux-based dendrogram
dend_t <- dl_untangled[[2]] # Optimized Growth-based dendrogram


# 3. Create color vectors based on labels
# Retrieve current label order from the left (FBA) dendrogram
current_labels_p <- labels(dend_p)
# Map categories and colors to the current labels
groups_p <- carbon_labels_ordered_cos$Category[match(current_labels_p, carbon_labels_ordered_cos$label)]
col_vector_p <- carbon_labels_ordered_cos$Category_col[match(current_labels_p, carbon_labels_ordered_cos$label)]

# 4. Set label colors
dend_p <- dend_p %>% set("labels_colors", col_vector_p)

# Match Growth-based tree labels with the FBA-based tree's color vector
dend_t <- dend_t %>% 
  set("labels_colors", col_vector_p[match(labels(dend_t), current_labels_p)])

# 5. Draw Tanglegram
# Visualizing the structural similarity between metabolic theory and growth phenotype
tanglegram(dend_p, dend_t,
           common_subtrees_color_lines = FALSE, 
           highlight_distinct_edges = FALSE,
           highlight_branches_lwd = FALSE,
           color_lines = col_vector_p, 
           main_left = "Flux",
           main_right = "Growth",
           lab.cex = 1,
           lwd=2,
           columns_width = c(4, 1.5, 4),
           margin_inner = 3.5,
           margin_outer = 0.5,
           axes = FALSE)


# 6. Permutation Test for Entanglement Score
# Lower entanglement indicates higher structural similarity
actual_ent <- entanglement(dl_untangled) # Entanglement score after untangling

print(Sys.time())
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- if_else(iteration_scale=="large",1000,10)
perm_ent <- numeric(n_perm)

# Fixed theory-based labels
labels_theory <- labels(dend_p)

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # Copy the experimental dendrogram and shuffle labels
  shuffled_dend <- dend_t
  labels(shuffled_dend) <- sample(labels_theory)
  
  # Calculate entanglement for the shuffled pair after untangling
  perm_dends <- dendlist(dend_p, shuffled_dend) %>% 
    dendextend::untangle(method = "step2side")
  perm_ent[i] <- entanglement(perm_dends)
  
  # Progress monitoring
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# 7. Calculate P-value
# P-value = Probability that random entanglement is lower than the observed value
p_val_ent <- sum(perm_ent <= actual_ent) / n_perm

# 8. Visualization of results
hist(perm_ent, main="Permutation Test for Entanglement", 
     xlab="Entanglement Score", xlim=c(0, 1))
abline(v = actual_ent, col = "red", lwd = 2)
cat(sprintf("Actual Entanglement: %.3f\nP-value: %.4f\n", actual_ent, p_val_ent))

Sys.time()
```

#### 4.8.2.5 Cophenetic correlation with permutation test (without upper glycolysis carbons)
```{r}
# Flux-based distance and Phenotypic distance from Growth rates
my_mat<-ecor_matrix_allrep
my_ins<-carbon_names %>%
  filter(Abb %in% rownames(my_mat)) %>%
  filter(Category %nin% "Upper Glycolysis") %>%
  pull(Abb) %>%
  sort()
dist_exp<-as.dist(1 - my_mat[my_ins,my_ins])
dist_theory<-mean_carbon_dist_matrix[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------ cosine distance

# Hierarchical clustering
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = cl_method)
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method)

dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# Calculate observed Cophenetic correlation (Spearman)
# This measures how well the tree structure reflects the original distance matrix
actual_cor <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_exp, method = "spearman")

# --- Permutation Test for Cophenetic Correlation ---
print(Sys.time())
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- 1000
perm_results <- data.frame(cor = numeric(n_perm))

# Get original labels (strain names) from the experimental distance matrix
exp_labels <- rownames(as.matrix(dist_exp))

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # 1. Shuffle labels while keeping the underlying matrix structure intact
  dist_shuffled <- dist_exp
  shuffled_labels <- sample(exp_labels)
  
  # Convert to matrix to reassign shuffled names
  temp_mat <- as.matrix(dist_shuffled)
  rownames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  colnames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  
  # 2. Reconstruct dendrogram from the shuffled distance matrix
  hc_shuffled <- hclust(as.dist(temp_mat), method = cl_method)
  dend_shuffled <- as.dendrogram(hc_shuffled)
  
  # 3. Calculate and store the correlation for this permutation
  perm_results$cor[i] <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_shuffled, method = "spearman")
  
  # Progress monitoring
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# --- Statistical Evaluation ---
# P-value: Proportion of permutations where correlation is equal to or greater than observed
p_val_cor <- sum(perm_results$cor >= actual_cor) / n_perm

cat("【Analysis Results】\n")
cat(sprintf("Cophenetic Cor (Spearman): %.3f (p = %.4f)\n", actual_cor, p_val_cor))

# --- Visualization: Cophenetic Correlation Bubble Plot ---

  Theory = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_theory)),

) %>%

# 2. Plotting with ggscatter
```

## 4.9 Using Nonzero-growth strains only (strain-level filtration Four reps)
### 4.9.1 filtration and calc interstrain correlation
```{r,fig.height=2.5,fig.width=9,dpi=300}
# Count of zero elements
gr_ecor_df %>% 
  filter(mu_max_allrep == 0) %>% 
  nrow()

# Count of non-zero elements
gr_ecor_df %>% 
  filter(mu_max_allrep != 0) %>% 
  nrow()

# Number of strains
gr_ecor_df$strain %>% unique() %>% length()

# Strains remaining after removing any strain that contains a zero value
my_strains <- gr_ecor_df %>%
  select(strain, carbon, mu_max_allrep) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon, values_from = mu_max_allrep)%>% 
  # Remove rows containing any zero (applied to all numeric columns)
  filter(if_all(where(is.numeric), ~ .x != 0)) %>%
  pull(strain)
print(length(my_strains))

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Summarize growth patterns (presence/absence of zeros) per carbon source pair
# and compute correlations using only non-zero values
# ---------------------------------------------------------

# Copy the base data frame
ecor_pair_all_filt <- carbon_dist_integrated_long %>%
  filter(carbon1 %in% ecor_carbons & carbon2 %in% ecor_carbons)

# Initialize result columns
ecor_pair_all_filt$n_nonzero_nonzero <- NA_integer_
ecor_pair_all_filt$n_zero_nonzero    <- NA_integer_
ecor_pair_all_filt$n_zero_zero       <- NA_integer_
ecor_pair_all_filt$n_total           <- NA_integer_
ecor_pair_all_filt$correlation_nonzero_only <- NA_real_

# Threshold for defining no-growth (zero growth defined as 0)
zero_threshold <- 0 

for (i in 1:nrow(ecor_pair_all_filt)) {
  my_carbon_1 <- ecor_pair_all_filt$carbon1[i]
  my_carbon_2 <- ecor_pair_all_filt$carbon2[i]
  
  # Extract data for carbon sources 1 and 2
  my_df1 <- gr_ecor_df %>% 
    filter(carbon == my_carbon_1) %>% 
    select(strain, mu_max_1 = mu_max_allrep)
  
  my_df2 <- gr_ecor_df %>% 
    filter(carbon == my_carbon_2) %>% 
    select(strain, mu_max_2 = mu_max_allrep)
  
  # Join by strain
  my_df <- inner_join(my_df1, my_df2, by = "strain") %>% 
    filter(!is.na(mu_max_1) & !is.na(mu_max_2)) 
  
  # 1. Count strains by zero/non-zero pattern
  is_nz1 <- my_df$mu_max_1 > zero_threshold
  is_nz2 <- my_df$mu_max_2 > zero_threshold
  
  nn_count <- sum(is_nz1 & is_nz2)                        # Nonzero - Nonzero
  zn_count <- sum((is_nz1 & !is_nz2) | (!is_nz1 & is_nz2)) # Zero - Nonzero 
  zz_count <- sum(!is_nz1 & !is_nz2)                       # Zero - Zero
  
  ecor_pair_all_filt$n_nonzero_nonzero[i] <- nn_count
  ecor_pair_all_filt$n_zero_nonzero[i]    <- zn_count
  ecor_pair_all_filt$n_zero_zero[i]       <- zz_count
  ecor_pair_all_filt$n_total[i]           <- nrow(my_df)
  
  # 2.A Recompute Spearman correlation using only Nonzero-Nonzero strains
  #     (strain-level removal: exclude strains with zero growth on any carbon source)
  df_nonzero <- my_df %>%
    filter(strain %in% my_strains) %>% # Remove strains that have zero growth on any carbon source
    filter(mu_max_1 > zero_threshold & mu_max_2 > zero_threshold)
  
  # Correlation requires at least 3 data points
  if (nrow(df_nonzero) >= 3) {
    # Also verify that variance is non-zero (i.e., values are not all identical)
    if (var(df_nonzero$mu_max_1) > 0 && var(df_nonzero$mu_max_2) > 0) {
      res_nz <- cor_test(df_nonzero, vars = "mu_max_1", vars2 = "mu_max_2", method = "spearman")
      ecor_pair_all_filt$correlation_nonzero_only[i] <- res_nz$cor
    }
  }
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Inspect results
# ---------------------------------------------------------
head(ecor_pair_all_filt)

Sys.time()
```

### 4.9.4 Comparison with dendrogram containing zero-growth data
#### 4.9.4.1 Entanglement score with permutation test (Fig. S7f)
```{r, fig.width=1.5,fig.height=3.5,dpi=300}

# Distance matrix built from non-zero data
dist_exp<-as.dist(1 - ecor_matrix_filt)
my_ins<-rownames(ecor_matrix_filt)

# Distance matrix built from data including zeros
dist_theory<-as.dist(1 - ecor_matrix_allrep[my_ins,my_ins])


# Hierarchical clustering using Ward's D2 method
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = cl_method) # Including zeros
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method) # Non-zero only

dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# 2. Untangle: Optimize the layout of the two dendrograms to minimize crossings
# Maintaining the topology while rotating branches for better visualization
dl <- dendlist(dend_theory, dend_exp)
dl_untangled <- dendextend::untangle(dl, method = "step2side")

dend_p <- dl_untangled[[1]] # Optimized (including zeros)
dend_t <- dl_untangled[[2]] # Optimized (non-zero only)


# 3. Create color vectors based on labels
# Retrieve current label order from the left (unnormalized) dendrogram
current_labels_p <- labels(dend_p)
# Map categories and colors to the current labels
groups_p <- carbon_labels_ordered_cos$Category[match(current_labels_p, carbon_labels_ordered_cos$label)]
col_vector_p <- carbon_labels_ordered_cos$Category_col[match(current_labels_p, carbon_labels_ordered_cos$label)]

# 4. Set label colors
dend_p <- dend_p %>% set("labels_colors", col_vector_p)

# Match Growth-based tree labels with the FBA-based tree's color vector
dend_t <- dend_t %>% 
  set("labels_colors", col_vector_p[match(labels(dend_t), current_labels_p)])

# 5. Draw Tanglegram
# Visualizing the structural similarity between metabolic theory and growth phenotype
tanglegram(dend_p, dend_t,
           common_subtrees_color_lines = FALSE, 
           highlight_distinct_edges = FALSE,
           highlight_branches_lwd = FALSE,
           color_lines = col_vector_p, 
           main_left = "Original",
           main_right = "Non-zero",
           lab.cex = 1,
           lwd=2,
           columns_width = c(4, 1.5, 4),
           margin_inner = 3.5,
           margin_outer = 0.5,
           axes = FALSE)


# 6. Permutation Test for Entanglement Score
# Lower entanglement indicates higher structural similarity
actual_ent <- entanglement(dl_untangled) # Entanglement score after untangling

print(Sys.time())
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- if_else(iteration_scale=="large",1000,10)
perm_ent <- numeric(n_perm)

# Fixed theory-based labels
labels_theory <- labels(dend_p)

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # Copy the experimental dendrogram and shuffle labels
  shuffled_dend <- dend_t
  labels(shuffled_dend) <- sample(labels_theory)
  
  # Calculate entanglement for the shuffled pair after untangling
  perm_dends <- dendlist(dend_p, shuffled_dend) %>% 
    dendextend::untangle(method = "step2side")
  perm_ent[i] <- entanglement(perm_dends)
  
  # Progress monitoring
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# 7. Calculate P-value
# P-value = Probability that random entanglement is lower than the observed value
p_val_ent <- sum(perm_ent <= actual_ent) / n_perm

# 8. Visualization of results
hist(perm_ent, main="Permutation Test for Entanglement", 
     xlab="Entanglement Score", xlim=c(0, 1))
abline(v = actual_ent, col = "red", lwd = 2)
cat(sprintf("Actual Entanglement: %.3f\nP-value: %.4f\n", actual_ent, p_val_ent))

Sys.time()
```

### 4.9.6 Elbow (Fig. S7g)

```{r, fig.height=4,fig.width=5}
dist_exp<-as.dist(1 - ecor_matrix_filt)

  ct <- cutree(hc_result, k = k)
  sum(sapply(unique(ct), function(cluster) {
    sub_dist <- as.matrix(dist_exp)[ct == cluster, ct == cluster, drop = FALSE]
    sum(sub_dist^2) / (2 * nrow(sub_dist))
  }))
})
```
