```{r,fig.width=4,fig.height=3,dpi=300}
  mutate(
    pair_type = case_when(
      cluster1_new == "Cluster 1" & cluster2_new == "Cluster 1" ~ "Cluster 1", # Both within Cluster 1
      cluster1_new == "Cluster 2" & cluster2_new == "Cluster 2" ~ "Cluster 2", # Both within Cluster 2
      TRUE                                                      ~ "Between"   # All other pairs (between clusters, etc.)
    )
  ) %>%
  # Fix the order for plotting and testing to "Cluster 1, Cluster 2, Between"
  mutate(pair_type = factor(pair_type, levels = c("Cluster 1", "Cluster 2", "Between")))


# ==========================================
# 3. Visualization and statistical testing
# ==========================================
# Draw a boxplot using the correlation coefficient (correlation_nonzero_only)
p_ecor_integrated <- ggboxplot(
  ecor_plot_df,
  x = "pair_type", 
  y = "correlation_nonzero_only",
  ylab = "Interstrain correlation (Nonzero-growth) [-]", 
  xlab = "",
  add = "jitter", 
  add.params = list(alpha = 0.4, size = 1.5), 
  theme = theme_pubr(base_size = 20)
) +
  font("xy.text", size = 18) +
  font("ylab", size = 18) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-0.4, 1.0, by = 0.4), limits = c(-0.5, 1.3)) +
  # Automatically add Wilcoxon tests against "Between" as the reference group
  stat_pwc(
    method = "wilcox.test",
    ref.group = "Between",      
    p.adjust.method = "BH",     
    label = "p.adj.signif",     
    tip.length = 0,
    bracket.nudge.y = 0.05, 
    hide.ns = TRUE              
  )

print(p_ecor_integrated)


# ==========================================
# 4. Print detailed statistical results to the console (for verification)
# ==========================================
ecor_stat_test <- ecor_plot_df %>%
  wilcox_test(
    formula = correlation_nonzero_only ~ pair_type,
    ref.group = "Between",
    p.adjust.method = "BH"
  )
print("Detailed adjusted p-values for comparisons against 'Between' in the ECOR dataset:")
print(ecor_stat_test)

Sys.time()
```

## 4.10  Using Nonzero-growth samples only (sample-level filtration Four reps)
### 4.10.1 filtration and calc interstrain correlation
```{r,fig.height=2.5,fig.width=9,dpi=300}

ecor_pair_all_filt_smpl <- carbon_dist_integrated_long %>%
  filter(carbon1 %in% ecor_carbons & carbon2 %in% ecor_carbons)

# 結果格納用の列を初期化
ecor_pair_all_filt_smpl$n_nonzero_nonzero <- NA_integer_
ecor_pair_all_filt_smpl$n_zero_nonzero    <- NA_integer_
ecor_pair_all_filt_smpl$n_zero_zero       <- NA_integer_
ecor_pair_all_filt_smpl$n_total           <- NA_integer_
ecor_pair_all_filt_smpl$correlation_nonzero_only <- NA_real_


zero_threshold <- 0 

for (i in 1:nrow(ecor_pair_all_filt_smpl)) {
  my_carbon_1 <- ecor_pair_all_filt_smpl$carbon1[i]
  my_carbon_2 <- ecor_pair_all_filt_smpl$carbon2[i]
  

  my_df1 <- gr_ecor_df %>% 
    filter(carbon == my_carbon_1) %>% 
    select(strain, mu_max_1 = mu_max_allrep)
  
  my_df2 <- gr_ecor_df %>% 
    filter(carbon == my_carbon_2) %>% 
    select(strain, mu_max_2 = mu_max_allrep)
  

  my_df <- inner_join(my_df1, my_df2, by = "strain") %>% 
    filter(!is.na(mu_max_1) & !is.na(mu_max_2)) # NAを除外
  

  is_nz1 <- my_df$mu_max_1 > zero_threshold
  is_nz2 <- my_df$mu_max_2 > zero_threshold
  
  nn_count <- sum(is_nz1 & is_nz2)                        # Nonzero - Nonzero
  zn_count <- sum((is_nz1 & !is_nz2) | (!is_nz1 & is_nz2)) # Zero - Nonzero 
  zz_count <- sum(!is_nz1 & !is_nz2)                       # Zero - Zero
  
  ecor_pair_all_filt_smpl$n_nonzero_nonzero[i] <- nn_count
  ecor_pair_all_filt_smpl$n_zero_nonzero[i]    <- zn_count
  ecor_pair_all_filt_smpl$n_zero_zero[i]       <- zz_count
  ecor_pair_all_filt_smpl$n_total[i]           <- nrow(my_df)
  
  df_nonzero <- my_df %>%
    filter(mu_max_1 > zero_threshold & mu_max_2 > zero_threshold)
  
  if (nrow(df_nonzero) >= 3) {
    if (var(df_nonzero$mu_max_1) > 0 && var(df_nonzero$mu_max_2) > 0) {
      res_nz <- cor_test(df_nonzero, vars = "mu_max_1", vars2 = "mu_max_2", method = "spearman")
      ecor_pair_all_filt_smpl$correlation_nonzero_only[i] <- res_nz$cor
    }
  }
}

head(ecor_pair_all_filt_smpl)

Sys.time()
```

### 4.10.4 Comparison with dendrogram containing zero-growth data
#### 4.10.4.1 Entanglement score with permutation test (Fig. S7c)
```{r, fig.width=1.5,fig.height=3.5,dpi=300}

dist_exp<-as.dist(1 - ecor_matrix_filt_smpl)
my_ins<-rownames(ecor_matrix_filt_smpl)
dist_theory<-as.dist(1 - ecor_matrix_allrep[my_ins,my_ins])


# Hierarchical clustering using Ward's D2 method
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = cl_method) 
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method) 

dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# 2. Untangle: Optimize the layout of the two dendrograms to minimize crossings
# Maintaining the topology while rotating branches for better visualization
dl <- dendlist(dend_theory, dend_exp)
dl_untangled <- dendextend::untangle(dl, method = "step2side")

dend_p <- dl_untangled[[1]] 
dend_t <- dl_untangled[[2]] 


# 3. Create color vectors based on labels
# Retrieve current label order from the left (unnormalized) dendrogram
current_labels_p <- labels(dend_p)
# Map categories and colors to the current labels
groups_p <- carbon_labels_ordered_cos$Category[match(current_labels_p, carbon_labels_ordered_cos$label)]
col_vector_p <- carbon_labels_ordered_cos$Category_col[match(current_labels_p, carbon_labels_ordered_cos$label)]

# 4. Set label colors
dend_p <- dend_p %>% set("labels_colors", col_vector_p)

# Match Growth-based tree labels with the FBA-based tree's color vector
dend_t <- dend_t %>% 
  set("labels_colors", col_vector_p[match(labels(dend_t), current_labels_p)])

# 5. Draw Tanglegram
# Visualizing the structural similarity between metabolic theory and growth phenotype
tanglegram(dend_p, dend_t,
           common_subtrees_color_lines = FALSE, 
           highlight_distinct_edges = FALSE,
           highlight_branches_lwd = FALSE,
           color_lines = col_vector_p, 
           main_left = "Original",
           main_right = "Non-zero",
           lab.cex = 1,
           lwd=2,
           columns_width = c(4, 1.5, 4),
           margin_inner = 3.5,
           margin_outer = 0.5,
           axes = FALSE)


# 6. Permutation Test for Entanglement Score
# Lower entanglement indicates higher structural similarity
actual_ent <- entanglement(dl_untangled) # Entanglement score after untangling

print(Sys.time())
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- if_else(iteration_scale=="large",1000,10)
perm_ent <- numeric(n_perm)

# Fixed theory-based labels
labels_theory <- labels(dend_p)

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # Copy the experimental dendrogram and shuffle labels
  shuffled_dend <- dend_t
  labels(shuffled_dend) <- sample(labels_theory)
  
  # Calculate entanglement for the shuffled pair after untangling
  perm_dends <- dendlist(dend_p, shuffled_dend) %>% 
    dendextend::untangle(method = "step2side")
  perm_ent[i] <- entanglement(perm_dends)
  
  # Progress monitoring
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# 7. Calculate P-value
# P-value = Probability that random entanglement is lower than the observed value
p_val_ent <- sum(perm_ent <= actual_ent) / n_perm

# 8. Visualization of results
hist(perm_ent, main="Permutation Test for Entanglement", 
     xlab="Entanglement Score", xlim=c(0, 1))
abline(v = actual_ent, col = "red", lwd = 2)
cat(sprintf("Actual Entanglement: %.3f\nP-value: %.4f\n", actual_ent, p_val_ent))

Sys.time()
```
#### 4.10.4.2  Cophenetic correlation with permutation test (Fig. S7c)
```{r}

dist_exp<-as.dist(1 - ecor_matrix_filt_smpl)
my_ins<-rownames(ecor_matrix_filt_smpl)

dist_theory<-as.dist(1 - ecor_matrix_allrep[my_ins,my_ins])

# Hierarchical clustering
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = cl_method)
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method) 

dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# Calculate observed Cophenetic correlation (Spearman)
# This measures how well the tree structure reflects the original distance matrix
actual_cor <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_exp, method = "spearman")

# --- Permutation Test for Cophenetic Correlation ---
print(Sys.time())
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- 1000
perm_results <- data.frame(cor = numeric(n_perm))

# Get original labels (strain names) from the experimental distance matrix
exp_labels <- rownames(as.matrix(dist_exp))

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # 1. Shuffle labels while keeping the underlying matrix structure intact
  dist_shuffled <- dist_exp
  shuffled_labels <- sample(exp_labels)
  
  # Convert to matrix to reassign shuffled names
  temp_mat <- as.matrix(dist_shuffled)
  rownames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  colnames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  
  # 2. Reconstruct dendrogram from the shuffled distance matrix
  hc_shuffled <- hclust(as.dist(temp_mat), method = cl_method)
  dend_shuffled <- as.dendrogram(hc_shuffled)
  
  # 3. Calculate and store the correlation for this permutation
  perm_results$cor[i] <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_shuffled, method = "spearman")
  
  # Progress monitoring
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# --- Statistical Evaluation ---
# P-value: Proportion of permutations where correlation is equal to or greater than observed
p_val_cor <- sum(perm_results$cor >= actual_cor) / n_perm

cat("【Analysis Results】\n")
cat(sprintf("Cophenetic Cor (Spearman): %.3f (p = %.4f)\n", actual_cor, p_val_cor))

# --- Visualization: Cophenetic Correlation Bubble Plot ---
# 1. Prepare data and count overlapping points (ties) for bubble sizing
df_coph <- data.frame(
  Theory = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_theory)),
  Experiment = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_exp))
) %>%
  group_by(Theory, Experiment) %>%
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = 'drop') # 各座標の重複数をカウント

my_txt<-paste("R=",sprintf("%.3f",actual_cor),sep="")

# 2. Plotting with ggscatter
# Bubble size and color intensity are log2-scaled to visualize the density of distance pairs
ggscatter(df_coph, x = "Theory", y = "Experiment",
          size = "count",           # Map count to dot size
          fill = "count",           # Map count to fill color
          color = "black",          # Fix border color to black
          shape = 21,               # Use filled circles with borders
          alpha= 0.8,
          xlab = "Cophenetic distance (Theory)",
          ylab = "Cophenetic distance (Experiment)",
          title = "Cophenetic Correlation (Log-scaled Bubble Size)",
          ylim=c(0,3)) +
  # Apply log2 transformation to size and color to handle the wide range of counts
  scale_size_continuous(trans = "log2", range = c(1, 12), name = "Count (log2)") +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Greys", trans = "log2", direction = 1, name = "Count (log2)")+
  annotate("text", x = 1, y = 2.7, label = my_txt,)

Sys.time()
```

## 4.11 Relationship between Preculture OD and growth rate
### 4.11.1 Two Reps
```{r,fig.height=10,fig.width=10,dpi=300}
my_dat<-paste(getwd(),"Preculture","Output","preculod_ecor.csv",sep="/") %>%
  read_csv() %>%
  select(Strain,Abb,PreculOD)
colnames(my_dat)<-qw(strain,carbon,precul_od)
my_df<-left_join(gr_ecor_df,my_dat,by=c("strain","carbon"))
# Two Reps
p<-ggscatter(my_df,x="precul_od",y="mu_max",color="carbon",alpha=0.2,legend="",
             title="Two reps",
          cor.coef = T,cor.coeff.args = list(method="spearman"))
facet(p,facet.by="carbon")

cor_results <- my_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(precul_od) & !is.na(mu_max)) %>% 
  group_by(carbon) %>%
  summarise(
    res = list(if(n() >= 3) cor.test(precul_od, mu_max, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE) else NULL)
  ) %>%
  filter(!map_lgl(res, is.null)) %>% 
  mutate(
    rho = map_dbl(res, ~ .x$estimate),
    p_value = map_dbl(res, ~ .x$p.value)
  ) %>%
  select(-res)

cor_results <- cor_results %>%
  mutate(p_adj = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH"))

significant_results <- cor_results %>%
  filter(p_adj < 0.05) %>%
  arrange(p_adj)

if (nrow(significant_results) == 0) {
  message("No carbons with significant correlations were found after BH correction for multiple testing.")
} else {
  print(significant_results)
}

wide_mu <- my_df %>%
  dplyr::select(strain, carbon, mu_max) %>%
  filter(!is.na(mu_max)) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon, values_from = mu_max)

wide_od <- my_df %>%
  dplyr::select(strain, carbon, precul_od) %>%
  filter(!is.na(precul_od)) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon, values_from = precul_od)

common_strains <- intersect(wide_mu$strain, wide_od$strain)

mat_mu <- wide_mu %>% 
  filter(strain %in% common_strains) %>% 
  arrange(strain) %>% 
  dplyr::select(-strain) %>% 
  as.matrix()

mat_od <- wide_od %>% 
  filter(strain %in% common_strains) %>% 
  arrange(strain) %>% 
  dplyr::select(-strain) %>% 
  as.matrix()

all_carbons <- colnames(mat_mu)
carbon_pairs_tmp <- t(combn(all_carbons, 2)) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  rename(carbon_1 = V1, carbon_2 = V2)


analysis_results <- carbon_pairs_tmp %>%
  split(1:nrow(.)) %>% 
  map_dfr(function(pair) {
    c1 <- pair$carbon_1
    c2 <- pair$carbon_2
    
    y1 <- mat_mu[, c1]
    y2 <- mat_mu[, c2]
    z1 <- mat_od[, c1]
    z2 <- mat_od[, c2]
    
    raw_cor <- cor.test(y1, y2, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)

    res_cor <- tryCatch({
      r_y1 <- rank(y1); r_y2 <- rank(y2); r_z1 <- rank(z1); r_z2 <- rank(z2)

      fit1 <- lm(r_y1 ~ r_z1 + r_z2)
      fit2 <- lm(r_y2 ~ r_z1 + r_z2)
      
      cor.test(residuals(fit1), residuals(fit2), method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)
    }, error = function(e) return(NULL))
    
    if (!is.null(res_cor)) {
      tibble(
        carbon_1   = c1,
        carbon_2   = c2,
        raw_rho    = raw_cor$estimate,
        raw_p      = raw_cor$p.value,
        pcor_rho   = res_cor$estimate,
        pcor_p     = res_cor$p.value
      )
    } else {
      NULL
    }
  })


final_comparison <- analysis_results %>%
  mutate(
    raw_p_adj  = p.adjust(raw_p, method = "BH"),
    pcor_p_adj = p.adjust(pcor_p, method = "BH"),
    rho_drop   = raw_rho - pcor_rho
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(carbon_1, carbon_2, raw_rho, raw_p_adj, pcor_rho, pcor_p_adj, rho_drop)

print(head(final_comparison, 10))

ggscatter(final_comparison, x="raw_rho",y="pcor_rho",
          cor.coef = T,
          cor.coeff.args = list(method="spearman"))+
  geom_abline(slope = 1,intercept = 0,color="red")
  



Sys.time()
```

```{r,fig.height=10,fig.width=10,dpi=300}
    z2 <- mat_od[, c2]
    
    # Standard (raw) correlation
    raw_cor <- cor.test(y1, y2, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)
    
    # Partial correlation: compute residuals after removing the effects of z1 and z2
    res_cor <- tryCatch({
      # Convert y1, y2, z1, z2 all to ranks
      r_y1 <- rank(y1); r_y2 <- rank(y2); r_z1 <- rank(z1); r_z2 <- rank(z2)
      
      # Regress on control variables (z1, z2) and extract residuals (unexplained variation)
      fit1 <- lm(r_y1 ~ r_z1 + r_z2)
      fit2 <- lm(r_y2 ~ r_z1 + r_z2)
      
      # Compute Spearman correlation between the residuals
      cor.test(residuals(fit1), residuals(fit2), method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)
    }, error = function(e) return(NULL))
    
    if (!is.null(res_cor)) {
      tibble(
        carbon_1   = c1,
        carbon_2   = c2,
        raw_rho    = raw_cor$estimate,
        raw_p      = raw_cor$p.value,
        pcor_rho   = res_cor$estimate,
        pcor_p     = res_cor$p.value
      )
    } else {
      NULL
    }
  })

# ----------------------------------------------------
# 3. Multiple testing correction (BH method)
# ----------------------------------------------------
final_comparison <- analysis_results %>%
  mutate(
    raw_p_adj  = p.adjust(raw_p, method = "BH"),
    pcor_p_adj = p.adjust(pcor_p, method = "BH"),
    rho_drop   = raw_rho - pcor_rho
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(carbon_1, carbon_2, raw_rho, raw_p_adj, pcor_rho, pcor_p_adj, rho_drop)

# Check results
print(head(final_comparison, 10))

ggscatter(final_comparison, x="raw_rho",y="pcor_rho",
          cor.coef = T,
          cor.coeff.args = list(method="spearman"))+
  geom_abline(slope = 1,intercept = 0,color="red")
  



Sys.time()
```

```{r}
calc_carbon_dist_per_strain<-function(fn_strains,fn_dist_long){
  fn_df<-fn_dist_long %>%
  filter(strain1 == strain2) %>%
    filter(strain1 %in% fn_strains) %>%
  group_by(carbon1, carbon2) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_cos_dist = mean(cos_dist, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_cos_dist   = sd(cos_dist, na.rm = TRUE),
    cv_cos_dist   = ifelse(mean_cos_dist == 0, 0, sd_cos_dist / mean_cos_dist),
    n_strains     = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
}
```

```{r, fig.width=12,fig.height=12}
# 1. Preprocessing and join (suppress warning by specifying relationship = "many-to-many")
fba_models <- ecor_fba_basalZ %>% 
  rename(model_strain = strain)

exp_data <- gr_ecor_df %>% 
  select(strain,carbon,mu_max_allrep) %>%
  rename(exp_strain = strain)

my_tmp<-gr_ma_anc_mean_df %>%
  rename(exp_strain=strain)

exp_data<-bind_rows(exp_data,my_tmp)

cross_df <- inner_join(fba_models, exp_data, by = "carbon", relationship = "many-to-many")

# 2. Spearman correlation for each model × experimental strain combination
cross_summary <- cross_df %>%
  group_by(model_strain, exp_strain) %>%
  filter(!is.na(mu_max_allrep) & !is.na(baseline_Z)) %>%
  filter(n() >= 3) %>%
  summarise(
    spearman_r = cor(mu_max_allrep, baseline_Z, method = "spearman"),
    p_value    = tryCatch({
      if(sd(baseline_Z, na.rm = TRUE) > 0 && sd(mu_max_allrep, na.rm = TRUE) > 0) {
        # Use exact = FALSE to suppress warnings caused by ties
        cor.test(mu_max_allrep, baseline_Z, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)$p.value
      } else { NA_real_ }
    }, error = function(e) NA_real_),
    n          = n(),
    .groups    = "drop"
  )

# 3. Evaluation of self-prediction vs. cross-strain prediction performance
#    (handles cases where no self-matching strain exists)
model_performance_eval <- cross_summary %>%
  group_by(model_strain) %>%
  summarise(
    # Return NA_real_ if no entry with model_strain == exp_strain is found
    self_r = {
      val <- spearman_r[model_strain == exp_strain]
      if (length(val) == 1) val else NA_real_
    },
    
    # Mean Spearman r across other (non-self) strains
    other_mean_r = mean(spearman_r[model_strain != exp_strain], na.rm = TRUE),
    
    # Standard deviation of Spearman r across other (non-self) strains
    other_sd_r = sd(spearman_r[model_strain != exp_strain], na.rm = TRUE),
    
    # Specificity index: self-prediction minus mean cross-strain prediction
    specificity_index = self_r - other_mean_r,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(self_r))

print("--- Self-prediction vs. generalized prediction performance for each model ---")
print(head(model_performance_eval, 10))

# 1. Extract diagonal entries (rows where model_strain == exp_strain)
diagonal_data <- cross_summary %>%
  filter(model_strain == exp_strain)

# 2. Draw heatmap
p<-ggplot(cross_summary, aes(x = exp_strain, y = model_strain)) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = spearman_r)) +
  # Overlay black borders on diagonal entries only (fill = NA keeps the interior transparent)
  geom_tile(
    data = diagonal_data,
    color = "black",
    fill = NA,
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "#377EB8", 
    mid = "white", 
    high = "#E41A1C", 
    midpoint = 0,
    name = "Spearman r",
    na.value = "grey90"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "right"
  ) +
  labs(

    subtitle = "Black borders highlight matching model-strain pairs (self-prediction)",
    x = "Experimental Data (Strain)",
    y = "FBA Model (Strain)"
  )+
```

##### 4.13.1.1.3 Entanglement score with permutation test (processing time: 15 min)
```{r,fig.width=1.8,fig.height=5,dpi=300}
# 1. Pre-processing: Create initial dendrograms
# Genetic distance (FBA theory) and Evolutionary distance (ECOR data)
dend_fba_raw <- as.dendrogram(carbon_row_cluster)
current_labels <- labels(dend_fba_raw)

# Color labels based on metabolic categories
dend_fba_raw <- dend_fba_raw %>% 
  set("labels_colors", carbon_labels_ordered$Category_col)

dend_ecor_raw<- as.dendrogram(ecor_row_cluster)

# 2. Untangle: Minimize crossing lines between the two dendrograms
# This optimizes the visualization without changing the underlying topology
dl <- dendlist(dend_fba_raw, dend_ecor_raw)
dl_untangled <- dendextend::untangle(dl, method = "step2side")

dend_p <- dl_untangled[[1]] # Optimized FBA-based dendrogram
dend_t <- dl_untangled[[2]] # Optimized ECOR-based dendrogram

# 3. Create color vectors for plotting
# Retrieve current label order from the left (FBA) tree
current_labels_p <- labels(dend_p)

# Map categories and colors to the current labels
groups_p <- carbon_labels_ordered$Category[match(current_labels_p, carbon_labels_ordered$label)]
col_vector_p <- carbon_labels_ordered$Category_col[match(current_labels_p, carbon_labels_ordered$label)]

# 4. Set label colors (branches remain black)
dend_p <- dend_p %>% set("labels_colors", col_vector_p)

# Match labels of the ECOR-based tree to the FBA-based tree's color vector
dend_t <- dend_t %>% 
  set("labels_colors", col_vector_p[match(labels(dend_t), current_labels_p)])

# 5. Draw Tanglegram for ECOR
# Assessing structural similarity between metabolic theory and natural evolution
tanglegram(dend_p, dend_t,
           common_subtrees_color_lines = FALSE, 
           highlight_distinct_edges = FALSE,
           highlight_branches_lwd = FALSE, 
           color_lines = col_vector_p, # Connecting lines match category colors
           main_left = "FBA-based",
           main_right = "Growth-based",
           lab.cex = 1,
           lwd=2,
           columns_width = c(4, 2.5, 4),  # Narrow central column to emphasize links
           margin_inner = 3.5,          
           margin_outer = 0.5,             
           # 枝の色を黒で固定
           axes = FALSE)

# legend
# legend("topleft", legend = names(pgPalette), fill = pgPalette, title = "Phylogroup", cex = 0.8)


# 6. Calculate Observed Entanglement Score
# Lower entanglement score suggests higher similarity between trees
actual_ent <- entanglement(dl_untangled) # Entanglement score after untangling

print(Sys.time())

# 7. Permutation Test for Entanglement
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- if_else(iteration_scale=="large",1000,10)
perm_ent <- numeric(n_perm)

# Fix the structural layout of the theoretical tree
labels_theory <- labels(dend_p)

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # Create a copy of the experimental dendrogram and shuffle labels
  shuffled_dend <- dend_t
  labels(shuffled_dend) <- sample(labels_theory)
  
  # Perform untangle for each shuffle to maintain consistency with the observed value
  perm_dends <- dendlist(dend_p, shuffled_dend) %>% dendextend::untangle(method = "step2side")
  perm_ent[i] <- entanglement(perm_dends)
  
  # Progress monitoring
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# 8. Calculate P-value
# P-value: Probability that random entanglement is lower than the observed value
p_val_ent <- sum(perm_ent <= actual_ent) / n_perm

# 9. Results Visualization
hist(perm_ent, main="Permutation Test for Entanglement", 
     xlab="Entanglement Score", xlim=c(0, 1))
abline(v = actual_ent, col = "red", lwd = 2)
cat(sprintf("Actual Entanglement: %.3f\nP-value: %.4f\n", actual_ent, p_val_ent))
Sys.time()
```
##### 4.13.1.1.4 Cophenetic correlation with permutation test
```{r}
# 1. Prepare distance matrices and initial dendrograms for ECOR
## load 7 GEM based distance matrix (essentiality based)
target_order<-sort(ecor_carbons)
my_cbdist_mat <- carbon_matrix_7gem[target_order,target_order]
my_cbdist_mat <- as.dist(my_cbdist_mat)
dist_theory<-my_cbdist_mat
## experimental
dist_exp<-ecor_dist_matrix

# Hierarchical clustering using Ward's D2 method
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = cl_method)
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method)

dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# Calculate observed Cophenetic correlation (Spearman)
# This evaluates the correlation between the dendrogram-induced distances and original matrices
actual_cor <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_exp, method = "spearman")

# --- Integrated Permutation Test ---
# Generating a null distribution by shuffling labels to evaluate statistical significance
print(Sys.time())
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- 1000
perm_results <- data.frame(cor = numeric(n_perm))

# Retrieve labels (strain names) from the experimental distance matrix
exp_labels <- rownames(as.matrix(dist_exp))

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # 1. Shuffle only the labels while maintaining the distance matrix structure
  dist_shuffled <- dist_exp
  shuffled_labels <- sample(exp_labels)
  
  # Re-assign shuffled labels to the matrix
  temp_mat <- as.matrix(dist_shuffled)
  rownames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  colnames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  
  # 2. Reconstruct the dendrogram from the shuffled distance matrix
  # Consistency in the clustering method (ward.D2) is crucial
  hc_shuffled <- hclust(as.dist(temp_mat), method = cl_method)
  dend_shuffled <- as.dendrogram(hc_shuffled)
  
  # 3. Compute and store correlation for the permuted pair
  perm_results$cor[i] <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_shuffled, method = "spearman")
  
  # Progress monitoring
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# --- Statistical Evaluation ---
# P-value: Probability of obtaining a correlation as high as observed by chance
p_val_cor <- sum(perm_results$cor >= actual_cor) / n_perm

cat("【Analysis Results】\n")
cat(sprintf("Cophenetic Cor (Spearman): %.3f (p = %.4f)\n", actual_cor, p_val_cor))

# --- Visualization: Cophenetic Correlation Bubble Plot ---
# 1. Prepare data and count overlapping distance pairs for bubble sizing
df_coph <- data.frame(
  Theory = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_theory)),
  Experiment = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_exp))
) %>%
  group_by(Theory, Experiment) %>%
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = 'drop')

my_txt<-paste("R=",sprintf("%.3f",actual_cor),sep="")

# 2. Visualization using ggscatter
# Point size and color intensity are log2-scaled to reflect the density of identical distance pairs
ggscatter(df_coph, x = "Theory", y = "Experiment",
          size = "count",          # Map number of ties to dot size
          fill = "count",           # Map number of ties to color intensity
          color = "black",          # Solid black borders for bubbles
          shape = 21,               # Filled circles with borders
          alpha= 0.8,
          xlab = "Cophenetic distance (Theory)",
          ylab = "Cophenetic distance (Experiment)",
          title = "Cophenetic Correlation (Log-scaled Bubble Size)",
          ylim=c(0,3)) +
  # Apply log2 transformation to handle the wide range of point densities
  scale_size_continuous(trans = "log2", range = c(1, 12), name = "Count (log2)") +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Greys", trans = "log2", direction = 1, name = "Count (log2)")+

Sys.time()
```

##### 4.13.1.1.5 Baker's Gamma Index for Topological Similarity
```{r}
# 1. Prepare distance matrices and initial dendrograms for ECOR
## load 7 GEM based distance matrix (essentiality based)
target_order<-sort(ecor_carbons)
my_cbdist_mat <- carbon_matrix_7gem[target_order,target_order]
my_cbdist_mat <- as.dist(my_cbdist_mat)
dist_theory<-my_cbdist_mat
## experimental
dist_exp<-ecor_dist_matrix

# Hierarchical clustering using Ward's D2 method
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = cl_method)
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method)

dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# 2. Calculate Observed Baker's Gamma Index
# Baker's Gamma measures the rank correlation between the stages at which 
# pairs of objects combine in each dendrogram.
actual_gamma <- cor_bakers_gamma(dend_theory, dend_exp)
cat(sprintf("Actual Baker's Gammer: %.3f\n", actual_gamma))

# 3. Permutation Test (1,000 iterations)
# Building a null distribution by randomly shuffling labels to assess significance
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- 1000
perm_gammas <- numeric(n_perm)

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # Randomly shuffle the labels of one dendrogram while preserving its structure
  perm_dend <- sample.dendrogram(dend_theory, replace = FALSE)
  # Compute Baker's Gamma for the shuffled pair
  perm_gammas[i] <- cor_bakers_gamma(perm_dend, dend_exp)
}

# 4. Calculate P-value
# P-value: The probability of obtaining a Gamma value as high as observed by chance
p_value <- sum(perm_gammas >= actual_gamma) / n_perm

print(Sys.time())
cat(sprintf("P-value: %.4f\n", p_value))
```
##### 4.13.1.1.6 Validation of essentiality-based Clusters using ECOR Evolutionary Correlations
```{r,fig.width=2,fig.height=3,dpi=300}
# 1. Clustering based on Theory (FBA) vs. Experiment (ECOR)
# Defining the number of clusters (k) for comparative analysis
k_val <- 3

## load 7 GEM based distance matrix (essentiality based)
target_order<-sort(ecor_carbons)
my_cbdist_mat <- carbon_matrix_7gem[target_order,target_order]
my_cbdist_mat <- as.dist(my_cbdist_mat)
dist_theory<-my_cbdist_mat
## experimental
dist_exp<-ecor_dist_matrix
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = cl_method)
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method)

# Assign clusters to each carbon source based on both datasets
cluster_theory <- cutree(hc_theory, k = k_val)
cluster_exp    <- cutree(hc_exp, k = k_val)

# Merge cluster assignments into a mapping table
my_df1<-data.frame(carbon=names(cluster_theory),theory=cluster_theory)
my_df2<-data.frame(carbon=names(cluster_exp),exp=cluster_exp)
my_tmp<-left_join(my_df1,my_df2,by="carbon")

# 2. Data Integration for Pairwise Correlation Analysis
# Filter for unique pairs (upper triangle) and map cluster assignments for both members of each pair
my_df<-ecor_pair_all[ecor_pair_all$key=="upper",]
my_tmp1<-my_tmp %>% rename(carbon1=carbon,theory1=theory,exp1=exp)
my_tmp2<-my_tmp %>% rename(carbon2=carbon,theory2=theory,exp2=exp)
my_df<-left_join(my_df,my_tmp1,by="carbon1")
my_df<-left_join(my_df,my_tmp2,by="carbon2")

# Display the mapping results for inspection
print("Mapping of Carbon Sources to FBA (Theory) and ECOR (Experiment) Clusters:")
print(my_tmp)

# 3. Statistical Comparison: Within-Theory-Cluster vs. Between-Cluster Correlations
# Testing if FBA-defined metabolic modules exhibit higher evolutionary coherence in ECOR data
my_clstrs<-seq(1,k_val)
my_list<-list()

for(i in 1:length(my_clstrs)){
  my_cls<-my_clstrs[i]
  
  # Select pairs where at least one member belongs to the current FBA cluster
  my_dat<-my_df[(my_df$theory1==my_cls)|(my_df$theory2==my_cls),]
  
  # Label pairs as "Within" (specific cluster ID) or "Between" (cross-cluster comparison)
  my_dat$pair_cluster_theory<-"Between"
  my_dat[my_dat$theory1 == my_dat$theory2, ]$pair_cluster_theory <- as.character(my_cls)
  
  # Set factor levels to ensure "Between" is the reference group in plots
  my_dat$pair_cluster_theory <- factor(my_dat$pair_cluster_theory, levels = c(as.character(my_cls), "Between"))
  
  # 4. Visualization: Boxplot with Wilcoxon Rank Sum Test
  my_list[[i]]<-ggboxplot(my_dat,
          x="pair_cluster_theory",y="correlation",
          ylab="Evolutionary correlation [arb. unit]",xlab="",
          add="jitter",add.params = list(alpha=0.5),
          # palette = my_palette,
          legend="")+
    # Use Wilcoxon test with BH adjustment to compare within-cluster correlation against the baseline
  stat_pwc(method = "wilcox.test",label = "p.adj.signif",
           ref.group = "Between",tip.length = 0,
    p.adjust.method = "BH",hide.ns = TRUE)+
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-0.4, 0.8, by = 0.4), limits = c(-0.4, 1))
}

# Display the comparison for Cluster 1
print("Plotting comparison for FBA Cluster 1:")
my_list[[1]]

Sys.time()
```

###### 4.13.1.1.7.1 Entanglement score with permutation test
```{r, fig.width=1.8,fig.height=2.5,dpi=300}

# 1. Data Preparation: Subsetting carbon sources
# Transforming ECOR growth data into a matrix and excluding 'Upper Glycolysis' category
mat_exp<-gr_ecor_df %>%
  select(carbon,mu_max,strain) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon,values_from = mu_max)
# my_rows<-paste("ECOR",sprintf("%02d", mat_exp$strain),sep="")
my_rows<-mat_exp$strain
mat_exp<-mat_exp %>% select(-strain)

# Filter carbon sources to exclude Upper Glycolysis based on the reference label dataframe
my_ins<-carbon_labels_ordered[carbon_labels_ordered$Category %nin% "Upper Glycolysis",]$label
mat_exp<-mat_exp %>% select(all_of(my_ins)) %>% as.matrix()
rownames(mat_exp)<-my_rows

# Calculate distances for the subset
## dist_exp uses Spearman correlation, dist_theory uses the FBA-based matrix
dist_exp<-mat_exp %>% spearman_dist()
# load 7 GEM based distance matrix (essentiality based)
my_cbdist_mat <- carbon_matrix_7gem[my_ins,my_ins]
my_cbdist_mat <- as.dist(my_cbdist_mat)
dist_theory<-my_cbdist_mat

# Hierarchical clustering
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = cl_method)
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method)

dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# 2. Untangle: Optimize the layout for visualization
# Rotating branches to minimize crossing lines while preserving topology
dl <- dendlist(dend_theory, dend_exp)
dl_untangled <- dendextend::untangle(dl, method = "step2side")

dend_p <- dl_untangled[[1]] # Optimized FBA-based tree
dend_t <- dl_untangled[[2]] # Optimized Growth-based tree

# 3. Create color vectors for the subset
current_labels_p <- labels(dend_p)
col_vector_p <- carbon_labels_ordered$Category_col[match(current_labels_p, carbon_labels_ordered$label)]

# 4. Set label colors
dend_p <- dend_p %>% set("labels_colors", col_vector_p)
dend_t <- dend_t %>% 
  set("labels_colors", col_vector_p[match(labels(dend_t), current_labels_p)])

# 5. Draw Tanglegram for the subset (Excluding Upper Glycolysis)
tanglegram(dend_p, dend_t,
           common_subtrees_color_lines = FALSE, 
           highlight_distinct_edges = FALSE,
           highlight_branches_lwd = FALSE,
           color_lines = col_vector_p, 
           main_left = "FBA-based",
           main_right = "Growth-based",
           lab.cex = 1,
           lwd=2,
           columns_width = c(4, 2.5, 4),
           margin_inner = 3.5,
           margin_outer = 0.5,
           axes = FALSE)


# 6. Permutation Test for Entanglement Score
# Evaluating the statistical significance of the topological similarity in the subset
actual_ent <- entanglement(dl_untangled) # Entanglement score after untangling

set.seed(123)
n_perm <- if_else(iteration_scale=="large",1000,10)
perm_ent <- numeric(n_perm)

# Shuffling labels while keeping the structural layout of the theoretical tree fixed
labels_theory <- labels(dend_p)

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  shuffled_dend <- dend_t
  labels(shuffled_dend) <- sample(labels_theory)
  
  # Standardize by applying untangle to each permuted pair
  perm_dends <- dendlist(dend_p, shuffled_dend) %>% 
    dendextend::untangle(method = "step2side")
  perm_ent[i] <- entanglement(perm_dends)
  
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# 7. Calculate P-value
# Lower entanglement score reflects higher similarity
p_val_ent <- sum(perm_ent <= actual_ent) / n_perm

# 8. Plot Results
hist(perm_ent, main="Permutation Test for Entanglement", 
     xlab="Entanglement Score", xlim=c(0, 1))
abline(v = actual_ent, col = "red", lwd = 2)
cat(sprintf("Actual Entanglement: %.3f\nP-value: %.4f\n", actual_ent, p_val_ent))

Sys.time()
```
###### 4.13.1.1.7.2 Cophenetic correlation with permutation test
```{r}
# 1. Data Preparation: Subsetting carbon sources for Cophenetic Correlation
# Excluding 'Upper Glycolysis' to test the robustness of the metabolic constraints
mat_exp<-gr_ecor_df %>%
  select(strain,carbon,mu_max) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon,values_from = mu_max)
# my_rows<-paste("ECOR",sprintf("%02d", mat_exp$strain),sep="")
my_rows<-mat_exp$strain
mat_exp<-mat_exp %>% select(-strain)

# Filter carbon sources based on category
my_ins<-carbon_labels_ordered[carbon_labels_ordered$Category %nin% "Upper Glycolysis",]$label
mat_exp<-mat_exp %>% select(all_of(my_ins)) %>% as.matrix()
rownames(mat_exp)<-my_rows

# Calculate distances for the subset
dist_exp<-mat_exp %>% spearman_dist()
# load 7 GEM based distance matrix (essentiality based)
my_cbdist_mat <- carbon_matrix_7gem[my_ins,my_ins]
my_cbdist_mat <- as.dist(my_cbdist_mat)
dist_theory<-my_cbdist_mat


# Hierarchical clustering using Ward's D2
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = cl_method)
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method)

# dend_theory <- as.data.frame(as.table(as.matrix(dist_theory))) # Placeholder for structure check
dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# Calculate observed Cophenetic correlation (Spearman)
actual_cor <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_exp, method = "spearman")

# --- Integrated Permutation Test ---
# Generating null distribution to evaluate statistical significance of the correlation
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- 1000
perm_results <- data.frame(cor = numeric(n_perm))

# Retrieve labels (strain names) from the subset experimental matrix
exp_labels <- rownames(as.matrix(dist_exp))

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # 1. Shuffle labels while maintaining the underlying distance structure
  dist_shuffled <- dist_exp
  shuffled_labels <- sample(exp_labels)
  
  # Re-assign shuffled names to the distance matrix
  temp_mat <- as.matrix(dist_shuffled)
  rownames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  colnames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  
  # 2. Reconstruct dendrogram from the shuffled matrix
  hc_shuffled <- hclust(as.dist(temp_mat), method = cl_method)
  dend_shuffled <- as.dendrogram(hc_shuffled)
  
  # 3. Compute and store correlation for the permuted pair
  perm_results$cor[i] <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_shuffled, method = "spearman")
}

# --- Statistical Evaluation ---
# P-value: Probability that random correlation is equal to or higher than observed
p_val_cor <- sum(perm_results$cor >= actual_cor) / n_perm

cat("【Analysis Results: Subset without Upper Glycolysis】\n")
cat(sprintf("Cophenetic Cor (Spearman): %.3f (p = %.4f)\n", actual_cor, p_val_cor))

# --- Visualization: Cophenetic Correlation Bubble Plot ---
# 1. Prepare data and count overlapping points (ties) for bubble sizing
df_coph <- data.frame(
  Theory = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_theory)),
  Experiment = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_exp))
) %>%
  group_by(Theory, Experiment) %>%
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = 'drop') 

my_txt<-paste("R=",sprintf("%.3f",actual_cor),sep="")

# 2. Visualization with ggscatter
# Point size and fill color reflect the density of identical distance pairs (log2-scaled)
ggscatter(df_coph, x = "Theory", y = "Experiment",
          size = "count",           # Map overlap count to bubble size
          fill = "count",           # Map overlap count to fill intensity
          color = "black",          # Solid black borders
          shape = 21,               # Filled circles with borders
          alpha= 0.8,
          xlab = "Cophenetic distance (Theory)",
          ylab = "Cophenetic distance (Experiment)",
          title = "Cophenetic Correlation (Log-scaled Bubble Size)",
          ylim=c(0,3)) +
  # Apply log2 transformation to optimize visualization of overlapping points
  scale_size_continuous(trans = "log2", range = c(1, 12), name = "Count (log2)") +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Greys", trans = "log2", direction = 1, name = "Count (log2)")+
  annotate("text", x = 10, y = 2.7, label = my_txt,)
Sys.time()
```

##### 4.13.1.3.2 Entanglement score with permutation test (processing time: 15 min)
```{r,fig.width=1.5,fig.height=3.5,dpi=300}
# Genetic distance from FBA (iML1515) and Phenotypic distance from Growth rates
dist_exp<-as.dist(1 - ecor_matrix)
my_ins<-rownames(ecor_matrix)
dist_theory<-carbon_matrix_iml[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------ iML1515

# Hierarchical clustering using Ward's D2 method
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = cl_method)
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method)

dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# 2. Untangle: Optimize the layout of the two dendrograms to minimize crossings
# Maintaining the topology while rotating branches for better visualization
dl <- dendlist(dend_theory, dend_exp)
dl_untangled <- dendextend::untangle(dl, method = "step2side")

dend_p <- dl_untangled[[1]] # Optimized FBA-based dendrogram
dend_t <- dl_untangled[[2]] # Optimized Growth-based dendrogram


# 3. Create color vectors based on labels
# Retrieve current label order from the left (FBA) dendrogram
current_labels_p <- labels(dend_p)
# Map categories and colors to the current labels
groups_p <- carbon_labels_ordered_7gem$Category[match(current_labels_p, carbon_labels_ordered_7gem$label)]
col_vector_p <- carbon_labels_ordered_7gem$Category_col[match(current_labels_p, carbon_labels_ordered_7gem$label)]

# 4. Set label colors
dend_p <- dend_p %>% set("labels_colors", col_vector_p)

# Match Growth-based tree labels with the FBA-based tree's color vector
dend_t <- dend_t %>% 
  set("labels_colors", col_vector_p[match(labels(dend_t), current_labels_p)])

# 5. Draw Tanglegram
# Visualizing the structural similarity between metabolic theory and growth phenotype
tanglegram(dend_p, dend_t,
           common_subtrees_color_lines = FALSE, 
           highlight_distinct_edges = FALSE,
           highlight_branches_lwd = FALSE,
           color_lines = col_vector_p, 
           main_left = "Essentiality",
           main_right = "ECOR_growth",
           lab.cex = 1,
           lwd=2,
           columns_width = c(4, 1.5, 4),
           margin_inner = 3.5,
           margin_outer = 0.5,
           axes = FALSE)


# 6. Permutation Test for Entanglement Score
# Lower entanglement indicates higher structural similarity
actual_ent <- entanglement(dl_untangled) # Entanglement score after untangling

print(Sys.time())
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- if_else(iteration_scale=="large",1000,10)
perm_ent <- numeric(n_perm)

# Fixed theory-based labels
labels_theory <- labels(dend_p)

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # Copy the experimental dendrogram and shuffle labels
  shuffled_dend <- dend_t
  labels(shuffled_dend) <- sample(labels_theory)
  
  # Calculate entanglement for the shuffled pair after untangling
  perm_dends <- dendlist(dend_p, shuffled_dend) %>% 
    dendextend::untangle(method = "step2side")
  perm_ent[i] <- entanglement(perm_dends)
  
  # Progress monitoring
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# 7. Calculate P-value
# P-value = Probability that random entanglement is lower than the observed value
p_val_ent <- sum(perm_ent <= actual_ent) / n_perm

# 8. Visualization of results
hist(perm_ent, main="Permutation Test for Entanglement", 
     xlab="Entanglement Score", xlim=c(0, 1))
abline(v = actual_ent, col = "red", lwd = 2)
cat(sprintf("Actual Entanglement: %.3f\nP-value: %.4f\n", actual_ent, p_val_ent))

Sys.time()
```
##### 4.13.1.3.3 Cophenetic correlation with permutation test
```{r}
# 1. Prepare distance matrices and initial dendrograms for ECOR
## load iML1515 based distance matrix (essentiality based)
target_order<-sort(ecor_carbons)
my_cbdist_mat <- carbon_matrix_iml[target_order,target_order]
my_cbdist_mat <- as.dist(my_cbdist_mat)
dist_theory<-my_cbdist_mat
## experimental
dist_exp<-ecor_dist_matrix

# Hierarchical clustering using Ward's D2 method
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = cl_method)
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method)

dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# Calculate observed Cophenetic correlation (Spearman)
# This evaluates the correlation between the dendrogram-induced distances and original matrices
actual_cor <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_exp, method = "spearman")

# --- Integrated Permutation Test ---
# Generating a null distribution by shuffling labels to evaluate statistical significance
print(Sys.time())
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- 1000
perm_results <- data.frame(cor = numeric(n_perm))

# Retrieve labels (strain names) from the experimental distance matrix
exp_labels <- rownames(as.matrix(dist_exp))

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # 1. Shuffle only the labels while maintaining the distance matrix structure
  dist_shuffled <- dist_exp
  shuffled_labels <- sample(exp_labels)
  
  # Re-assign shuffled labels to the matrix
  temp_mat <- as.matrix(dist_shuffled)
  rownames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  colnames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  
  # 2. Reconstruct the dendrogram from the shuffled distance matrix
  # Consistency in the clustering method (ward.D2) is crucial
  hc_shuffled <- hclust(as.dist(temp_mat), method = cl_method)
  dend_shuffled <- as.dendrogram(hc_shuffled)
  
  # 3. Compute and store correlation for the permuted pair
  perm_results$cor[i] <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_shuffled, method = "spearman")
  
  # Progress monitoring
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# --- Statistical Evaluation ---
# P-value: Probability of obtaining a correlation as high as observed by chance
p_val_cor <- sum(perm_results$cor >= actual_cor) / n_perm

cat("【Analysis Results】\n")
cat(sprintf("Cophenetic Cor (Spearman): %.3f (p = %.4f)\n", actual_cor, p_val_cor))

# --- Visualization: Cophenetic Correlation Bubble Plot ---
# 1. Prepare data and count overlapping distance pairs for bubble sizing
df_coph <- data.frame(
  Theory = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_theory)),
  Experiment = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_exp))
) %>%
  group_by(Theory, Experiment) %>%
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = 'drop')

my_txt<-paste("R=",sprintf("%.3f",actual_cor),sep="")

# 2. Visualization using ggscatter
# Point size and color intensity are log2-scaled to reflect the density of identical distance pairs
ggscatter(df_coph, x = "Theory", y = "Experiment",
          size = "count",          # Map number of ties to dot size
          fill = "count",           # Map number of ties to color intensity
          color = "black",          # Solid black borders for bubbles
          shape = 21,               # Filled circles with borders
          alpha= 0.8,
          xlab = "Cophenetic distance (Theory)",
          ylab = "Cophenetic distance (Experiment)",
          title = "Cophenetic Correlation (Log-scaled Bubble Size)",
          ylim=c(0,3)) +
  # Apply log2 transformation to handle the wide range of point densities
  scale_size_continuous(trans = "log2", range = c(1, 12), name = "Count (log2)") +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Greys", trans = "log2", direction = 1, name = "Count (log2)")+
  annotate("text", x = 10, y = 2.7, label = my_txt)

Sys.time()
```

### 4.14.2 Pairwise correlation across strains (All pairs)
```{r,fig.height=3,fig.width=6}
df_up<-combn(gr_ecor_df$strain %>% unique(), 2) %>% t() %>% as.data.frame()
colnames(df_up)<-qw(strain1,strain2)
df_up$key<-"upper"
df_diag<-data.frame(strain1=gr_ecor_df$strain %>% unique(),strain2=gr_ecor_df$strain %>% unique(),key="diag")
df_lw<-df_up
colnames(df_lw)<-qw(strain2,strain1,key)
df_lw$key<-"lower"
ecorstrain_pairs<-bind_rows(df_up,df_diag)
ecorstrain_pairs<-bind_rows(ecorstrain_pairs,df_lw)
ecor_strain_pair_all<-ecorstrain_pairs
ecor_strain_pair_all$correlation<-NA
ecor_strain_pair_all$correlation_allrep<-NA
i<-1
for (i in 1:nrow(ecor_strain_pair_all)){
  my_strain_1<-ecor_strain_pair_all$strain1[i]
  my_strain_2<-ecor_strain_pair_all$strain2[i]
  my_df1<-gr_ecor_df[gr_ecor_df$strain==my_strain_1,]
  my_df1<-my_df1 %>% rename(mu_max_1="mu_max",mu_max_allrep_1="mu_max_allrep")
  my_df2<-gr_ecor_df[gr_ecor_df$strain==my_strain_2,]
  my_df2<-my_df2 %>% rename(mu_max_2="mu_max",mu_max_allrep_2="mu_max_allrep")
  my_df<-left_join(my_df1,my_df2,by="carbon")
  my_res<-cor_test(my_df,vars = "mu_max_1",vars2 = "mu_max_2",method = "spearman")
  ecor_strain_pair_all$correlation[i]<-my_res$cor
  my_res<-cor_test(my_df,vars = "mu_max_allrep_1",vars2 = "mu_max_allrep_2",method = "spearman")
  ecor_strain_pair_all$correlation_allrep[i]<-my_res$cor
}

Sys.time()
```

### 4.14.3 Clustering across ECOR strains
#### 4.14.3.1 Hierarchical clustering for growth profiles across ECOR strains
```{r,fig.height=10,fig.width=10}
# Convert to matrix
ecor_strain_matrix <- ecor_strain_pair_all %>% select(strain1, strain2, correlation) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = strain2, values_from = correlation) %>%
  column_to_rownames("strain1") %>%
  as.matrix()

# Sorting
target_order <- sort(rownames(ecor_strain_matrix))
ecor_strain_matrix <- ecor_strain_matrix[target_order, target_order]

# Calc distance (1 - r)
ecor_strain_dist_matrix <- as.dist(1 - ecor_strain_matrix)

# 1. Convert the distance object to a square matrix
my_mat <- as.matrix(ecor_strain_dist_matrix)

# 2. Create all pair labels using expand.grid
# Generate all pairs from row and column names
ecor_strain_dist_df <- expand.grid(
  strain1 = rownames(my_mat),
  strain2 = colnames(my_mat),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# 3. Add the distance values (mumax_dist)
ecor_strain_dist_df$mumax_dist <- as.vector(my_mat)

# 4. Attach positional tags (Type)
# Create a tag matrix with the same dimensions and attach it as a vector
n <- nrow(my_mat)

ecor_strain_labels_ordered <- left_join(ecor_strain_labels_ordered, my_tmp, by = "label")

my_colors <- colorRampPalette(rev(brewer.pal(11, "RdBu")))(200)

# Visualization
corrplot(ecor_strain_matrix,
         method = "color",

         hclust.method = cl_method,

         tl.cex = 1,
```

#### 4.14.4.3 Mantel test (Four Reps) (Fig. 2e)
```{r}
# 1. Rank correlation of growth rates between strains
all_strains <- unique(c(ecor_strain_pair_all$strain1, ecor_strain_pair_all$strain2))

my_gr_mat <- ecor_strain_pair_all %>%
  select(strain1, strain2, correlation_allrep) %>%
  # 2. Convert strain1 and strain2 to factors with a shared level set
  #    (ensures consistent row/column ordering)
  mutate(
    strain1 = factor(strain1, levels = all_strains),
    strain2 = factor(strain2, levels = all_strains)
  ) %>%
  # 3. Fill in all pairwise combinations and reshape to wide format
  complete(strain1, strain2) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = strain2, values_from = correlation_allrep) %>%
  # 4. Convert to an R matrix
  column_to_rownames(var = "strain1") %>%
  as.matrix()
# Convert the Spearman r matrix to a dissimilarity matrix (1 − r)
my_gr_dist <- 1 - my_gr_mat
my_rows<-rownames(my_gr_dist)

# 2. Phylogenetic distance between strains
my_phydist_mat<-phylo_dist_df %>%
  select(strain1,strain2,phylo_dist) %>%
  filter(strain1 %in% all_strains) %>%
  filter(strain2 %in% all_strains) %>%
  # Convert strain1 and strain2 to factors with a shared level set
  # (ensures consistent row/column ordering)
  mutate(
    strain1 = factor(strain1, levels = all_strains),
    strain2 = factor(strain2, levels = all_strains)
  ) %>%
  # Fill in all pairwise combinations and reshape to wide format
  complete(strain1, strain2) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = strain2, values_from = phylo_dist) %>%
  # Convert to an R matrix
  column_to_rownames(var = "strain1") %>%
  as.matrix()
my_phydist_mat<-my_phydist_mat[my_rows,my_rows]

# 3. Mantel test
# (Note: if the correlation matrix already represents dissimilarity,
#  as.dist(my_gr_mat) can be passed directly instead of as.dist(my_gr_dist))
set.seed(123)
mantel_result <- mantel(
  xdis         = as.dist(my_gr_dist),
  ydis         = as.dist(my_phydist_mat),
  method       = "spearman",   # Rank correlation (change to "pearson" if preferred)
  permutations = 999,          # Number of permutations for stable p-value estimation
  na.rm        = TRUE          # Handle diagonal entries and missing values (NA)
)

# Print results
print(mantel_result)
```
### 4.14.5 Phylogenetic signals (Two Reps)
#### 4.14.5.1 Kmult (multi variate)
```{r}
my_tmp <- gr_ecor_df %>%
  select(strain,carbon,mu_max) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon, values_from = mu_max)

ecor_mlsubtree <- sub_tree
my_df <- data.frame(label = ecor_mlsubtree$tip.label) %>%
  left_join(labdf_sub, by = "label")
ecor_mlsubtree$tip.label <- my_df$strain
ecor_mlsubtree <- keep.tip(ecor_mlsubtree, my_tmp$strain)

ecor_physig_mat <- my_tmp %>%
  select(-strain) %>%
  as.matrix()
rownames(ecor_physig_mat) <- my_tmp$strain
ecor_physig_mat <- ecor_physig_mat[ecor_mlsubtree$tip.label, ]

# Replace branches of length 1e-08 or 0 with a small computable value (e.g., 1e-06)
ecor_mlsubtree$edge.length[ecor_mlsubtree$edge.length < 1e-6] <- 1e-6

k_mult_result <- physignal(ecor_physig_mat, ecor_mlsubtree, iter = 999)
print(summary(k_mult_result)) 

# 1. Standardize the data (mean = 0, variance = 1 for each column)
ecor_physig_mat_scaled <- scale(ecor_physig_mat)

# 2. Recompute the multivariate phylogenetic signal
# * Use 'ecor_mlsubtree' whose branch lengths were adjusted to 1e-06 above
mult_signal_scaled <- physignal(A = ecor_physig_mat_scaled, phy = ecor_mlsubtree, iter = 999)

# 3. Display the results
summary(mult_signal_scaled)
Sys.time()
```

#### 4.14.5.3 Blomberg's K
```{r, fig.height=3,fig.width=5, dpi=300 }
# 1. Phylogenetic Signal Estimation using Blomberg's K
# Initialize a data frame to store K-statistics and P-values for each environment (carbon source)
k_results <- data.frame(Environment = env_names, K_stat = NA, P_val = NA)

for(i in 1:length(env_names)) {
  # Extract scaled growth data for the current environment
  env_data <- ecor_physig_mat_scaled[, i]
  names(env_data) <- rownames(ecor_physig_mat_scaled)
  
  # Remove missing values (NA) to ensure tree-data compatibility
  clean_data <- env_data[!is.na(env_data)]
  # Prune the ML subtree to match the available phenotypic data
  current_tree <- keep.tip(ecor_mlsubtree, names(clean_data))
  
  # Compute Blomberg's K with 999 permutations to assess significance
  sig_k <- phylosig(current_tree, clean_data, method = "K", test = TRUE, nsim = 999)
  
  k_results$K_stat[i] <- sig_k$K
  k_results$P_val[i] <- sig_k$P
}

# 2. Statistical Correction
# Apply Benjamini–Hochberg (BH) adjustment for multiple testing across environments
k_results$P_adj <- p.adjust(k_results$P_val, method = "BH")

# Display significant environments (where phylogenetic signal is detected)
print("Significant Phylogenetic Signals (BH-adjusted P < 0.05):")
print(k_results[k_results$P_adj < 0.05, ])

ggbarplot(k_results,x="Environment",y="K_stat",fill="grey50",size=0)+
  scale_y_log10(
    limits = c(0.001, NA),      
    breaks = log_breaks(n = 5), 
    labels = label_log()       
  )+
  rotate_x_text(angle=90)

k_results$log_K <- log10(k_results$K_stat)

# 3. Visualization: Log-scaled Bar Plot for Blomberg's K
# Set the baseline for the log plot (K=1 represents the Brownian Motion expectation)
base_val <- 0.001
p<-ggplot(k_results, aes(x = Environment, y = K_stat)) +
  # Using geom_rect to precisely control the base of bars on a log-scale
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = as.numeric(as.factor(Environment)) - 0.4, 
                xmax = as.numeric(as.factor(Environment)) + 0.4, 
                ymin = base_val, 
                ymax = K_stat), 
            fill = "grey50") +
  # Configure log10 scale with appropriate breaks and labels
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(base_val, 10), 
                breaks = trans_breaks("log10", function(x) 10^x), 
    labels = label_log())+                              
  # Horizontal line at K = 1 (Standard Brownian Motion model)
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1)+
  theme_pubr() +
  labs(y = "Blomberg's K [arb. unit]")+
  rotate_x_text(angle = 90)
ggpar(p,xlab="")

Sys.time()
```
### 4.14.6 Entanglement analysis between phylogeny and growth-based dendrogram (Two Reps)
#### 4.14.6.1 Entanglement score with permutation test
```{r, fig.width=5,fig.height=4}
# 1. Pre-processing: Ultrametric tree conversion and dendrogram creation
# Convert the ML tree to an ultrametric tree (equal root-to-tip distances)
tree_ultra <- chronos(ecor_mlsubtree)
dend_p_raw <- as.dendrogram(as.hclust(tree_ultra))

# Compute phenotypic distance based on Spearman correlation of growth profiles
dist_trait <- as.dist(1 - cor(t(ecor_physig_mat), method = "spearman"))
dend_t_raw <- as.dendrogram(hclust(dist_trait, method = cl_method))

# 2. Untangle: Optimize branch rotation for visualization
# Minimizing line crossings while strictly maintaining the topology of both trees
dl <- dendlist(dend_p_raw, dend_t_raw)
dl_untangled <- dendextend::untangle(dl, method = "step2side")

dend_p <- dl_untangled[[1]] 
dend_t <- dl_untangled[[2]] 

# 3. Color mapping based on Phylogroups
# Retrieve labels in the current optimized order from the phylogeny (left tree)
current_labels_p <- labels(dend_p)

# Map labels to their respective Phylogroups and assign colors from pgPalette
groups_p <- labdf_sub$Phylogroup[match(current_labels_p, labdf_sub$strain)]
col_vector_p <- pgPalette[groups_p]

# Align trait tree label colors with the phylogeny colors
dend_p <- dend_p %>% set("labels_colors", col_vector_p)

# 4. Set label colors (branches remain neutral black)
dend_t <- dend_t %>% 
  set("labels_colors", col_vector_p[match(labels(dend_t), current_labels_p)])

# 5. Draw Tanglegram: Phylogeny vs. Growth Traits
tanglegram(dend_p, dend_t,
           common_subtrees_color_lines = FALSE, 
           highlight_distinct_edges = FALSE,
           highlight_branches_lwd = FALSE,         
           color_lines = col_vector_p, 
           main_left = "Phylogeny",
           main_right = "Trait-based",
           lab.cex = 0.4,
           columns_width = c(5, 5, 5), 
           margin_inner = 4,           
           margin_outer = 1,             
           axes = FALSE)
# legend("topleft", legend = names(pgPalette), fill = pgPalette, title = "Phylogroup", cex = 0.8)

# Calculate the observed entanglement score after untangling
actual_ent<-dendextend::entanglement(dend_p, dend_t) # Entanglement score
cat(sprintf("Actual Entanglement (after untangle): %.3f\n", actual_ent))

# 6. Permutation Test for Significance
# Assessing if the topological similarity is better than random expectation
n_perm <- if_else(iteration_scale=="large",1000,10)
null_entanglements <- numeric(n_perm)

cat("Starting permutation test (this may take a while)...\n")
print(Sys.time())

set.seed(123) 
labels_fixed <- labels(dend_p)

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # Copy the trait tree and shuffle its labels
  dend_shuffled <- dend_t
  labels(dend_shuffled) <- sample(labels_fixed)
  
  # Re-run untangle for each shuffle to create a fair null distribution
  dl_perm <- dendlist(dend_p, dend_shuffled) %>% 
    dendextend::untangle(method = "step2side")
  
  # Record optimized entanglement for the null model
  null_entanglements[i] <- dendextend::entanglement(dl_perm)
  
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# 7. Statistical Evaluation (P-value)
# Proportion of shuffled trees that achieved a score as low as the actual data
p_value <- sum(null_entanglements <= actual_ent) / (n_perm + 1)

# 8. Plot the Null Distribution
print(Sys.time())
cat(sprintf("P-value: %.4f\n", p_value))

hist(null_entanglements, 
     main="Permutation Test (with untangle)", 
     xlab="Entanglement Score", 
     xlim=c(0, 1), col="lightgray")
abline(v = actual_ent, col = "red", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
legend("topright", legend=c("Actual Score"), col="red", lwd=2, lty=2)
```

### 4.14.7 Baker's Gamma Index for Phylogeny-Trait Congruence
```{r}
# 1. Calculate Observed Baker's Gamma Index
# This measures the rank correlation between the merging stages of the Phylogeny 
# and the Trait-based dendrograms.
actual_gamma <- cor_bakers_gamma(dend_p, dend_t)
cat(sprintf("Actual Baker's Gammer: %.3f\n", actual_gamma))

# 2. Permutation Test (1,000 iterations)
# Assessing the significance of the topological similarity by shuffling labels
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- 1000
perm_gammas <- numeric(n_perm)

# Progress tracking for larger permutations
cat("Calculating null distribution for Baker's Gamma...\n")

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # Shuffle the labels of the phylogeny dendrogram while preserving its branching structure
  perm_dend <- sample.dendrogram(dend_p, replace = FALSE)
  
  # Compute Baker's Gamma for the permuted pair
  perm_gammas[i] <- cor_bakers_gamma(perm_dend, dend_t)
}

# 3. P-value Calculation
# P-value: The probability that a random label assignment would yield 
# a Baker's Gamma equal to or higher than the observed value.
p_value <- sum(perm_gammas >= actual_gamma) / n_perm

print(Sys.time())
cat(sprintf("P-value: %.4f\n", p_value))

# 4. Result Interpretation
if(p_value < 0.05) {
  cat("The topological similarity between phylogeny and traits is statistically significant.\n")
} else {
  cat("No significant topological similarity was detected between phylogeny and traits.\n")
}

```

```{r, fig.height=3,fig.width=5, dpi=300 }
# Set the baseline for the log plot (K=1 represents the Brownian Motion expectation)
base_val <- 0.001
p<-ggplot(k_results, aes(x = Environment, y = K_stat)) +
  # Using geom_rect to precisely control the base of bars on a log-scale
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = as.numeric(as.factor(Environment)) - 0.4, 
                xmax = as.numeric(as.factor(Environment)) + 0.4, 
                ymin = base_val, 
                ymax = K_stat), 
            fill = "grey50") +
  # Configure log10 scale with appropriate breaks and labels
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(base_val, 10), 
                breaks = trans_breaks("log10", function(x) 10^x), 
    labels = label_log())+                              
  # Horizontal line at K = 1 (Standard Brownian Motion model)
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1)+
  theme_pubr() +
  labs(y = "Blomberg's K [-]")+
  rotate_x_text(angle = 90)
ggpar(p,xlab="")

Sys.time()
```
##### 4.14.8.2.3 Entanglement analysis (Fig. 2d)
```{r, fig.width=5,fig.height=4}
# 1. Pre-processing: Ultrametric tree conversion and dendrogram creation
# Convert the ML tree to an ultrametric tree (equal root-to-tip distances)
tree_ultra <- chronos(ecor_mlsubtree)
dend_p_raw <- as.dendrogram(as.hclust(tree_ultra))

# Compute phenotypic distance based on Spearman correlation of growth profiles
dist_trait <- as.dist(1 - cor(t(ecor_physig_mat_allrep), method = "spearman"))
dend_t_raw <- as.dendrogram(hclust(dist_trait, method = cl_method))

# 2. Untangle: Optimize branch rotation for visualization
# Minimizing line crossings while strictly maintaining the topology of both trees
dl <- dendlist(dend_p_raw, dend_t_raw)
dl_untangled <- dendextend::untangle(dl, method = "step2side")

dend_p <- dl_untangled[[1]] 
dend_t <- dl_untangled[[2]] 

# 3. Color mapping based on Phylogroups
# Retrieve labels in the current optimized order from the phylogeny (left tree)
current_labels_p <- labels(dend_p)

# Map labels to their respective Phylogroups and assign colors from pgPalette
groups_p <- labdf_sub$Phylogroup[match(current_labels_p, labdf_sub$strain)]
col_vector_p <- pgPalette[groups_p]

# Align trait tree label colors with the phylogeny colors
dend_p <- dend_p %>% set("labels_colors", col_vector_p)

# 4. Set label colors (branches remain neutral black)
dend_t <- dend_t %>% 
  set("labels_colors", col_vector_p[match(labels(dend_t), current_labels_p)])

# 5. Draw Tanglegram: Phylogeny vs. Growth Traits
tanglegram(dend_p, dend_t,
           common_subtrees_color_lines = FALSE, 
           highlight_distinct_edges = FALSE,
           highlight_branches_lwd = FALSE,         
           color_lines = col_vector_p, 
           main_left = "Phylogeny",
           main_right = "Trait-based",
           lab.cex = 0.4,
           columns_width = c(5, 5, 5), 
           margin_inner = 4,           
           margin_outer = 1,             
           axes = FALSE)
# legend("topleft", legend = names(pgPalette), fill = pgPalette, title = "Phylogroup", cex = 0.8)

# Calculate the observed entanglement score after untangling
actual_ent<-dendextend::entanglement(dend_p, dend_t) # Entanglement score
cat(sprintf("Actual Entanglement (after untangle): %.3f\n", actual_ent))

# 6. Permutation Test for Significance
# Assessing if the topological similarity is better than random expectation
n_perm <- if_else(iteration_scale=="large",1000,10)
null_entanglements <- numeric(n_perm)

cat("Starting permutation test (this may take a while)...\n")
print(Sys.time())

set.seed(123) 
labels_fixed <- labels(dend_p)

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # Copy the trait tree and shuffle its labels
  dend_shuffled <- dend_t
  labels(dend_shuffled) <- sample(labels_fixed)
  
  # Re-run untangle for each shuffle to create a fair null distribution
  dl_perm <- dendlist(dend_p, dend_shuffled) %>% 
    dendextend::untangle(method = "step2side")
  
  # Record optimized entanglement for the null model
  null_entanglements[i] <- dendextend::entanglement(dl_perm)
  
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# 7. Statistical Evaluation (P-value)
# Proportion of shuffled trees that achieved a score as low as the actual data
p_value <- sum(null_entanglements <= actual_ent) / (n_perm + 1)

# 8. Plot the Null Distribution
print(Sys.time())
cat(sprintf("P-value: %.4f\n", p_value))

hist(null_entanglements, 
     main="Permutation Test (with untangle)", 
     xlab="Entanglement Score", 
     xlim=c(0, 1), col="lightgray")
abline(v = actual_ent, col = "red", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
legend("topright", legend=c("Actual Score"), col="red", lwd=2, lty=2)
```

#### 4.14.8.4 Baker's Gamma Index for Phylogeny-Trait Congruence (Fig. 2d)
```{r}
# 1. Calculate Observed Baker's Gamma Index
# This measures the rank correlation between the merging stages of the Phylogeny 
# and the Trait-based dendrograms.
actual_gamma <- cor_bakers_gamma(dend_p, dend_t)
cat(sprintf("Actual Baker's Gammer: %.3f\n", actual_gamma))

# 2. Permutation Test (1,000 iterations)
# Assessing the significance of the topological similarity by shuffling labels
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- 1000
perm_gammas <- numeric(n_perm)

# Progress tracking for larger permutations
cat("Calculating null distribution for Baker's Gamma...\n")

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # Shuffle the labels of the phylogeny dendrogram while preserving its branching structure
  perm_dend <- sample.dendrogram(dend_p, replace = FALSE)
  
  # Compute Baker's Gamma for the permuted pair
  perm_gammas[i] <- cor_bakers_gamma(perm_dend, dend_t)
}

# 3. P-value Calculation
# P-value: The probability that a random label assignment would yield 
# a Baker's Gamma equal to or higher than the observed value.
p_value <- sum(perm_gammas >= actual_gamma) / n_perm

print(Sys.time())
cat(sprintf("P-value: %.4f\n", p_value))

# 4. Result Interpretation
if(p_value < 0.05) {
  cat("The topological similarity between phylogeny and traits is statistically significant.\n")
} else {
  cat("No significant topological similarity was detected between phylogeny and traits.\n")
}
Sys.time()
```
#### 4.14.8.5 Phylogenetic Generalized Least Squares (PGLS)
##### 4.14.8.5.1 Calc. PGLS-derived evolutionary correlation
```{r}
env_names <- colnames(ecor_physig_mat_scaled_allrep)
n_envs <- length(env_names)

# Initialize an empty matrix to store pairwise PGLS correlations
pgls_cor_mat <- matrix(NA, nrow = n_envs, ncol = n_envs, dimnames = list(env_names, env_names))
diag(pgls_cor_mat) <- 1.0

# Generate all pairwise index combinations
pairs_idx <- combn(n_envs, 2)

for(k in 1:ncol(pairs_idx)) {
  i <- pairs_idx[1, k]
  j <- pairs_idx[2, k]
  
  e1 <- env_names[i]
  e2 <- env_names[j]
  
  # 1. Extract data and remove rows with missing values
  df_clean <- data.frame(
    strain = rownames(ecor_physig_mat_scaled_allrep),
    val1   = ecor_physig_mat_scaled_allrep[, e1],
    val2   = ecor_physig_mat_scaled_allrep[, e2],
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ) %>% 
    na.omit()
  
  if(nrow(df_clean) < 5) {
    warning(sprintf("Too few samples to fit PGLS (%s – %s: n = %d)", e1, e2, nrow(df_clean)))
    next
  }
  
  # 2. Trim the phylogeny to the retained strains and rescale branch lengths
  my_tree <- keep.tip(ecor_mlsubtree, df_clean$strain)
  my_tree$node.label <- NULL
  my_tree$edge.length <- my_tree$edge.length * 100
  
  # 3. Prepare the data frame for caper
  df_caper <- df_clean
  df_caper$Species <- as.factor(df_clean$strain)
  
  # 4. Run PGLS with a fallback strategy
  res_val <- tryCatch({
    # Link phenotypic data to the phylogeny
    comp_data <- comparative.data(phy = my_tree, data = df_caper, names.col = "Species", vcv = TRUE)
    
    # First, attempt ML optimization of lambda
    fit <- tryCatch({
      pgls(val2 ~ val1, data = comp_data, lambda = "ML")
    }, error = function(e) {
      # If ML optimization fails, retry with lambda fixed at 1e-6 (effectively zero)
      message(sprintf("[Optimization failed] %s \u00d7 %s: optim error. Retrying with lambda = 1e-6.", e1, e2))
      pgls(val2 ~ val1, data = comp_data, lambda = 1e-6)
    })
    
    sum_fit <- summary(fit)
    
    # Extract test statistics
    t_val  <- sum_fit$coefficients["val1", "t value"]
    df_res <- sum_fit$df[2] 
    
    # Compute the partial correlation coefficient r from the t statistic
    t_val / sqrt(t_val^2 + df_res)
    
  }, error = function(e) {
    # Return NA only when the computation is entirely intractable
    message(sprintf("[Fatal error] %s \u00d7 %s could not be computed: %s", e1, e2, e$message))
    return(NA)
  })
  
  # Store the result in both cells of the symmetric matrix
  pgls_cor_mat[i, j] <- res_val
  pgls_cor_mat[j, i] <- res_val
}

# Convert the symmetric correlation matrix to a long-format data frame
pgls_cor_df <- pgls_cor_mat %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("carbon1") %>%
  pivot_longer(-carbon1, names_to = "carbon2", values_to = "pgls_correlation")

Sys.time()
```

##### 4.14.8.5.5 Cophenetic correlation with permutation test (Fig. S5c)
```{r}
# 1. Prepare distance matrices and initial dendrograms
dist_exp<-as.dist(1 - pgls_cor_mat)
my_ins<-rownames(pgls_cor_mat)

# Flux-based metabolic distance
dist_theory<-mean_carbon_dist_matrix[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------ cosine distance

# Hierarchical clustering
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = cl_method)
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method)

dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# Calculate observed Cophenetic correlation (Spearman)
# This measures how well the tree structure reflects the original distance matrix
actual_cor <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_exp, method = "spearman")

# --- Permutation Test for Cophenetic Correlation ---
print(Sys.time())
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- 1000
perm_results <- data.frame(cor = numeric(n_perm))

# Get original labels (strain names) from the experimental distance matrix
exp_labels <- rownames(as.matrix(dist_exp))

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # 1. Shuffle labels while keeping the underlying matrix structure intact
  dist_shuffled <- dist_exp
  shuffled_labels <- sample(exp_labels)
  
  # Convert to matrix to reassign shuffled names
  temp_mat <- as.matrix(dist_shuffled)
  rownames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  colnames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  
  # 2. Reconstruct dendrogram from the shuffled distance matrix
  hc_shuffled <- hclust(as.dist(temp_mat), method = cl_method)
  dend_shuffled <- as.dendrogram(hc_shuffled)
  
  # 3. Calculate and store the correlation for this permutation
  perm_results$cor[i] <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_shuffled, method = "spearman")
  
  # Progress monitoring
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# --- Statistical Evaluation ---
# P-value: Proportion of permutations where correlation is equal to or greater than observed
p_val_cor <- sum(perm_results$cor >= actual_cor) / n_perm

cat("【Analysis Results】\n")
cat(sprintf("Cophenetic Cor (Spearman): %.3f (p = %.4f)\n", actual_cor, p_val_cor))

# --- Visualization: Cophenetic Correlation Bubble Plot ---
# 1. Prepare data and count overlapping points (ties) for bubble sizing
df_coph <- data.frame(
  Theory = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_theory)),
  Experiment = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_exp))
) %>%
  group_by(Theory, Experiment) %>%
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = 'drop') # 各座標の重複数をカウント

my_txt<-paste("R=",sprintf("%.3f",actual_cor),sep="")

# 2. Plotting with ggscatter
# Bubble size and color intensity are log2-scaled to visualize the density of distance pairs
ggscatter(df_coph, x = "Theory", y = "Experiment",
          size = "count",           # Map count to dot size
          fill = "count",           # Map count to fill color
          color = "black",          # Fix border color to black
          shape = 21,               # Use filled circles with borders
          alpha= 0.8,
          xlab = "Cophenetic distance (Theory)",
          ylab = "Cophenetic distance (Experiment)",
          title = "Cophenetic Correlation (Log-scaled Bubble Size)",
          ylim=c(0,3)) +
  # Apply log2 transformation to size and color to handle the wide range of counts
  scale_size_continuous(trans = "log2", range = c(1, 12), name = "Count (log2)") +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Greys", trans = "log2", direction = 1, name = "Count (log2)")+
  annotate("text", x = 0.2, y = 2.7, label = my_txt,)

Sys.time()
```

#### 4.14.8.6 Phylogenetically Independent Contrasts (PIC)
##### 4.14.8.6.1 Calc. PIC-derived evolutionary correlation
```{r,}
env_names <- colnames(ecor_physig_mat_scaled_allrep)
n_envs <- length(env_names)

# Initialize a matrix to store phylogenetically independent contrast (PIC)
# vectors for each carbon source
pic_mat <- matrix(NA, nrow = n_strains - 1, ncol = n_envs, 
                  dimnames = list(NULL, env_names))

for(e in env_names) {
  env_data <- ecor_physig_mat_scaled_allrep[, e]
  names(env_data) <- rownames(ecor_physig_mat_scaled_allrep)
  clean_d <- na.omit(env_data)
  
  sub_t <- keep.tip(ecor_mlsubtree, names(clean_d))
  
  # Compute phylogenetically independent contrasts (PICs)
  pic_mat[1:(length(clean_d)-1), e] <- pic(clean_d, sub_t)
}

# Compute a Spearman correlation matrix from the PIC matrix
pic_cor_mat <- cor(pic_mat, method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

pic_cor_df<-pic_cor_mat %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("carbon1") %>%
  pivot_longer(-carbon1, names_to = "carbon2", values_to = "pic_correlation")

Sys.time()
```
