##### 4.14.8.6.4 Entanglement score with permutation test (Fig. S5f)
```{r, fig.width=1.5,fig.height=3.5,dpi=300}

# Flux-based distance and Phenotypic distance from Growth rates
dist_exp<-as.dist(1 - pic_cor_mat)
my_ins<-rownames(pic_cor_mat)
dist_theory<-mean_carbon_dist_matrix[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------ cosine distance


# Hierarchical clustering using Ward's D2 method
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = cl_method)
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method)

dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# 2. Untangle: Optimize the layout of the two dendrograms to minimize crossings
# Maintaining the topology while rotating branches for better visualization
dl <- dendlist(dend_theory, dend_exp)
dl_untangled <- dendextend::untangle(dl, method = "step2side")

dend_p <- dl_untangled[[1]] # Optimized FBA-based dendrogram
dend_t <- dl_untangled[[2]] # Optimized Growth-based dendrogram


# 3. Create color vectors based on labels
# Retrieve current label order from the left (FBA) dendrogram
current_labels_p <- labels(dend_p)
# Map categories and colors to the current labels
groups_p <- carbon_labels_ordered_cos$Category[match(current_labels_p, carbon_labels_ordered_cos$label)]
col_vector_p <- carbon_labels_ordered_cos$Category_col[match(current_labels_p, carbon_labels_ordered_cos$label)]

# 4. Set label colors
dend_p <- dend_p %>% set("labels_colors", col_vector_p)

# Match Growth-based tree labels with the FBA-based tree's color vector
dend_t <- dend_t %>% 
  set("labels_colors", col_vector_p[match(labels(dend_t), current_labels_p)])

# 5. Draw Tanglegram
# Visualizing the structural similarity between metabolic theory and growth phenotype
tanglegram(dend_p, dend_t,
           common_subtrees_color_lines = FALSE, 
           highlight_distinct_edges = FALSE,
           highlight_branches_lwd = FALSE,
           color_lines = col_vector_p, 
           main_left = "Flux",
           main_right = "Growth",
           lab.cex = 1,
           lwd=2,
           columns_width = c(4, 1.5, 4),
           margin_inner = 3.5,
           margin_outer = 0.5,
           axes = FALSE)


# 6. Permutation Test for Entanglement Score
# Lower entanglement indicates higher structural similarity
actual_ent <- entanglement(dl_untangled) # Entanglement score after untangling

print(Sys.time())
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- if_else(iteration_scale=="large",1000,10)
perm_ent <- numeric(n_perm)

# Fixed theory-based labels
labels_theory <- labels(dend_p)

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # Copy the experimental dendrogram and shuffle labels
  shuffled_dend <- dend_t
  labels(shuffled_dend) <- sample(labels_theory)
  
  # Calculate entanglement for the shuffled pair after untangling
  perm_dends <- dendlist(dend_p, shuffled_dend) %>% 
    dendextend::untangle(method = "step2side")
  perm_ent[i] <- entanglement(perm_dends)
  
  # Progress monitoring
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# 7. Calculate P-value
# P-value = Probability that random entanglement is lower than the observed value
p_val_ent <- sum(perm_ent <= actual_ent) / n_perm

# 8. Visualization of results
hist(perm_ent, main="Permutation Test for Entanglement", 
     xlab="Entanglement Score", xlim=c(0, 1))
abline(v = actual_ent, col = "red", lwd = 2)
cat(sprintf("Actual Entanglement: %.3f\nP-value: %.4f\n", actual_ent, p_val_ent))

Sys.time()
```
##### 4.14.8.6.5 Cophenetic correlation with permutation test (Fig. S5f)
```{r}
# 1. Prepare distance matrices and initial dendrograms
dist_exp<-as.dist(1 - pic_cor_mat)
my_ins<-rownames(pic_cor_mat)

# Flux-based metabolic distance
dist_theory<-mean_carbon_dist_matrix[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------ cosine distance

# Hierarchical clustering
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = cl_method)
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method)

dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# Calculate observed Cophenetic correlation (Spearman)
# This measures how well the tree structure reflects the original distance matrix
actual_cor <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_exp, method = "spearman")

# --- Permutation Test for Cophenetic Correlation ---
print(Sys.time())
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- 1000
perm_results <- data.frame(cor = numeric(n_perm))

# Get original labels (strain names) from the experimental distance matrix
exp_labels <- rownames(as.matrix(dist_exp))

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # 1. Shuffle labels while keeping the underlying matrix structure intact
  dist_shuffled <- dist_exp
  shuffled_labels <- sample(exp_labels)
  
  # Convert to matrix to reassign shuffled names
  temp_mat <- as.matrix(dist_shuffled)
  rownames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  colnames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  
  # 2. Reconstruct dendrogram from the shuffled distance matrix
  hc_shuffled <- hclust(as.dist(temp_mat), method = cl_method)
  dend_shuffled <- as.dendrogram(hc_shuffled)
  
  # 3. Calculate and store the correlation for this permutation
  perm_results$cor[i] <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_shuffled, method = "spearman")
  
  # Progress monitoring
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# --- Statistical Evaluation ---
# P-value: Proportion of permutations where correlation is equal to or greater than observed
p_val_cor <- sum(perm_results$cor >= actual_cor) / n_perm

cat("【Analysis Results】\n")
cat(sprintf("Cophenetic Cor (Spearman): %.3f (p = %.4f)\n", actual_cor, p_val_cor))

# --- Visualization: Cophenetic Correlation Bubble Plot ---
# 1. Prepare data and count overlapping points (ties) for bubble sizing
df_coph <- data.frame(
  Theory = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_theory)),
  Experiment = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_exp))
) %>%
  group_by(Theory, Experiment) %>%
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = 'drop') # 各座標の重複数をカウント

my_txt<-paste("R=",sprintf("%.3f",actual_cor),sep="")

# 2. Plotting with ggscatter
# Bubble size and color intensity are log2-scaled to visualize the density of distance pairs
ggscatter(df_coph, x = "Theory", y = "Experiment",
          size = "count",           # Map count to dot size
          fill = "count",           # Map count to fill color
          color = "black",          # Fix border color to black
          shape = 21,               # Use filled circles with borders
          alpha= 0.8,
          xlab = "Cophenetic distance (Theory)",
          ylab = "Cophenetic distance (Experiment)",
          title = "Cophenetic Correlation (Log-scaled Bubble Size)",
          ylim=c(0,3)) +
  # Apply log2 transformation to size and color to handle the wide range of counts
  scale_size_continuous(trans = "log2", range = c(1, 12), name = "Count (log2)") +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Greys", trans = "log2", direction = 1, name = "Count (log2)")+
  annotate("text", x = 0.2, y = 2.7, label = my_txt,)

Sys.time()
```
##### 4.14.8.6.6 Elbow
```{r, fig.height=4,fig.width=5}

dist_exp<-as.dist(1 - pic_cor_mat)
my_ins<-rownames(pic_cor_mat)
hc_result <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method)

k_range <- 1:10
wss_values <- sapply(k_range, function(k) {
  ct <- cutree(hc_result, k = k)
  sum(sapply(unique(ct), function(cluster) {
    sub_dist <- as.matrix(dist_exp)[ct == cluster, ct == cluster, drop = FALSE]
    sum(sub_dist^2) / (2 * nrow(sub_dist))
  }))
})

elbow_df <- data.frame(k = k_range, wss = wss_values)


# Elbow Method for Optimal Number of Clusters
p_elbow <- ggplot(elbow_df, aes(x = k, y = wss)) +
  geom_line(color = "black", size = 1.5) +
  geom_point(color = "black", size = 4) +
```

##### 4.14.8.6.7 Concordance with clusters defined from flux-based metabolic distance
```{r,fig.width=4,fig.height=3,dpi=300}
# Extract unique carbon source pairs from the ECOR dataset (upper triangle only)
ecor_df_integrated <-ecor_pair_all %>%
  filter (key=="upper") %>%
  left_join(pic_cor_df,by=c("carbon1","carbon2"))
# Join flux-based cluster assignments (from theory) to the ECOR dataset
ecor_tmp1 <- cbnclust_tbl_fluxbased %>% rename(carbon1 = carbon, cluster1_new = pair_type)
ecor_tmp2 <- cbnclust_tbl_fluxbased %>% rename(carbon2 = carbon, cluster2_new = pair_type)

ecor_df_integrated <- left_join(ecor_df_integrated, ecor_tmp1, by = "carbon1")
ecor_df_integrated <- left_join(ecor_df_integrated, ecor_tmp2, by = "carbon2")


# ==========================================
# 2. Data wrangling: define three pair-type groups with "Between" as reference
# ==========================================
ecor_plot_df <- ecor_df_integrated %>%
  mutate(
    pair_type = case_when(
      cluster1_new == "Cluster 1" & cluster2_new == "Cluster 1" ~ "Cluster 1", # Both in Cluster 1
      cluster1_new == "Cluster 2" & cluster2_new == "Cluster 2" ~ "Cluster 2", # Both in Cluster 2
      TRUE                                                      ~ "Between"   # All other (cross-cluster) pairs
    )
  ) %>%
  # Fix factor level order for plotting and testing: Cluster 1, Cluster 2, Between
  mutate(pair_type = factor(pair_type, levels = c("Cluster 1", "Cluster 2", "Between")))


# ==========================================
# 3. Visualization and statistical testing
# ==========================================
# Draw a boxplot of PIC-based evolutionary correlations (pic_correlation)
p_ecor_integrated <- ggboxplot(
  ecor_plot_df,
  x = "pair_type", 
  y = "pic_correlation",
  ylab = "Evolutionary correlation [-]", 
  xlab = "",
  add = "jitter", 
  add.params = list(alpha = 0.4, size = 1.5), 
  theme = theme_pubr(base_size = 20)
) +
  font("xy.text", size = 18) +
  font("ylab", size = 18) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-0.4, 1.0, by = 0.4), limits = c(-0.4, 1.3)) +
  # Add pairwise Wilcoxon tests against "Between" as the reference group
  stat_pwc(
    method = "wilcox.test",
    ref.group = "Between",      
    p.adjust.method = "BH",     
    label = "p.adj.signif",     
    tip.length = 0,
    bracket.nudge.y = 0.05, 
    hide.ns = TRUE              
  )


print(p_ecor_integrated)


# ==========================================
# 4. Print detailed statistical results to the console (for verification)
# ==========================================
ecor_stat_test <- ecor_plot_df %>%
  wilcox_test(
    formula = pic_correlation ~ pair_type,
    ref.group = "Between",
    p.adjust.method = "BH"
  )
print("Adjusted p-values from pairwise Wilcoxon tests against 'Between' (ECOR dataset):")
print(ecor_stat_test)

Sys.time()
```

```{r}
my_gr_mat<-gr_ecor_df %>%

  select(-strain) %>%
  as.matrix()

# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Compute pairwise cosine similarities between carbon sources
#    from the experimental data (my_gr_mat)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# my_gr_mat is a (strain × carbon source) matrix.
# coop::cosine computes column-wise similarities, so it returns a
# (carbon source × carbon source) cosine similarity matrix.
exp_cos_sim_mat <- coop::cosine(my_gr_mat)
exp_cos_sim_df<-exp_cos_sim_mat %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("carbon1") %>%

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# ECOR dataset: comparison of the Spearman correlation matrix and the
# cosine similarity matrix
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

# Reshape the Spearman correlation matrix to long format (using ecor_matrix_allrep)
ecor_spearman_df <- ecor_matrix_allrep %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("carbon1") %>%
  pivot_longer(-carbon1, names_to = "carbon2", values_to = "spearman_r")

# Reshape the cosine similarity matrix to long format
ecor_cos_sim_df <- exp_cos_sim_mat %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("carbon1") %>%
  pivot_longer(-carbon1, names_to = "carbon2", values_to = "cos_sim")

# Join the two data frames and retain only the upper triangle
ecor_comparison_df <- left_join(ecor_cos_sim_df, ecor_spearman_df,
                                 by = c("carbon1", "carbon2")) %>%
  filter(carbon1 > carbon2)

# Check agreement between cosine similarity and Spearman correlation
cor.test(ecor_comparison_df$cos_sim, ecor_comparison_df$spearman_r,
         method = "spearman")

my_df<-ecor_pair_all[ecor_pair_all$key=="upper",]
my_tmp<-c(carbon_categories,"between")

my_df$pair_category<-factor(my_df$pair_category,levels = my_tmp)
my_df<-my_df[order(my_df$pair_category,decreasing = TRUE),]
my_palette<-c("#0072B2","#E69F00","#56B4E9","#009E73","#8FD926", "grey60")
my_df<-my_df %>%
  left_join(exp_cos_sim_df,by=c("carbon1","carbon2"))
## cosine distance
ggscatter(my_df,
          x="mean_cos_dist",y="exp_cos_sim",alpha=0.8,
          xlab = "Flux-based metabolic distance [-]",
          ylab = "Cosine similarity in growth vectors in ECOR",
          title="ECOR (Pearson correlation)",
          color = "pair_category",palette = my_palette,legend="right",legend.title="",
          shape="pair_category",
          cor.coef = TRUE,cor.method = "pearson",cor.coef.coord = c(0,0.99))+
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 16, 16, 16, 16, 4))+
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = get_breaks(from = -0.4,to = 0.8,by = 0.4),limits = c(-0.4,1))
Sys.time()
```

# 6 Strain-baseline-normalization in ECOR strains (Four reps)
## 6.1 ECOR: growth rate matrix with per-strain mean subtracted (Fig. S6a)
```{r}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Data reshaping: construct the strain × carbon source matrix
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
my_gr_mat <- gr_ecor_df %>%
  select(strain, carbon, mu_max_allrep) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon, values_from = mu_max_allrep)

my_rownames <- my_gr_mat$strain
my_gr_mat <- my_gr_mat %>% 
  select(-strain) %>%
  as.matrix()
rownames(my_gr_mat) <- my_rownames


# Standardize within each carbon source (column-wise z-score)
my_gr_mat<-scale(my_gr_mat)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Remove per-strain mean growth rate (subtract row-wise)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Compute the mean growth rate for each strain (row)
my_means <- rowMeans(my_gr_mat, na.rm = TRUE)

# Use sweep() to subtract each strain's mean from its own row (MARGIN = 1)
my_gr_mat_centered <- sweep(my_gr_mat, 1, my_means, FUN = "-")


# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Compute pairwise Spearman correlations between carbon sources
#    using the mean-centered data
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Spearman correlation matrix across all carbon source pairs
cor_matrix_zznorm <- cor(my_gr_mat_centered, method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

# Reshape to long format
cor_long <- as.data.frame(as.table(cor_matrix_zznorm)) %>%
  setNames(c("carbon1", "carbon2", "correlation")) %>%
  mutate(
    carbon1 = as.character(carbon1),
    carbon2 = as.character(carbon2)
  )

# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Join FBA distance data (my_pair_all) with the correlation results
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
my_pair_all <- carbon_dist_integrated_long %>%
  filter(carbon1 %in% ecor_carbons) %>%
  filter(carbon2 %in% ecor_carbons)

# Drop any pre-existing 'correlation' column before joining the newly computed values
if ("correlation" %in% colnames(my_pair_all)) {
  my_pair_all <- my_pair_all %>% select(-correlation)
}

my_pair_all <- my_pair_all %>%
  left_join(cor_long, by = c("carbon1", "carbon2"))

# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Filter data for visualization and set pair-category factor levels
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
my_df <- my_pair_all %>% filter(key == "upper")

my_tmp <- c(carbon_categories, "between")
my_tmp <- my_tmp[my_tmp %in% my_df$pair_category]
my_df$pair_category <- factor(my_df$pair_category, levels = my_tmp)
my_df <- my_df[order(my_df$pair_category, decreasing = TRUE), ]

my_palette <- c("#0072B2", "#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73", "#8FD926", "grey60")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Scatter plot
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
ggscatter(my_df,
          x="mean_cos_dist",y="correlation",alpha=0.8,
          title="ECOR (Strain's mean normalized)",
          color = "pair_category",palette = my_palette,legend="right",legend.title="",
          shape="pair_category",
          cor.coef = TRUE,cor.method = "spearman",cor.coef.coord = c(0,0.9),cor.coef.size = 6)+
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 16, 16, 16, 16, 4))+
  font("xy.text",size=20)+
  font("legend.text",size=14)+
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = get_breaks(from = -0.8,to = 0.8,by = 0.4),limits = c(-0.8,1))



# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Heatmap
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
## Convert to matrix
my_mat <- my_pair_all %>% select(carbon1,carbon2,correlation) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon2, values_from = correlation) %>%
  column_to_rownames("carbon1") %>%
  as.matrix()

## Sorting
target_order <- sort(rownames(my_mat))
my_mat <- my_mat[target_order, target_order]

## Calc distance
my_dist<- as.dist(1 - my_mat)
my_dist_df<-make_dist_dataframe(my_dist,"ecor")

## Clustering
my_row_cluster <- hclust(my_dist, method = cl_method)
my_label <- data.frame(label=my_row_cluster$labels[my_row_cluster$order])
my_label<-left_join(my_label,carbon_names,by=c("label"="Abb"))
my_colors <- colorRampPalette(rev(brewer.pal(11, "RdBu")))(200)

## Visualization
corrplot(my_mat, 
         method = "color",
         order = "hclust",
         hclust.method = cl_method,
         col = my_colors,
         # cl.lim = c(-1, 1),      # set 0 as white
         tl.srt = 90,
         tl.cex = 1,
         tl.col=my_label$Category_col,
         addgrid.col = 'white',
         type="upper",diag =T)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Dendrogram
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
dend_sbst<-as.dendrogram(my_row_cluster)
current_labels <- labels(dend_sbst)
dend_sbst <- dend_sbst %>% 
  set("labels_cex", 1.5) %>%
  set("labels_colors", my_label$Category_col) %>% 
  set("branches_lwd", 3)
#plot(dend_sbst, main = cl_method)
wrap_elements(~ {
  # Set plot margins: c(bottom, left, top, right).
  # Default is approximately c(5, 4, 4, 2).
  # A large top value (~15) creates space above the dendrogram;
  # trimming the bottom (~2) compensates.
  par(mar = c(4, 4, 15, 2))
  
  # Plot the dendrogram with the enlarged top margin
  plot(dend_sbst, main = cl_method) 
})

Sys.time()
```

## 6.3 Entanglement analysis with flux-based dendrogram
```{r, fig.width=1.5,fig.height=3.5,dpi=300}

# Genetic distance from FBA (7 GEMs consensus) and Phenotypic distance from Growth rates
dist_exp<-as.dist(1 - cor_matrix_zznorm)
my_ins<-rownames(cor_matrix_zznorm)
dist_theory<-mean_carbon_dist_matrix[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------ cosine distance


# Hierarchical clustering using Ward's D2 method
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = cl_method)
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method)

dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# 2. Untangle: Optimize the layout of the two dendrograms to minimize crossings
# Maintaining the topology while rotating branches for better visualization
dl <- dendlist(dend_theory, dend_exp)
dl_untangled <- dendextend::untangle(dl, method = "step2side")

dend_p <- dl_untangled[[1]] # Optimized FBA-based dendrogram
dend_t <- dl_untangled[[2]] # Optimized Growth-based dendrogram


# 3. Create color vectors based on labels
# Retrieve current label order from the left (FBA) dendrogram
current_labels_p <- labels(dend_p)
# Map categories and colors to the current labels
groups_p <- carbon_labels_ordered_cos$Category[match(current_labels_p, carbon_labels_ordered_cos$label)]
col_vector_p <- carbon_labels_ordered_cos$Category_col[match(current_labels_p, carbon_labels_ordered_cos$label)]

# 4. Set label colors
dend_p <- dend_p %>% set("labels_colors", col_vector_p)

# Match Growth-based tree labels with the FBA-based tree's color vector
dend_t <- dend_t %>% 
  set("labels_colors", col_vector_p[match(labels(dend_t), current_labels_p)])

# 5. Draw Tanglegram
# Visualizing the structural similarity between metabolic theory and growth phenotype
tanglegram(dend_p, dend_t,
           common_subtrees_color_lines = FALSE, 
           highlight_distinct_edges = FALSE,
           highlight_branches_lwd = FALSE,
           color_lines = col_vector_p, 
           main_left = "Flux",
           main_right = "Growth",
           lab.cex = 1,
           lwd=2,
           columns_width = c(4, 1.5, 4),
           margin_inner = 3.5,
           margin_outer = 0.5,
           axes = FALSE)


# 6. Permutation Test for Entanglement Score
# Lower entanglement indicates higher structural similarity
actual_ent <- entanglement(dl_untangled) # Entanglement score after untangling

print(Sys.time())
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- if_else(iteration_scale=="large",1000,10)
perm_ent <- numeric(n_perm)

# Fixed theory-based labels
labels_theory <- labels(dend_p)

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # Copy the experimental dendrogram and shuffle labels
  shuffled_dend <- dend_t
  labels(shuffled_dend) <- sample(labels_theory)
  
  # Calculate entanglement for the shuffled pair after untangling
  perm_dends <- dendlist(dend_p, shuffled_dend) %>% 
    dendextend::untangle(method = "step2side")
  perm_ent[i] <- entanglement(perm_dends)
  
  # Progress monitoring
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# 7. Calculate P-value
# P-value = Probability that random entanglement is lower than the observed value
p_val_ent <- sum(perm_ent <= actual_ent) / n_perm

# 8. Visualization of results
hist(perm_ent, main="Permutation Test for Entanglement", 
     xlab="Entanglement Score", xlim=c(0, 1))
abline(v = actual_ent, col = "red", lwd = 2)
cat(sprintf("Actual Entanglement: %.3f\nP-value: %.4f\n", actual_ent, p_val_ent))

Sys.time()
```
## 6.4 Cophenetic correlation with flux-based dendrogram
```{r}
# 1. Prepare distance matrices and initial dendrograms
dist_exp<-as.dist(1 - cor_matrix_zznorm)
my_ins<-rownames(cor_matrix_zznorm)

# Theoretical distance based on 7 GEMs consensus
dist_theory<-mean_carbon_dist_matrix[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------ cosine distance

# Hierarchical clustering
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = cl_method)
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method)

dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# Calculate observed Cophenetic correlation (Spearman)
# This measures how well the tree structure reflects the original distance matrix
actual_cor <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_exp, method = "spearman")

# --- Permutation Test for Cophenetic Correlation ---
print(Sys.time())
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- 1000
perm_results <- data.frame(cor = numeric(n_perm))

# Get original labels (strain names) from the experimental distance matrix
exp_labels <- rownames(as.matrix(dist_exp))

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # 1. Shuffle labels while keeping the underlying matrix structure intact
  dist_shuffled <- dist_exp
  shuffled_labels <- sample(exp_labels)
  
  # Convert to matrix to reassign shuffled names
  temp_mat <- as.matrix(dist_shuffled)
  rownames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  colnames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  
  # 2. Reconstruct dendrogram from the shuffled distance matrix
  hc_shuffled <- hclust(as.dist(temp_mat), method = cl_method)
  dend_shuffled <- as.dendrogram(hc_shuffled)
  
  # 3. Calculate and store the correlation for this permutation
  perm_results$cor[i] <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_shuffled, method = "spearman")
  
  # Progress monitoring
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# --- Statistical Evaluation ---
# P-value: Proportion of permutations where correlation is equal to or greater than observed
p_val_cor <- sum(perm_results$cor >= actual_cor) / n_perm

cat("【Analysis Results】\n")
cat(sprintf("Cophenetic Cor (Spearman): %.3f (p = %.4f)\n", actual_cor, p_val_cor))

# --- Visualization: Cophenetic Correlation Bubble Plot ---
# 1. Prepare data and count overlapping points (ties) for bubble sizing
df_coph <- data.frame(
  Theory = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_theory)),
  Experiment = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_exp))
) %>%
  group_by(Theory, Experiment) %>%
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = 'drop') # 各座標の重複数をカウント

my_txt<-paste("R=",sprintf("%.3f",actual_cor),sep="")

# 2. Plotting with ggscatter
# Bubble size and color intensity are log2-scaled to visualize the density of distance pairs
ggscatter(df_coph, x = "Theory", y = "Experiment",
          size = "count",           # Map count to dot size
          fill = "count",           # Map count to fill color
          color = "black",          # Fix border color to black
          shape = 21,               # Use filled circles with borders
          alpha= 0.8,
          xlab = "Cophenetic distance (Theory)",
          ylab = "Cophenetic distance (Experiment)",
          title = "Cophenetic Correlation (Log-scaled Bubble Size)",
          ylim=c(0,3)) +
  # Apply log2 transformation to size and color to handle the wide range of counts
  scale_size_continuous(trans = "log2", range = c(1, 12), name = "Count (log2)") +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Greys", trans = "log2", direction = 1, name = "Count (log2)")+
  annotate("text", x = 1, y = 2.7, label = my_txt,)

Sys.time()
```

## 6.7 Elbow (Fig. S6c)
```{r, fig.height=4,fig.width=5}
dist_exp<-as.dist(1 - cor_matrix_zznorm)
my_ins<-rownames(cor_matrix_zznorm)
hc_result <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method)

k_range <- 1:10
wss_values <- sapply(k_range, function(k) {
  ct <- cutree(hc_result, k = k)

  sum(sapply(unique(ct), function(cluster) {
    sub_dist <- as.matrix(dist_exp)[ct == cluster, ct == cluster, drop = FALSE]
    sum(sub_dist^2) / (2 * nrow(sub_dist))
  }))
})

elbow_df <- data.frame(k = k_range, wss = wss_values)

p_elbow <- ggplot(elbow_df, aes(x = k, y = wss)) +
  geom_line(color = "black", size = 1.5) +
  geom_point(color = "black", size = 4) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 2, linetype = 2, color = "red") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = k_range) + 
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,15))+

  font("xy.text",size=26)+
  font("xylab",size=26)+

    x = "Number of clusters",
    y = "Total within-cluster\n sum of squares"
```

## 6.7 Concordance with clusters defined from flux-based metabolic distance
```{r,fig.width=4,fig.height=3,dpi=300}

my_df <- as.data.frame(as.table(cor_matrix_zznorm)) %>%
  setNames(c("carbon1", "carbon2", "normalized_correlation")) %>%
  mutate(
    carbon1 = as.character(carbon1),
    carbon2 = as.character(carbon2)
  )

ecor_df_integrated <-ecor_pair_all %>%
  filter (key=="upper") %>%
  left_join(my_df,by=c("carbon1","carbon2"))
ecor_tmp1 <- cbnclust_tbl_fluxbased %>% rename(carbon1 = carbon, cluster1_new = pair_type)
ecor_tmp2 <- cbnclust_tbl_fluxbased %>% rename(carbon2 = carbon, cluster2_new = pair_type)

ecor_df_integrated <- left_join(ecor_df_integrated, ecor_tmp1, by = "carbon1")
ecor_df_integrated <- left_join(ecor_df_integrated, ecor_tmp2, by = "carbon2")


ecor_plot_df <- ecor_df_integrated %>%
  mutate(
    pair_type = case_when(
      cluster1_new == "Cluster 1" & cluster2_new == "Cluster 1" ~ "Cluster 1",
      cluster1_new == "Cluster 2" & cluster2_new == "Cluster 2" ~ "Cluster 2",
      TRUE                                                      ~ "Between"   
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(pair_type = factor(pair_type, levels = c("Cluster 1", "Cluster 2", "Between")))


p_ecor_integrated <- ggboxplot(
  ecor_plot_df,
  x = "pair_type", 
  y = "normalized_correlation",
  ylab = "Normalized correlation [-]", 
  xlab = "",
  add = "jitter", 
  add.params = list(alpha = 0.4, size = 1.5), 
  theme = theme_pubr(base_size = 20)
) +
  font("xy.text", size = 18) +
  font("ylab", size = 18) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-0.8, 1.0, by = 0.4), limits = c(-0.8, 1.3)) +
  stat_pwc(
    method = "wilcox.test",
    ref.group = "Between",      
    p.adjust.method = "BH",     
    label = "p.adj.signif",     
    tip.length = 0,
    bracket.nudge.y = 0.05, 
    hide.ns = TRUE              
  )

print(p_ecor_integrated)


ecor_stat_test <- ecor_plot_df %>%
  wilcox_test(
    formula = normalized_correlation ~ pair_type,
    ref.group = "Between",
    p.adjust.method = "BH"
  )
print("Adjusted p-values from pairwise Wilcoxon tests against 'Between' (ECOR dataset):")
print(ecor_stat_test)

Sys.time()
```

## 6.9 Check whether any strain consistently grows fast across all carbon sources
```{r}
my_gr_mat <- gr_ecor_df %>%
  select(strain, carbon, mu_max_allrep) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon, values_from = mu_max_allrep)

my_rownames <- my_gr_mat$strain
my_gr_mat <- my_gr_mat %>% 
  select(-strain) %>%
  as.matrix()
rownames(my_gr_mat) <- my_rownames

# my_gr_mat: growth rate matrix (strain × carbon source)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Compute within-strain rank variability across carbon sources
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Rank strains within each carbon source (column-wise ranks, 1 to n)
rank_mat <- apply(my_gr_mat, 2, rank)

# Compute the mean and SD of ranks for each strain (row)
strain_rank_stats <- data.frame(
  strain = rownames(rank_mat),
  mean_rank = rowMeans(rank_mat),
  sd_rank = apply(rank_mat, 1, sd)
)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Compute PC1 variance explained via PCA
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
pca_res <- prcomp(scale(my_gr_mat))
pc1_var <- summary(pca_res)$importance[2, 1] * 100

message(sprintf("PC1 (general vigor) variance explained: %.1f%%", pc1_var))

# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Visualize the growth rate distribution per strain (boxplot)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Reshape to long format and plot the spread of growth rates per strain
gr_long_by_strain <- as.data.frame(my_gr_mat) %>%
  rownames_to_column("strain") %>%
  pivot_longer(-strain, names_to = "carbon", values_to = "mu_max_allrep") %>%
  # Order strains by mean rank (ascending: slowest to fastest)
  mutate(strain = factor(strain, levels = strain_rank_stats$strain[order(strain_rank_stats$mean_rank)]))

ggplot(gr_long_by_strain, aes(x = strain, y = mu_max_allrep)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.5, alpha = 0.6, fill = "lightblue") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5, size = 7)) +
  labs(
    title = "Growth rate distribution across carbon sources for each ECOR strain",
    x = "ECOR Strains (ordered by mean growth rate)",
    y = "Maximum growth rate (mu_max)"
  )
```

## 6.10 Visualization
```{r}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Preprocessing (my_gr_mat: raw mu_max matrix, strain × carbon source)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
my_gr_mat <- gr_ecor_df %>%
  select(strain, carbon, mu_max_allrep) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon, values_from = mu_max_allrep)

my_rownames <- my_gr_mat$strain
my_gr_mat <- my_gr_mat %>% 
  select(-strain) %>%
  as.matrix()
rownames(my_gr_mat) <- my_rownames
# Standardize within each carbon source (column-wise z-score: mean 0, SD 1)
z_mat <- scale(my_gr_mat)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Verification: distribution of per-strain mean Z-score (general vigor)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Mean Z-score for each strain (row) — represents the general vigor component
strain_mean_z <- rowMeans(z_mat, na.rm = TRUE)

# SD of Z-scores across carbon sources for each strain
# (magnitude of environment-specific variation)
strain_sd_z <- apply(z_mat, 1, sd, na.rm = TRUE)

df_vigor <- data.frame(
  strain = rownames(z_mat),
  mean_z = strain_mean_z,
  sd_z = strain_sd_z
)

# Reshape to long format for visualization
df_z_long <- as.data.frame(z_mat) %>%
  rownames_to_column("strain") %>%
  pivot_longer(-strain, names_to = "carbon", values_to = "z_score") %>%
  left_join(df_vigor, by = "strain") %>%
  # Order strains by mean_z ascending (lowest to highest general vigor)
  mutate(strain = factor(strain, levels = df_vigor$strain[order(df_vigor$mean_z)]))

# Plot 1A: per-strain Z-score distribution (boxplot) vs. per-strain mean Z-score
p1 <- ggplot(df_z_long, aes(x = strain, y = z_score)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.8, alpha = 0.5, fill = "lightblue", color = "grey30") +
  # Per-strain mean Z-score (red dots)
  geom_point(data = df_vigor, aes(x = factor(strain, levels = levels(df_z_long$strain)), y = mean_z), 
             color = "firebrick", size = 1.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5, size = 6),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "A. Strain Growth Profile Across Carbon Sources (Z-scores)",
    subtitle = "Box: Z-score range across carbons; Red dots: Strain's mean Z-score (General vigor)",
    x = "ECOR Strains (ordered by mean Z-score)",
    y = "Z-score of Growth Rate"
  )

# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Verification: Spearman rank correlation of strain rankings
#    between all carbon source pairs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Compute Spearman rank correlations between all carbon source pairs
carbon_cor_mat <- cor(z_mat, method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

# Extract upper-triangle values (exclude diagonal / self-pairs)
pair_cors <- carbon_cor_mat[upper.tri(carbon_cor_mat)]

df_pair_cors <- data.frame(correlation = pair_cors)

# Plot 2: histogram of pairwise Spearman rank correlations between carbon sources
p2 <- ggplot(df_pair_cors, aes(x = correlation)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.05, fill = "#0072B2", color = "white", alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(pair_cors), color = "firebrick", linetype = "dashed", size = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = mean(pair_cors) - 0.05, y = Inf, vjust = 2, 
           label = sprintf("Mean R = %.2f", mean(pair_cors)), color = "firebrick", fontface = "bold") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    title = "B. Pairwise Carbon Source Rank Correlations Across Strains",
    subtitle = "Spearman rank correlations for all carbon source pairs",
    x = "Pairwise Rank Correlation (Spearman R)",
    y = "Frequency (Number of Carbon Pairs)"
  )

# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Display plots and print numerical summary
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
print(p1)
print(p2)

# Quantitative summary of key findings
cat("\n=== Summary of Key Findings ===\n")
cat(sprintf("1. SD of Z-scores across all carbon sources (overall spread):     %.3f\n",
            sd(df_z_long$z_score)))
cat(sprintf("2. SD of per-strain mean Z-scores (general vigor):                %.3f\n",
            sd(df_vigor$mean_z)))
cat(sprintf("   -> Variance in mean Z-score accounts for only %.1f%% of total Z-score variability.\n",
            (sd(df_vigor$mean_z) / sd(df_z_long$z_score)) * 100))
cat(sprintf("3. Mean Spearman R across all carbon source pairs:                 %.3f\n",
            mean(pair_cors)))
cat(sprintf("   -> Fraction of carbon source pairs with Spearman R <= 0.3:     %.1f%%\n",
            mean(pair_cors < 0.3) * 100))
cat("================================\n")
```
## 6.11 Two-way ANOVA model: residual extraction
```{r}

my_gr_mat <- gr_ecor_df %>%
  select(strain, carbon, mu_max_allrep) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon, values_from = mu_max_allrep)

my_rownames <- my_gr_mat$strain
my_gr_mat <- my_gr_mat %>% 
  select(-strain) %>%
  as.matrix()
rownames(my_gr_mat) <- my_rownames
# my_gr_mat: growth rate matrix (strain × carbon source)

# 1. Reshape to long format and fit a two-way additive ANOVA model
df_long <- as.data.frame(my_gr_mat) %>%
  rownames_to_column("strain") %>%
  pivot_longer(-strain, names_to = "carbon", values_to = "growth_rate")

# 2. Fit the additive main-effects model (strain + carbon source, no interaction term)
fit <- lm(growth_rate ~ strain + carbon, data = df_long)

# 3. Extract residuals (= strain × carbon source specific interaction,
#    i.e., metabolic fitness beyond additive main effects)
df_long$residual <- residuals(fit)

# 4. Reconstruct the residual matrix (strain × carbon source)
res_mat <- df_long %>%
  select(strain, carbon, residual) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon, values_from = residual) %>%
  column_to_rownames("strain")

# 5. Recompute Spearman correlations between carbon sources using the residual
#    matrix, then assess their agreement with pFBA-based distances
residual_carbon_cor <- cor(res_mat, method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

my_map <- residual_carbon_cor %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("carbon1") %>%
  pivot_longer(-carbon1, names_to = "carbon2", values_to = "correlation_rsdl")

my_df<-ecor_pair_all[ecor_pair_all$key=="upper",]
my_tmp<-c(carbon_categories,"between")
my_tmp<-my_tmp[my_tmp %in% my_df$pair_category]
my_df$pair_category<-factor(my_df$pair_category,levels = my_tmp)
my_df<-my_df[order(my_df$pair_category,decreasing = TRUE),]
my_palette<-c("#0072B2","#E69F00","#56B4E9","#009E73","#8FD926", "grey60")
my_df<-my_df %>%
  left_join(my_map,by=c("carbon1","carbon2"))
## cosine distance
ggscatter(my_df,
          x="mean_cos_dist",y="correlation_rsdl",alpha=0.5,
          xlab = "Cosine distance across carbon sources based on pFBA",
          ylab = "Residual Correlation in ECOR",
          title="ECOR (after 2 way ANOVA)",
          color = "pair_category",palette = my_palette,legend="right",legend.title="",
          cor.coef = TRUE,cor.method = "pearson",cor.coef.coord = c(0,-0.4))+
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = get_breaks(from = -0.4,to = 0.8,by = 0.4),limits = c(-0.4,1))
Sys.time()
```

# 7 PCA (Four reps)
## 7.1 ECOR projected onto MA space
```{r,fig.height=2.5,fig.width=2.5, dpi=300}
# A (ECOR)
gr_ecor_com_mat_allrep<-gr_ecor_df %>%
  select(strain,carbon,mu_max_allrep) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon,values_from = mu_max_allrep)
my_rows<-paste("ECOR",gr_ecor_com_mat_allrep$strain,sep="_")
gr_ecor_com_mat_allrep<-gr_ecor_com_mat_allrep %>% select(carbons_ecorma_common) %>% as.matrix()
rownames(gr_ecor_com_mat_allrep)<-my_rows
A_mat<-gr_ecor_com_mat_allrep

# B (MA)
## Anc
gr_ma_anc_df_allrep<-gr_ma_df[gr_ma_df$round==0,] %>% distinct(carbon,.keep_all = TRUE) %>% select(lineage,round,carbon,rel_mu_max_allrep)
gr_ma_anc_df_allrep$name<-"MA_Anc@0"
## Offspring
gr_ma_offsp_df_allrep<-gr_ma_df[gr_ma_df$round!=0,] %>% select(lineage,round,carbon,rel_mu_max_allrep)
gr_ma_offsp_df_allrep$name<-paste(gr_ma_offsp_df_allrep$lineage,sprintf("%02d", gr_ma_offsp_df_allrep$round),sep="@R")
## Anc & Offspring
gr_ma_com_mat_allrep<-bind_rows(gr_ma_anc_df_allrep,gr_ma_offsp_df_allrep) %>% select(name,carbon,rel_mu_max_allrep)
gr_ma_com_mat_allrep<-gr_ma_com_mat_allrep%>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon,values_from = rel_mu_max_allrep)
my_rows<-gr_ma_com_mat_allrep$name
my_rows<-my_rows %>% str_replace_all(pattern = "lineage",replacement = "L")
gr_ma_com_mat_allrep<-gr_ma_com_mat_allrep %>% select(carbons_ecorma_common) %>% as.matrix()
rownames(gr_ma_com_mat_allrep)<-my_rows
B_mat<-gr_ma_com_mat_allrep


# 1. Normalization
A_scaled <- scale(A_mat) # ECOR
B_scaled <- scale(B_mat) # MA

# 2. Extract principal components of (co-)variation across carbon sources
## 2.1. PCA for dataset B
pca_B <- prcomp(B_scaled, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)
## 2.2. PCA for dataset A
pca_A <- prcomp(A_scaled, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)

# 3. Calc. variance explained
## 3.1. for dataset B 
var_B_own <- pca_B$sdev^2 / sum(pca_B$sdev^2) # ratio of total variance
cum_B_own <- cumsum(var_B_own) # cumulative variance
## 3.2. for dataset A
var_A_own <- pca_A$sdev^2 / sum(pca_A$sdev^2)
cum_A_own <- cumsum(var_A_own)

# 4. Generate a dataframe for visualization
pca_summary <- data.frame(
  PC = 1:length(var_B_own),
  Variance = var_B_own,
  Cumulative = cum_B_own
)

# 5. Project A onto the principal component space of B
# Apply the principal component axis (rotation matrix) of B to A_scaled
# A_projected represents principal score (coordinates) of A in B's PC space.
A_projected <- scale(A_mat,center = pca_B$center,scale = pca_B$scale) %*% pca_B$rotation
var_A_on_B <- apply(A_projected, 2, var)
var_explained_A_on_B <- var_A_on_B / sum(var_A_on_B)
cum_A_on_B <- cumsum(var_explained_A_on_B)

# 6. Generate a dataframe for visualization
pca_compare <- data.frame(
  PC = rep(1:length(var_B_own), 2),
  Variance = c(var_B_own, var_explained_A_on_B),
  Cumulative = c(cum_B_own, cum_A_on_B),
  Type = rep(c("MA", "ECOR"), each = length(var_B_own))
)

# dataset B: MA
fviz_pca_biplot(pca_B, repel = TRUE, col.var = "red", col.ind = "grey50",labelsize = 2,arrowsize=0.3)+
  theme_pubr()
# dataset A: ECOR
fviz_pca_biplot(pca_A, repel = TRUE, col.var = "red", col.ind = "grey50",labelsize = 2,arrowsize=0.3)+
  theme_pubr()


#
pc_map<-data.frame(
  PC1=c(pca_B$x[,1],A_projected[,1]),
  PC2=c(pca_B$x[,2],A_projected[,2]),
  PC3=c(pca_B$x[,3],A_projected[,3]),
  Type=c(rep("MA",nrow(pca_B$x)),rep("ECOR",nrow(A_projected))),
  Name=c(rownames(pca_B$x),rownames(A_projected))
)
ggscatter(pc_map[pc_map$Type=="MA",],x="PC1",y="PC2",
          # repel = TRUE,label = "Name",font.label = c(6),
          color="#00BFC4",legend.title="",alpha=0.9)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Proposed null model: within-strain permutation of carbon source labels
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

n_sim <- 1000
n_col <- length(carbons_ecorma_common)
n_row <- nrow(A_mat)

sim_results_perm <- matrix(NA, nrow = n_sim, ncol = n_col)

set.seed(123)

for (i in 1:n_sim) {
  # 1. Randomly shuffle carbon source values (columns) within each strain (row).
  #    This preserves the marginal variance of each carbon source while
  #    destroying the cross-carbon correlation structure.
  A_perm_mat <- t(apply(A_mat, 1, sample))
  colnames(A_perm_mat) <- colnames(A_mat)
  
  # 2. Standardize using the PCA center and scale parameters from dataset B (MA)
  A_perm_scaled <- scale(A_perm_mat, center = pca_B$center, scale = pca_B$scale)
  
  # 3. Project onto the principal component space (rotation matrix) of dataset B (MA)
  A_perm_proj <- A_perm_scaled %*% pca_B$rotation
  
  # 4. Compute cumulative variance explained across PCs
  vars_perm <- apply(A_perm_proj, 2, var)
  sim_results_perm[i, ] <- cumsum(vars_perm) / sum(vars_perm)
}

# 5. Summarize permutation null statistics: mean, 2.5th, and 97.5th percentiles
stats_permAontoB_df <- data.frame(
  PC = 1:n_col,
  Mean = colMeans(sim_results_perm),
  Lower = apply(sim_results_perm, 2, quantile, probs = 0.025),
  Upper = apply(sim_results_perm, 2, quantile, probs = 0.975)
)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Update plot: overlay the permutation null distribution
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
ggline(pca_compare, x = "PC", y = "Cumulative", color = "Type",
       numeric.x.axis = TRUE,
       xlab = "Principal Component of MA", 
       ylab = "Cumulative fraction of \n variance explained",
       legend.title="",
       ylim = c(0, 1.1)) +
  geom_line(data = stats_permAontoB_df, aes(x = PC, y = Mean), color = "gray20", size = 1) +
  geom_ribbon(data = stats_permAontoB_df, aes(x = PC, y = NULL, ymin = Lower, ymax = Upper), alpha = 0.2, fill = "black") +
  geom_point(data = stats_permAontoB_df, aes(x = PC, y = Mean), inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "gray20", size = 2) +
  theme_pubr()



Sys.time()
```
## 7.2 MA projected onto ECOR space
```{r,fig.height=3,fig.width=3,dpi=300}

A_mat<-gr_ecor_com_mat_allrep # ECOR
B_mat<-gr_ma_com_mat_allrep # MA

# 1. Normalization
A_scaled <- scale(A_mat) # ECOR
B_scaled <- scale(B_mat) # MA

## 2.2. PCA for dataset A
pca_A <- prcomp(A_scaled, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)


# 1. Project MA (B_mat) onto the principal component space of ECOR (pca_A)
# Important: Use the scaling parameters (center/scale) from the ECOR PCA
B_projected_on_A <- scale(B_mat, center = pca_A$center, scale = pca_A$scale) %*% pca_A$rotation

# 2. Calculate variance explained by MA within ECOR's PC axes
var_MA_on_A <- apply(B_projected_on_A, 2, var)
var_explained_MA_on_A <- var_MA_on_A / sum(var_MA_on_A)
cum_MA_on_A <- cumsum(var_explained_MA_on_A)

# 3. Create a dataframe for visualization (ECOR as baseline)
pca_compare_rev <- data.frame(

  Cumulative = c(cum_A_own, cum_MA_on_A),
  Type = rep(c("ECOR (Original)", "MA (Projected)"), each = length(var_A_own))
)

# 4. Create a random dataset
# 4.1. Settings
n_row <- nrow(gr_ma_com_mat); n_col <- length(carbons_ecorma_common)
#set.seed(123)

# 4.2. Generate random datasets 10,000 times

for (i in 1:n_sim) {
  # A_rnd_mat
  B_rnd_tmp <- matrix(rnorm(n_row * n_col), nrow = n_row, ncol = n_col)
  # Normalize using the parameters from dataset B (MA)

  B_rnd_proj <- B_rnd_scaled %*% pca_A$rotation
  
  # Compute cumulative explained variance
  vars <- apply(B_rnd_proj, 2, var)
  sim_results[i, ] <- cumsum(vars) / sum(vars)
}

# 3. Compute summary statistics (mean, 2.5th percentile, 97.5th percentile)
stats_randBontoA_df <- data.frame(
  PC = 1:n_col,
  Mean = colMeans(sim_results),
  Lower = apply(sim_results, 2, quantile, probs = 0.025),
  Upper = apply(sim_results, 2, quantile, probs = 0.975)
)

# 4. Visualization: Cumulative Variance Explained
# This shows how much of the MA variance is captured by the major axes of ECOR
ggline(pca_compare_rev, x = "PC", y = "Cumulative", color = "Type",
       numeric.x.axis = TRUE,
       xlab = "Principal Component of ECOR", 
       ylab = "Cumulative fraction of \n variance explained",
       legend.title="",
       ylim=c(0,1))+
  geom_line(data = stats_randBontoA_df,aes(x=PC,y=Mean),color = "gray20", size = 1) +

  geom_point(data = stats_randBontoA_df, aes(x = PC, y = Mean), inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "gray20", size = 2) +

Sys.time()
```

## 8.2 inner wells
```{r}
my_gr_df<-gr_ecor_df %>%
  filter(strain %in% inner_ecor)

my_pair_df<-carbon_dist_integrated_long
my_pair_df<-my_pair_df %>%
  filter(carbon1 %in% ecor_carbons) %>%
  filter(carbon2 %in% ecor_carbons)
my_pair_df$correlation<-NA
i<-1
for (i in 1:nrow(my_pair_df)){
  my_carbon_1<-my_pair_df$carbon1[i]
  my_carbon_2<-my_pair_df$carbon2[i]
  my_df1<-my_gr_df[my_gr_df$carbon==my_carbon_1,]
  my_df1<-my_df1 %>% rename(mu_max_1=mu_max,mu_max_allrep_1=mu_max_allrep)
  my_df2<-my_gr_df[my_gr_df$carbon==my_carbon_2,]
  my_df2<-my_df2 %>% rename(mu_max_2=mu_max,mu_max_allrep_2=mu_max_allrep)
  my_df<-left_join(my_df1,my_df2,by="strain")
  my_res<-cor_test(my_df,vars = "mu_max_1",vars2 = "mu_max_2",method = "spearman")
  my_pair_df$correlation[i]<-my_res$cor
  my_res<-cor_test(my_df,vars = "mu_max_allrep_1",vars2 = "mu_max_allrep_2",method = "spearman")
  my_pair_df$correlation_allrep[i]<-my_res$cor
}

## cosine distance
ggscatter(my_df,
          x="mean_cos_dist",y="correlation_allrep",alpha=0.8,
          title="All GEMs based cosine distance",
          color = "pair_category",palette = my_palette,legend="",legend.title="",
          shape="pair_category",
          cor.coef = TRUE,cor.method = "spearman",cor.coef.coord = c(0,-0.4))+
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 16, 16, 16, 16, 4))+
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = get_breaks(from = -0.4,to = 0.8,by = 0.4),limits = c(-0.4,1))


# Heat map
## Convert to matrix
my_mat <- my_pair_df %>% select(carbon1,carbon2,correlation_allrep) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon2, values_from = correlation_allrep) %>%
  column_to_rownames("carbon1") %>%
  as.matrix()

## Sorting
target_order <- sort(rownames(my_mat))
my_mat <- my_mat[target_order, target_order]

## Calc distance
my_dist<- as.dist(1 - my_mat)
my_dist_df<-make_dist_dataframe(my_dist,"ecor")

## Clustering
my_row_cluster <- hclust(my_dist, method = cl_method)
my_label <- data.frame(label=my_row_cluster$labels[my_row_cluster$order])
my_label<-left_join(my_label,carbon_names,by=c("label"="Abb"))
my_colors <- colorRampPalette(rev(brewer.pal(11, "RdBu")))(200)

## Visualization
corrplot(my_mat, 
         method = "color",
         order = "hclust",
         hclust.method = cl_method,
         col = my_colors,
         # cl.lim = c(-1, 1),      # set 0 as white
         tl.srt = 90,
         tl.cex = 1,
         tl.col=my_label$Category_col,
         addgrid.col = 'white',
         type="upper",diag =T)

# Dendrogram
dend_sbst<-as.dendrogram(my_row_cluster)
current_labels <- labels(dend_sbst)
dend_sbst <- dend_sbst %>% 
  set("labels_cex", 1.5) %>%
  set("labels_colors", my_label$Category_col) %>%

#plot(dend_sbst, main = cl_method)
wrap_elements(~ {
  par(mar = c(4, 4, 15, 2)) 
  plot(dend_sbst, main = cl_method) 
})


# cophenetic analysis

# carbons
my_carbons<-ecor_carbons
my_carbons<-my_carbons[order(my_carbons)]

# Subset ECOR strains
dist_exp<-as.dist(1 - my_mat[my_carbons,my_carbons])

# FBA based
dist_theory<-mean_carbon_dist_matrix[my_carbons,my_carbons] %>% as.dist() # <------ cosine distance

# Hierarchical clustering
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = cl_method)
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method)

dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# Calculate observed Cophenetic correlation (Spearman)
# This measures how well the tree structure reflects the original distance matrix
actual_cor <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_exp, method = "spearman")

# --- Permutation Test for Cophenetic Correlation ---
print(Sys.time())
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- 1000
perm_results <- data.frame(cor = numeric(n_perm))

# Get original labels (strain names) from the experimental distance matrix
exp_labels <- rownames(as.matrix(dist_exp))

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # 1. Shuffle labels while keeping the underlying matrix structure intact
  dist_shuffled <- dist_exp
  shuffled_labels <- sample(exp_labels)
  
  # Convert to matrix to reassign shuffled names
  temp_mat <- as.matrix(dist_shuffled)
  rownames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  colnames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  
  # 2. Reconstruct dendrogram from the shuffled distance matrix
  hc_shuffled <- hclust(as.dist(temp_mat), method = cl_method)
  dend_shuffled <- as.dendrogram(hc_shuffled)
  
  # 3. Calculate and store the correlation for this permutation
  perm_results$cor[i] <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_shuffled, method = "spearman")
  
  # Progress monitoring
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# --- Statistical Evaluation ---
# P-value: Proportion of permutations where correlation is equal to or greater than observed
p_val_cor <- sum(perm_results$cor >= actual_cor) / n_perm

cat("【Analysis Results】\n")
cat(sprintf("Cophenetic Cor (Spearman): %.3f (p = %.4f)\n", actual_cor, p_val_cor))

# --- Visualization: Cophenetic Correlation Bubble Plot ---
# 1. Prepare data and count overlapping points (ties) for bubble sizing
df_coph <- data.frame(
  Theory = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_theory)),
  Experiment = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_exp))
) %>%
  group_by(Theory, Experiment) %>%
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = 'drop') # 各座標の重複数をカウント

my_txt<-paste("R=",sprintf("%.3f",actual_cor),sep="")

# 2. Plotting with ggscatter
# Bubble size and color intensity are log2-scaled to visualize the density of distance pairs
ggscatter(df_coph, x = "Theory", y = "Experiment",
          size = "count",           # Map count to dot size
          fill = "count",           # Map count to fill color
          color = "black",          # Fix border color to black
          shape = 21,               # Use filled circles with borders
          alpha= 0.8,
          xlab = "Cophenetic distance (Theory)",
          ylab = "Cophenetic distance (Experiment)",
          title = "Cophenetic Correlation (Log-scaled Bubble Size)",
          ylim=c(0,3)) +
  # Apply log2 transformation to size and color to handle the wide range of counts
  scale_size_continuous(trans = "log2", range = c(1, 12), name = "Count (log2)") +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Greys", trans = "log2", direction = 1, name = "Count (log2)")+
  annotate("text", x = 1, y = 2.7, label = my_txt,)

Sys.time()
```

```{r}
# The ancestor (Anc) data in gr_ma_df contains no duplicates: each founder
# has exactly one record. That record corresponds to lineage 1, round 0.
# Scrolling through gr_ma_df confirms that lineages 2, 3, and 4 have no
# round-0 data.

ma_pair_unnorm<-carbon_dist_integrated_long
ma_pair_unnorm<-ma_pair_unnorm[(ma_pair_unnorm$carbon1 %in% ma_carbons)&(ma_pair_unnorm$carbon2 %in% ma_carbons),]
ma_pair_unnorm$correlation<-NA
i<-1
for (i in 1:nrow(ma_pair_unnorm)){
  my_carbon_1<-ma_pair_unnorm$carbon1[i]
  my_carbon_2<-ma_pair_unnorm$carbon2[i]
  my_df1<-gr_ma_df[gr_ma_df$carbon==my_carbon_1,]
  my_df1<-my_df1 %>% select(carbon,Anc,lineage,round,mu_max,rel_mu_max,mu_max_allrep,rel_mu_max_allrep) %>%
    rename(mu_max_1=mu_max,rel_mu_max_1=rel_mu_max,mu_max_allrep_1=mu_max_allrep,rel_mu_max_allrep_1=rel_mu_max_allrep)
  my_df2<-gr_ma_df[gr_ma_df$carbon==my_carbon_2,]
  my_df2<-my_df2 %>% select(carbon,Anc,lineage,round,mu_max,rel_mu_max,mu_max_allrep,rel_mu_max_allrep) %>%
    rename(mu_max_2=mu_max,rel_mu_max_2=rel_mu_max,mu_max_allrep_2=mu_max_allrep,rel_mu_max_allrep_2=rel_mu_max_allrep)
  my_df<-left_join(my_df1,my_df2,by=qw(Anc,lineage,round))
  # my_df <- my_df[my_df$round > 0, ]  # Remove Anc — previously active in
  # the preceding chunk, but kept inactive here to include round-0 data
  # per Reviewer 1's suggestion.
  my_res<-cor_test(my_df,vars = "mu_max_1",vars2 = "mu_max_2",method = "spearman")
  ma_pair_unnorm$correlation[i]<-my_res$cor
  my_res<-cor_test(my_df,vars = "mu_max_allrep_1",vars2 = "mu_max_allrep_2",method = "spearman")
  ma_pair_unnorm$correlation_allrep[i]<-my_res$cor
}

my_df<-ma_pair_unnorm[ma_pair_unnorm$key=="upper",]
my_tmp<-c(carbon_categories,"between")
my_tmp<-my_tmp[my_tmp %in% my_df$pair_category]
my_df$pair_category<-factor(my_df$pair_category,levels = my_tmp)

## Scatter plot: flux-based cosine distance vs. evolutionary correlation
ggscatter(my_df,
          x="mean_cos_dist",y="correlation_allrep",alpha=0.8,size=3,
          title="All GEMs based cosine distance",
          color = "pair_category",palette = my_palette,legend="right",legend.title="",
          shape="pair_category",
          xlab="Metabolic distance [-]",ylab="Evolutoinary correlation [-]",
          cor.coef = TRUE,cor.method = "spearman",cor.coef.coord = c(0,0.9),cor.coef.size = 10)+
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 16, 16, 16, 4))+
  font("xy.text", size = 28)+

  font("ylab",size=28)+
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = get_breaks(from = -0.4,to = 0.8,by = 0.4),limits = c(-0.4,1))


## Mantel test
# 1. All carbon sources to be considered
my_carbons <- unique(c(ma_pair_unnorm$carbon1, ma_pair_unnorm$carbon2))

# 2. Rank correlation of growth rates between carbon sources
my_mat1 <- ma_pair_unnorm %>%
  select(carbon1, carbon2, correlation_allrep) %>%
  # Convert carbon1 and carbon2 to factors with shared levels
  # (ensures consistent row/column ordering)）
  mutate(
    carbon1 = factor(carbon1, levels = my_carbons),
    carbon2 = factor(carbon2, levels = my_carbons)
  ) %>%
  # Fill in all pairwise combinations and reshape to wide format
  complete(carbon1, carbon2) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon2, values_from = correlation_allrep) %>%
  # Convert to an R matrix
  column_to_rownames(var = "carbon1") %>%
  as.matrix()

# Convert Spearman r to a dissimilarity measure (1 − r)
my_mat1 <- 1 - my_mat1
my_rows<-rownames(my_mat1)

# 3. Flux-based cosine distance between carbon sources
my_mat2<-mean_carbon_dist_matrix[my_rows,my_rows]

# 4. Mantel test
# (Note: if the correlation matrix already represents dissimilarity,
#  as.dist(my_mat1) can be passed directly without the 1 − r conversion)
set.seed(123)
mantel_result <- mantel(
  xdis = as.dist(my_mat1), 
  ydis = as.dist(my_mat2), 
  method       = "spearman",   # Rank correlation (change to "pearson" if preferred)
  permutations = 999,          # Number of permutations for stable p-value estimation
  na.rm        = TRUE          # Handle diagonal entries and missing values (NA)
)

print(mantel_result)
```

## 9.2 Entanglement score with permutation test (comparison with flux-based metabolic distance)
```{r, fig.width=1.5,fig.height=3.5,dpi=300}

# Genetic distance from FBA (7 GEMs consensus) and Phenotypic distance from Growth rates
dist_exp<-as.dist(1 - ma_matrix_unnorm)
my_ins<-rownames(ma_matrix_unnorm)
dist_theory<-mean_carbon_dist_matrix[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------ cosine distance


# Hierarchical clustering using Ward's D2 method
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = cl_method)
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method)

dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# 2. Untangle: Optimize the layout of the two dendrograms to minimize crossings
# Maintaining the topology while rotating branches for better visualization
dl <- dendlist(dend_theory, dend_exp)
dl_untangled <- dendextend::untangle(dl, method = "step2side")

dend_p <- dl_untangled[[1]] # Optimized FBA-based dendrogram
dend_t <- dl_untangled[[2]] # Optimized Growth-based dendrogram


# 3. Create color vectors based on labels
# Retrieve current label order from the left (FBA) dendrogram
current_labels_p <- labels(dend_p)
# Map categories and colors to the current labels
groups_p <- carbon_labels_ordered_cos$Category[match(current_labels_p, carbon_labels_ordered_cos$label)]
col_vector_p <- carbon_labels_ordered_cos$Category_col[match(current_labels_p, carbon_labels_ordered_cos$label)]

# 4. Set label colors
dend_p <- dend_p %>% set("labels_colors", col_vector_p)

# Match Growth-based tree labels with the FBA-based tree's color vector
dend_t <- dend_t %>% 
  set("labels_colors", col_vector_p[match(labels(dend_t), current_labels_p)])

# 5. Draw Tanglegram
# Visualizing the structural similarity between metabolic theory and growth phenotype
tanglegram(dend_p, dend_t,
           common_subtrees_color_lines = FALSE, 
           highlight_distinct_edges = FALSE,
           highlight_branches_lwd = FALSE,
           color_lines = col_vector_p, 
           main_left = "Flux",
           main_right = "Growth",
           lab.cex = 1,
           lwd=2,
           columns_width = c(4, 1.5, 4),
           margin_inner = 3.5,
           margin_outer = 0.5,
           axes = FALSE)


# 6. Permutation Test for Entanglement Score
# Lower entanglement indicates higher structural similarity
actual_ent <- entanglement(dl_untangled) # Entanglement score after untangling

print(Sys.time())
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- if_else(iteration_scale=="large",1000,10)
perm_ent <- numeric(n_perm)

# Fixed theory-based labels
labels_theory <- labels(dend_p)

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # Copy the experimental dendrogram and shuffle labels
  shuffled_dend <- dend_t
  labels(shuffled_dend) <- sample(labels_theory)
  
  # Calculate entanglement for the shuffled pair after untangling
  perm_dends <- dendlist(dend_p, shuffled_dend) %>% 
    dendextend::untangle(method = "step2side")
  perm_ent[i] <- entanglement(perm_dends)
  
  # Progress monitoring
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# 7. Calculate P-value
# P-value = Probability that random entanglement is lower than the observed value
p_val_ent <- sum(perm_ent <= actual_ent) / n_perm

# 8. Visualization of results
hist(perm_ent, main="Permutation Test for Entanglement", 
     xlab="Entanglement Score", xlim=c(0, 1))
abline(v = actual_ent, col = "red", lwd = 2)
cat(sprintf("Actual Entanglement: %.3f\nP-value: %.4f\n", actual_ent, p_val_ent))

Sys.time()
```
## 9.3 Cophenetic correlation with permutation test (comparison with flux metabolic distance)
```{r}
# 1. Prepare distance matrices and initial dendrograms
dist_exp<-as.dist(1 - ma_matrix_unnorm)
my_ins<-rownames(ma_matrix_unnorm)

# Theoretical distance based on 7 GEMs consensus
dist_theory<-mean_carbon_dist_matrix[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------ cosine distance

# Hierarchical clustering
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = cl_method)
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method)

dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# Calculate observed Cophenetic correlation (Spearman)
# This measures how well the tree structure reflects the original distance matrix
actual_cor <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_exp, method = "spearman")

# --- Permutation Test for Cophenetic Correlation ---
print(Sys.time())
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- 1000
perm_results <- data.frame(cor = numeric(n_perm))

# Get original labels (strain names) from the experimental distance matrix
exp_labels <- rownames(as.matrix(dist_exp))

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # 1. Shuffle labels while keeping the underlying matrix structure intact
  dist_shuffled <- dist_exp
  shuffled_labels <- sample(exp_labels)
  
  # Convert to matrix to reassign shuffled names
  temp_mat <- as.matrix(dist_shuffled)
  rownames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  colnames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  
  # 2. Reconstruct dendrogram from the shuffled distance matrix
  hc_shuffled <- hclust(as.dist(temp_mat), method = cl_method)
  dend_shuffled <- as.dendrogram(hc_shuffled)
  
  # 3. Calculate and store the correlation for this permutation
  perm_results$cor[i] <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_shuffled, method = "spearman")
  
  # Progress monitoring
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# --- Statistical Evaluation ---
# P-value: Proportion of permutations where correlation is equal to or greater than observed
p_val_cor <- sum(perm_results$cor >= actual_cor) / n_perm

cat("【Analysis Results】\n")
cat(sprintf("Cophenetic Cor (Spearman): %.3f (p = %.4f)\n", actual_cor, p_val_cor))

# --- Visualization: Cophenetic Correlation Bubble Plot ---
# 1. Prepare data and count overlapping points (ties) for bubble sizing
df_coph <- data.frame(
  Theory = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_theory)),
  Experiment = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_exp))
) %>%
  group_by(Theory, Experiment) %>%
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = 'drop') # 各座標の重複数をカウント

my_txt<-paste("R=",sprintf("%.3f",actual_cor),sep="")

# 2. Plotting with ggscatter
# Bubble size and color intensity are log2-scaled to visualize the density of distance pairs
ggscatter(df_coph, x = "Theory", y = "Experiment",
          size = "count",           # Map count to dot size
          fill = "count",           # Map count to fill color
          color = "black",          # Fix border color to black
          shape = 21,               # Use filled circles with borders
          alpha= 0.8,
          xlab = "Cophenetic distance (Theory)",
          ylab = "Cophenetic distance (Experiment)",
          title = "Cophenetic Correlation (Log-scaled Bubble Size)",
          ylim=c(0,3)) +
  # Apply log2 transformation to size and color to handle the wide range of counts
  scale_size_continuous(trans = "log2", range = c(1, 12), name = "Count (log2)") +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Greys", trans = "log2", direction = 1, name = "Count (log2)")+
  annotate("text", x = 1, y = 2.7, label = my_txt,)

Sys.time()
```

```{r,fig.height=2.5,fig.width=2.5, dpi=300}
rownames(A_mat)<-my_rows

# B (MA)
## Anc
Banc_df<-gr_ma_df[gr_ma_df$round==0,] %>%
  distinct(carbon,.keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  select(lineage,round,carbon,mu_max_allrep)
Banc_df$name<-"MA_Anc@0"
## Offspring
Boffsp_df<-gr_ma_df[gr_ma_df$round!=0,] %>%

Boffsp_df$name<-paste(Boffsp_df$lineage,sprintf("%02d", Boffsp_df$round),sep="@R")
## Anc & Offspring
B_mat<-bind_rows(Banc_df,Boffsp_df) %>% 
  select(name,carbon,mu_max_allrep)
B_mat<-B_mat %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon,values_from = mu_max_allrep)
my_rows<-B_mat$name
my_rows<-my_rows %>% 
  str_replace_all(pattern = "lineage",replacement = "L")
B_mat<-B_mat %>% 
  select(my_carbons) %>% 
  as.matrix()
rownames(B_mat)<-my_rows


# 1. Normalization
A_scaled <- scale(A_mat) # ECOR
B_scaled <- scale(B_mat) # MA

# 2. Extract principal components of (co-)variation across carbon sources
## 2.1. PCA for dataset B
pca_B <- prcomp(B_scaled, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)
## 2.2. PCA for dataset A
pca_A <- prcomp(A_scaled, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)

# 3. Calc. variance explained
## 3.1. for dataset B 
var_B_own <- pca_B$sdev^2 / sum(pca_B$sdev^2) # ratio of total variance
cum_B_own <- cumsum(var_B_own) # cumulative variance
## 3.2. for dataset A
var_A_own <- pca_A$sdev^2 / sum(pca_A$sdev^2)
cum_A_own <- cumsum(var_A_own)

# 4. Generate a dataframe for visualization
pca_summary <- data.frame(
  PC = 1:length(var_B_own),
  Variance = var_B_own,
  Cumulative = cum_B_own
)

# 5. Project A onto the principal component space of B
# Apply the principal component axis (rotation matrix) of B to A_scaled
# A_projected represents principal score (coordinates) of A in B's PC space.
A_projected <- scale(A_mat,center = pca_B$center,scale = pca_B$scale) %*% pca_B$rotation
var_A_on_B <- apply(A_projected, 2, var)
var_explained_A_on_B <- var_A_on_B / sum(var_A_on_B)
cum_A_on_B <- cumsum(var_explained_A_on_B)

# 6. Generate a dataframe for visualization
pca_compare <- data.frame(
  PC = rep(1:length(var_B_own), 2),
  Variance = c(var_B_own, var_explained_A_on_B),
  Cumulative = c(cum_B_own, cum_A_on_B),
  Type = rep(c("MA", "ECOR"), each = length(var_B_own))
)

# dataset B: MA
fviz_pca_biplot(pca_B, repel = TRUE, col.var = "red", col.ind = "grey50",labelsize = 2,arrowsize=0.3)+
  theme_pubr()
# dataset A: ECOR
fviz_pca_biplot(pca_A, repel = TRUE, col.var = "red", col.ind = "grey50",labelsize = 2,arrowsize=0.3)+
  theme_pubr()


#
pc_map<-data.frame(
  PC1=c(pca_B$x[,1],A_projected[,1]),
  PC2=c(pca_B$x[,2],A_projected[,2]),
  PC3=c(pca_B$x[,3],A_projected[,3]),
  Type=c(rep("MA",nrow(pca_B$x)),rep("ECOR",nrow(A_projected))),
  Name=c(rownames(pca_B$x),rownames(A_projected))
)
ggscatter(pc_map[pc_map$Type=="MA",],x="PC1",y="PC2",
          # repel = TRUE,label = "Name",font.label = c(6),
          color="#00BFC4",legend.title="",alpha=0.9)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Proposed null model: within-strain permutation of carbon source labels
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

n_sim <- 1000
n_col <- length(my_carbons)
n_row <- nrow(A_mat)

sim_results_perm <- matrix(NA, nrow = n_sim, ncol = n_col)

set.seed(123) 

for (i in 1:n_sim) {
  # 1. Randomly shuffle carbon source values (columns) within each strain (row).
  #    This preserves the marginal variance of each carbon source while
  #    destroying the cross-carbon correlation structure.
  A_perm_mat <- t(apply(A_mat, 1, sample))
  colnames(A_perm_mat) <- colnames(A_mat)
  
  # 2. Standardize using the PCA center and scale parameters from dataset B (MA)
  A_perm_scaled <- scale(A_perm_mat, center = pca_B$center, scale = pca_B$scale)
  
  # 3. Project onto the principal component space (rotation matrix) of dataset B (MA)
  A_perm_proj <- A_perm_scaled %*% pca_B$rotation
  
  # 4. Compute cumulative variance explained across PCs
  vars_perm <- apply(A_perm_proj, 2, var)
  sim_results_perm[i, ] <- cumsum(vars_perm) / sum(vars_perm)
}

# 5. Summarize permutation null statistics: mean, 2.5th, and 97.5th percentiles
stats_permAontoB_df <- data.frame(
  PC = 1:n_col,
  Mean = colMeans(sim_results_perm),
  Lower = apply(sim_results_perm, 2, quantile, probs = 0.025),
  Upper = apply(sim_results_perm, 2, quantile, probs = 0.975)
)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Update plot: overlay the permutation null distribution
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
ggline(pca_compare, x = "PC", y = "Cumulative", color = "Type",
       numeric.x.axis = TRUE,
       xlab = "Principal Component of MA", 
       ylab = "Cumulative fraction of \n variance explained",
       legend.title="",
       ylim = c(0, 1.1)) +
  geom_line(data = stats_permAontoB_df, aes(x = PC, y = Mean), color = "gray20", size = 1) +
  geom_ribbon(data = stats_permAontoB_df, aes(x = PC, y = NULL, ymin = Lower, ymax = Upper), alpha = 0.2, fill = "black") +
  geom_point(data = stats_permAontoB_df, aes(x = PC, y = Mean), inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "gray20", size = 2) +
  theme_pubr()

Sys.time()
```

# 10 LMM (linear mixed effects model) in MA
## 10.1 Fixed slope linear mixed-effects model
### 10.1.1 LMM
```{r}
# lineage:       evolutionary lineage label (12 lineages)
# founder:       ancestor strain label (3 strains)
# round:         transfer round (4, 8, 12, …, 28)
# carbon_source: carbon source name (~30 sources)
# rel_growth:    relative growth rate

my_df<-gr_ma_df %>%
  select(lineage,Anc,round,Abb,rel_mu_max) %>%
  rename(founder=Anc,carbon_source=Abb,rel_growth=rel_mu_max) %>%
  filter(round>0)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Function to fit a LMM for each carbon source and extract residuals
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model structure:
#   rel_growth ~ round + founder + (1 | lineage)
# (1 | founder/lineage) is equivalent to (1 | founder) + (1 | founder:lineage).
fit_lmm_and_get_res <- function(df) {
  tryCatch({
    # Treat founder (colony 1–3) as a fixed effect and lineage (1–12) as a random effect
    fit <- lmer(rel_growth ~ round + founder + (1 | lineage), data = df)
    df %>% mutate(residual = residuals(fit))
  }, error = function(e) {
    # Return NA on convergence errors or other failures
    df %>% mutate(residual = NA_real_)
  })
}

# # Robust fallback: for carbon sources that produce a singular fit, switch to
# # an ordinary fixed-effects model lm(rel_growth ~ round + founder + lineage)
# fit_lmm_and_get_res_robust <- function(df) {
#   # 1. First attempt the mixed-effects model
#   fit <- tryCatch({
#     lmer(rel_growth ~ round + founder + (1 | lineage), data = df)
#   }, error = function(e) NULL)
#
#   # 2. Fall back to lm (fixed-effects model) on singular fit or error
#   if (is.null(fit) || isSingular(fit)) {
#     # Use the same fixed effects as lmer (round, founder) and add lineage as a fixed factor
#     fit_lm <- lm(rel_growth ~ round + founder + factor(lineage), data = df)
#     df %>% mutate(residual = residuals(fit_lm))
#   } else {
#     df %>% mutate(residual = residuals(fit))
#   }
# }

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Apply the function to all carbon sources
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
res_df <- my_df %>%
  split(.$carbon_source) %>%
  map_dfr(fit_lmm_and_get_res)

# res_df <- my_df %>%
#   split(.$carbon_source) %>%
#   map_dfr(fit_lmm_and_get_res_robust)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Pivot to a residual matrix (rows: lineage × round, columns: carbon source)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
res_matrix <- res_df %>%
  mutate(sample_id = paste(lineage, round, sep = "_")) %>%
  select(sample_id, carbon_source, residual) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon_source, values_from = residual) %>%
  column_to_rownames("sample_id")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Compute the Spearman correlation matrix and p-values from the residuals
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Compute Spearman r and p-values simultaneously
res_corr <- rcorr(as.matrix(res_matrix), type = "spearman")

# Extract results
corr_matrix_residual <- res_corr$r
p_matrix_residual    <- res_corr$P

# ======================================================================
# 1. Compute the raw correlation matrix (before LMM correction)
# ======================================================================
raw_matrix <- my_df %>%
  mutate(sample_id = paste(lineage, round, sep = "_")) %>%
  select(sample_id, carbon_source, rel_growth) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon_source, values_from = rel_growth) %>%
  column_to_rownames("sample_id")

raw_corr_res <- rcorr(as.matrix(raw_matrix), type = "spearman")

# Reshape the raw correlation matrix to long format
# (exclude self-pairs and duplicate pairs)
raw_corr_df <- raw_corr_res$r %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("carbon_1") %>%
  pivot_longer(-carbon_1, names_to = "carbon_2", values_to = "r_raw") %>%
  filter(carbon_1 < carbon_2)

# ======================================================================
# 2. Reshape the residual correlation matrix to long format
#    (after LMM correction; uses corr_matrix_residual from the previous step)
# ======================================================================
res_corr_df <- corr_matrix_residual %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("carbon_1") %>%
  pivot_longer(-carbon_1, names_to = "carbon_2", values_to = "r_residual") %>%
  filter(carbon_1 < carbon_2)

# Join the raw and residual correlation data frames
comp_df <- left_join(raw_corr_df, res_corr_df, by = c("carbon_1", "carbon_2"))

# Assess structural agreement: Spearman correlation between raw and residual
# correlations (analogous to a Mantel test)
comp_cor <- cor.test(comp_df$r_raw, comp_df$r_residual)
r_val <- round(comp_cor$estimate, 3)
p_val_text <- if(comp_cor$p.value < 0.001) "p < 0.001" else paste0("p = ", round(comp_cor$p.value, 2))

# ======================================================================
# 3. Build the comparison plot with ggplot2
# ======================================================================
p_comparison <- ggplot(comp_df, aes(x = r_raw, y = r_residual)) +
  # 1:1 reference line (represents zero change between raw and corrected correlations)
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50", size = 0.8) +
  # Scatter plot of raw vs. residual correlations
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, color = "#2b5c8f", size = 2.5) +
  # geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "#d95f02", se = FALSE, size = 1) +
  # Annotate with Spearman r and p-value
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = -Inf, y = Inf,
    label = paste0("  Spearman r = ", r_val, "\n  ", p_val_text),
    hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.3,
    size = 4.5, fontface = "bold", color = "black"
  ) +
  # Fix both axes to [-1, 1]
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(-1, 1), ylim = c(-1, 1)) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14, hjust = 0.5),
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Comparison of MA Correlations",
    x = "Raw MA Correlation (Spearman r)",
    y = "Residual Correlation (LMM Corrected)"
  )
print(p_comparison)
Sys.time()
```
