### 10.1.6 Lag-1 autocorrelation of residual change vectors
```{r}
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Compute the change vector Δϵ for each lineage and each step
#    (difference between consecutive rounds)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
delta_df <- res_df %>%
  select(lineage, founder, round, carbon_source, residual) %>%
  arrange(lineage, carbon_source, round) %>%
  group_by(lineage, founder, carbon_source) %>%
  mutate(delta_res = residual - lag(residual)) %>% # Round-to-round change: Δϵ_t = ϵ_t − ϵ_{t−4}
  filter(!is.na(delta_res)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Helper function to compute cosine similarity between two vectors
calc_cosine <- function(v1, v2) {
  sum(v1 * v2) / (sqrt(sum(v1^2)) * sqrt(sum(v2^2)))
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Cosine similarity of consecutive step pairs within the same lineage
#    (observed values)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Reshape change vectors for each lineage and round to wide format
delta_wide <- delta_df %>%
  mutate(step = paste0(round - 4, "to", round)) %>% # 例: "4to8"
  select(lineage, founder, step, carbon_source, delta_res) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon_source, values_from = delta_res)

# Define ordered consecutive step pairs:
# "4to8", "8to12", "12to16", "16to20", "20to24", "24to28"
steps <- unique(delta_wide$step)
step_pairs <- tibble(
  step1 = steps[-length(steps)],
  step2 = steps[-1]
)

# Extract consecutive step pairs (e.g., "4to8" and "8to12") and
# compute cosine similarity for each pair within the same lineage
obs_results <- delta_wide %>%
  group_by(lineage, founder) %>%
  nest() %>%
  # Explicitly use purrr::map to avoid namespace conflicts
  mutate(cosine_sims = purrr::map(data, function(df_lineage) {
    step_pairs %>%
      rowwise() %>%
      mutate(cos_sim = {
        v1 <- df_lineage %>% filter(step == step1) %>% select(-step) %>% unlist()
        v2 <- df_lineage %>% filter(step == step2) %>% select(-step) %>% unlist()
        if (length(v1) > 0 && length(v2) > 0) calc_cosine(v1, v2) else NA_real_
      })
  })) %>%
  select(-data) %>%
  unnest(cosine_sims) %>%
  filter(!is.na(cos_sim))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Generate the null model: cosine similarities from shuffled
#    cross-lineage pairs
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
set.seed(42)
n_perm <- 1000

null_cos_sims <- numeric(n_perm)

for (i in 1:n_perm) {
  # Randomly select two distinct lineages and a random adjacent step pair,
  # then compute cosine similarity between their change vectors
  l1 <- sample(unique(delta_wide$lineage), 1)
  l2 <- sample(setdiff(unique(delta_wide$lineage), l1), 1)
  
  pair_idx <- sample(seq_len(nrow(step_pairs)), 1)
  s1 <- step_pairs$step1[pair_idx]
  s2 <- step_pairs$step2[pair_idx]
  
  v1 <- delta_wide %>% filter(lineage == l1, step == s1) %>% select(-lineage, -founder, -step) %>% unlist()
  v2 <- delta_wide %>% filter(lineage == l2, step == s2) %>% select(-lineage, -founder, -step) %>% unlist()
  
  if (length(v1) > 0 && length(v2) > 0) {
    null_cos_sims[i] <- calc_cosine(v1, v2)
  }
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Statistical test: observed vs. null model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Wilcoxon rank-sum test (two-sided)
test_res <- wilcox.test(obs_results$cos_sim, null_cos_sims, alternative = "two.sided")

cat("=== Analysis Results ===\n")
cat("Mean cosine similarity (Observed):      ", mean(obs_results$cos_sim), "\n")
cat("Mean cosine similarity (Null/Shuffled): ", mean(null_cos_sims),       "\n")
cat("Wilcoxon p-value:                       ", test_res$p.value,          "\n")
Sys.time()
```

## 10.2. Random-slope LMM without ancestor normalization or log transformation (Four reps)
### 10.2.1 Fitting the LMM
```{r}
my_df<-gr_ma_df %>%
  select(lineage,Anc,round,Abb,mu_max_allrep) %>%
  rename(founder=Anc,carbon_source=Abb,growth_allrep=mu_max_allrep) %>%
  filter(round>0)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Fit the random-slope model and extract slopes and summary statistics
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model: growth ~ round + founder + (1 + round | lineage)
# (1 + round | lineage) estimates per-lineage random effects for both the
# intercept and the slope of round.

fit_random_slope_lmm_allrep <- function(df) {
  cs_name <- unique(df$carbon_source)
  
  # 1. Fit the LMM (fall back to lm on convergence error)
  fit <- tryCatch({
    lmer(growth_allrep ~ round + founder + (1 + round | lineage), data = df)
  }, error = function(e) NULL)
  
  # Handle singular fit or convergence failure
  if (is.null(fit) || isSingular(fit)) {
    # If the random slope cannot be estimated, substitute a fixed-effects lm
    # with a lineage × round interaction term
    fit_lm <- lm(growth_allrep ~ round * factor(lineage) + founder, data = df)
    
    # Extract per-lineage slopes from lm (main effect of round + interaction term)
    coefs <- summary(fit_lm)$coefficients
    base_slope <- coefs["round", "Estimate"]
    
    slopes_df <- tibble(lineage = paste0("lineage", 1:12)) %>%
      mutate(
        random_slope = map_dbl(lineage, function(l) {
          term <- paste0("round:factor(lineage)", l)
          if (term %in% rownames(coefs)) base_slope + coefs[term, "Estimate"] else base_slope
        })
      )
    
    res_df <- df %>% mutate(residual = residuals(fit_lm))
    var_slope <- var(slopes_df$random_slope)
    p_val_slope <- NA_real_ # Skip the likelihood ratio test when falling back to lm
    
    # Approximate R² for the lm fallback
    r2_cond <- cor(df$growth_allrep, predict(fit_lm))^2
    r2_marg <- NA_real_ # Marginal R² is not separable for the lm fallback (interaction included)
    
    
  } else {
    # Normal fit: extract random slopes
    ranef_res <- ranef(fit)$lineage
    # Per-lineage effective slope = population-level slope (β₁) + lineage-specific deviation (b_j)
    fix_slope <- fixef(fit)["round"]
    
    slopes_df <- ranef_res %>%
      rownames_to_column("lineage") %>%
      mutate(random_slope = fix_slope + round) %>%
      select(lineage, random_slope)
    
    res_df <- df %>% mutate(residual = residuals(fit))
    
    # Variance of the random slope (σ²_slope): spread of evolutionary trends across lineages
    vc <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(fit))
    var_slope <- vc %>% filter(grp == "lineage", var1 == "round") %>% pull(vcov)
    if (length(var_slope) == 0) var_slope <- 0
    
    # Test significance of the random slope: likelihood ratio test against a
    # random-intercept-only model
    fit_null <- lmer(growth_allrep ~ round + founder + (1 | lineage), data = df, REML = FALSE)
    fit_full <- lmer(growth_allrep ~ round + founder + (1 + round | lineage), data = df, REML = FALSE)
    lrt <- anova(fit_null, fit_full)
    p_val_slope <- lrt$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2]
    
    # Compute approximate R² for the lmer fit
    pred_cond <- predict(fit)                    # Fixed + random effects (conditional predictions)
    pred_marg <- predict(fit, re.form = NA)      # Fixed effects only (marginal predictions)
    
    r2_cond <- cor(df$growth_allrep, pred_cond)^2   # Approximate conditional R²
    r2_marg <- cor(df$growth_allrep, pred_marg)^2   # Approximate marginal R²
    
  }
  
  return(list(
    res_df = res_df,
    slopes_df = slopes_df %>% mutate(carbon_source = cs_name),
    var_summary = tibble(
      carbon_source = cs_name, 
      var_slope = var_slope, 
      p_val_slope = p_val_slope,
      r2_cond = r2_cond,  
      r2_marg = r2_marg   
      )
  ))
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Apply the function to all carbon sources
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
lmm_results_allrep <- my_df %>%
  split(.$carbon_source) %>%
  purrr::map(fit_random_slope_lmm_allrep)

# A. Reconstruct the residual data frame
res_df_rs_allrep <- map_dfr(lmm_results_allrep, ~ .x$res_df)

# 1. Build the new residual matrix
res_matrix_rs_allrep <- res_df_rs_allrep %>%
  mutate(sample_id = paste(lineage, round, sep = "_")) %>%
  select(sample_id, carbon_source, residual) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon_source, values_from = residual) %>%
  column_to_rownames("sample_id")

# 2. Compute the Spearman residual correlation matrix
res_corr_rs_allrep <- Hmisc::rcorr(as.matrix(res_matrix_rs_allrep), type = "spearman")
corr_matrix_residual_rs_allrep <- res_corr_rs_allrep$r


# B. Extract the evolutionary rate matrix (per-lineage slope b_{jk},
#    carbon source × lineage)
slopes_df_all_allrep <- map_dfr(lmm_results_allrep, ~ .x$slopes_df)

slope_matrix_allrep <- slopes_df_all_allrep %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon_source, values_from = random_slope) %>%
  column_to_rownames("lineage")

# C. Variance summary: divergence of evolutionary trajectories
#    (spread of slopes across lineages) per carbon source
var_summary_df <- map_dfr(lmm_results_allrep, ~ .x$var_summary)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Inspect analysis outputs
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# ① Check whether the divergence of evolutionary trends across lineages
#   (random slope variance) is significant for each carbon source
cat("=== Random slope variance per carbon source (divergence of evolutionary trends) ===\n")
print(head(var_summary_df))
print(var_summary_df,n=22)

# ② Correlation analysis of per-lineage evolutionary slope vectors
#    (12 lineages × ~30 carbon sources)
#    (Do lineages that decline on one carbon source tend to decline / rise on others?)
slope_corr_allrep <- rcorr(as.matrix(slope_matrix_allrep), type = "spearman")
corr_matrix_slope_allrep <- slope_corr_allrep$r
p_matrix_slope_allrep    <- slope_corr_allrep$P
Sys.time()
```

```{r}

# Helper function to compute cosine similarity between two vectors
calc_cosine <- function(v1, v2) {
  sum(v1 * v2) / (sqrt(sum(v1^2)) * sqrt(sum(v2^2)))
}

  step1 = steps[-length(steps)],
  step2 = steps[-1]
)

  nest() %>%
  # Explicitly use purrr::map to avoid namespace conflicts
  mutate(cosine_sims = purrr::map(data, function(df_lineage) {

      rowwise() %>%
      mutate(cos_sim = {
        v1 <- df_lineage %>% filter(step == step1) %>% select(-step) %>% unlist()
        v2 <- df_lineage %>% filter(step == step2) %>% select(-step) %>% unlist()
        if (length(v1) > 0 && length(v2) > 0) calc_cosine(v1, v2) else NA_real_
      })
  })) %>%
  select(-data) %>%
  unnest(cosine_sims) %>%
  filter(!is.na(cos_sim))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Generate the null model: cosine similarities from shuffled
#    cross-lineage pairs
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
set.seed(42)
n_perm <- 1000

null_cos_sims <- numeric(n_perm)

for (i in 1:n_perm) {

  # then compute cosine similarity between their change vectors

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Wilcoxon rank-sum test (two-sided)
test_res <- wilcox.test(obs_results$cos_sim, null_cos_sims, alternative = "two.sided")

cat("=== Analysis Results ===\n")
cat("Mean cosine similarity (Observed):      ", mean(obs_results$cos_sim), "\n")
cat("Mean cosine similarity (Null/Shuffled): ", mean(null_cos_sims),       "\n")
cat("Wilcoxon p-value:                       ", test_res$p.value,          "\n")
Sys.time()
```

### 10.2.9 Similarity of pairwise carbon source correlation structure before and after LMM correction
```{r}
my_df<-gr_ma_df %>%
  select(lineage,Anc,round,Abb,mu_max_allrep) %>%
  rename(founder=Anc,carbon_source=Abb,growth_allrep=mu_max_allrep) %>%
  filter(round>0)
# ======================================================================
# 1. Compute the raw correlation matrix (before LMM correction)
# ======================================================================
raw_matrix <- my_df %>%
  mutate(sample_id = paste(lineage, round, sep = "_")) %>%
  select(sample_id, carbon_source, growth_allrep) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon_source, values_from = growth_allrep) %>%
  column_to_rownames("sample_id")

raw_corr_res <- rcorr(as.matrix(raw_matrix), type = "spearman")

# Reshape the raw correlation matrix to long format
# (exclude self-pairs and duplicate pairs)
raw_corr_df <- raw_corr_res$r %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("carbon_1") %>%
  pivot_longer(-carbon_1, names_to = "carbon_2", values_to = "r_raw") %>%
  filter(carbon_1 < carbon_2)

# ======================================================================
# 2. Reshape the residual correlation matrix to long format
#    (after LMM correction; uses corr_matrix_residual_rs from the previous step)
# ======================================================================
res_corr_df <- corr_matrix_residual_rs_allrep %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("carbon_1") %>%
  pivot_longer(-carbon_1, names_to = "carbon_2", values_to = "r_residual") %>%
  filter(carbon_1 < carbon_2)


# Join the raw and residual correlation data frames
comp_df <- left_join(raw_corr_df, res_corr_df, by = c("carbon_1", "carbon_2"))

# Assess structural agreement: Spearman correlation between raw and residual
# correlations (analogous to a Mantel test)
comp_cor <- cor.test(comp_df$r_raw, comp_df$r_residual)
r_val <- round(comp_cor$estimate, 3)
p_val_text <- if(comp_cor$p.value < 0.001) "p < 0.001" else paste0("p = ", round(comp_cor$p.value, 2))

# ======================================================================
# 3. Build the comparison plot with ggplot2
# ======================================================================
p_comparison <- ggplot(comp_df, aes(x = r_raw, y = r_residual)) +
  # 1:1 reference line (represents zero change between raw and corrected correlations)
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50", size = 0.8) +
  # Scatter plot of raw vs. residual correlations
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, color = "#2b5c8f", size = 2.5) +
  # geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "#d95f02", se = FALSE, linewidth = 1) +  # trendline (disabled)
  # Annotate with Spearman r and p-value
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = -Inf, y = Inf,
    label = paste0("  Spearman r = ", r_val, "\n  ", p_val_text),
    hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.3,
    size = 4.5, fontface = "bold", color = "black"
  ) +
  # Fix both axes to [-1, 1]
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(-1, 1), ylim = c(-1, 1)) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14, hjust = 0.5),
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Comparison of MA Correlations",
    x = "Raw MA Correlation (Spearman r)",
    y = "Residual Correlation (LMM Corrected)"
  )
print(p_comparison)
Sys.time()
```
### 10.2.10 Comparison with theoretical dendrogram
#### 10.2.10.1 Flux-based metabolic distance
##### 10.2.10.1.1 Entanglement score with permutation test
```{r, fig.width=1.5,fig.height=3.5,dpi=300}

# Flux-based distance and Phenotypic distance from Growth rates
dist_exp<-as.dist(1 - ma_matrix_lmmrs_allrep)
my_ins<-rownames(ma_matrix_lmmrs_allrep)
dist_theory<-mean_carbon_dist_matrix[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------ cosine distance


# Hierarchical clustering using Ward's D2 method
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = cl_method)
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method)

dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# 2. Untangle: Optimize the layout of the two dendrograms to minimize crossings
# Maintaining the topology while rotating branches for better visualization
dl <- dendlist(dend_theory, dend_exp)
dl_untangled <- dendextend::untangle(dl, method = "step2side")

dend_p <- dl_untangled[[1]] # Optimized FBA-based dendrogram
dend_t <- dl_untangled[[2]] # Optimized Growth-based dendrogram


# 3. Create color vectors based on labels
# Retrieve current label order from the left (FBA) dendrogram
current_labels_p <- labels(dend_p)
# Map categories and colors to the current labels
groups_p <- carbon_labels_ordered_cos$Category[match(current_labels_p, carbon_labels_ordered_cos$label)]
col_vector_p <- carbon_labels_ordered_cos$Category_col[match(current_labels_p, carbon_labels_ordered_cos$label)]

# 4. Set label colors
dend_p <- dend_p %>% set("labels_colors", col_vector_p)

# Match Growth-based tree labels with the FBA-based tree's color vector
dend_t <- dend_t %>% 
  set("labels_colors", col_vector_p[match(labels(dend_t), current_labels_p)])

# 5. Draw Tanglegram
# Visualizing the structural similarity between metabolic theory and growth phenotype
tanglegram(dend_p, dend_t,
           common_subtrees_color_lines = FALSE, 
           highlight_distinct_edges = FALSE,
           highlight_branches_lwd = FALSE,
           color_lines = col_vector_p, 
           main_left = "Flux",
           main_right = "Growth",
           lab.cex = 1,
           lwd=2,
           columns_width = c(4, 1.5, 4),
           margin_inner = 3.5,
           margin_outer = 0.5,
           axes = FALSE)


# 6. Permutation Test for Entanglement Score
# Lower entanglement indicates higher structural similarity
actual_ent <- entanglement(dl_untangled) # Entanglement score after untangling

print(Sys.time())
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- if_else(iteration_scale=="large",1000,10)
perm_ent <- numeric(n_perm)

# Fixed theory-based labels
labels_theory <- labels(dend_p)

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # Copy the experimental dendrogram and shuffle labels
  shuffled_dend <- dend_t
  labels(shuffled_dend) <- sample(labels_theory)
  
  # Calculate entanglement for the shuffled pair after untangling
  perm_dends <- dendlist(dend_p, shuffled_dend) %>% 
    dendextend::untangle(method = "step2side")
  perm_ent[i] <- entanglement(perm_dends)
  
  # Progress monitoring
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# 7. Calculate P-value
# P-value = Probability that random entanglement is lower than the observed value
p_val_ent <- sum(perm_ent <= actual_ent) / n_perm

# 8. Visualization of results
hist(perm_ent, main="Permutation Test for Entanglement", 
     xlab="Entanglement Score", xlim=c(0, 1))
abline(v = actual_ent, col = "red", lwd = 2)
cat(sprintf("Actual Entanglement: %.3f\nP-value: %.4f\n", actual_ent, p_val_ent))

Sys.time()
```
##### 10.2.10.1.2 Cophenetic correlation with permutation test
```{r}
# 1. Prepare distance matrices and initial dendrograms
dist_exp<-as.dist(1 - ma_matrix_lmmrs_allrep)
my_ins<-rownames(ma_matrix_lmmrs_allrep)

# Flux-based metabolic distance
dist_theory<-mean_carbon_dist_matrix[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------ cosine distance

# Hierarchical clustering
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = cl_method)
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method)

dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# Calculate observed Cophenetic correlation (Spearman)
# This measures how well the tree structure reflects the original distance matrix
actual_cor <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_exp, method = "spearman")

# --- Permutation Test for Cophenetic Correlation ---
print(Sys.time())
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- 1000
perm_results <- data.frame(cor = numeric(n_perm))

# Get original labels (strain names) from the experimental distance matrix
exp_labels <- rownames(as.matrix(dist_exp))

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # 1. Shuffle labels while keeping the underlying matrix structure intact
  dist_shuffled <- dist_exp
  shuffled_labels <- sample(exp_labels)
  
  # Convert to matrix to reassign shuffled names
  temp_mat <- as.matrix(dist_shuffled)
  rownames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  colnames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  
  # 2. Reconstruct dendrogram from the shuffled distance matrix
  hc_shuffled <- hclust(as.dist(temp_mat), method = cl_method)
  dend_shuffled <- as.dendrogram(hc_shuffled)
  
  # 3. Calculate and store the correlation for this permutation
  perm_results$cor[i] <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_shuffled, method = "spearman")
  
  # Progress monitoring
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# --- Statistical Evaluation ---
# P-value: Proportion of permutations where correlation is equal to or greater than observed
p_val_cor <- sum(perm_results$cor >= actual_cor) / n_perm

cat("【Analysis Results】\n")
cat(sprintf("Cophenetic Cor (Spearman): %.3f (p = %.4f)\n", actual_cor, p_val_cor))

# --- Visualization: Cophenetic Correlation Bubble Plot ---
# 1. Prepare data and count overlapping points (ties) for bubble sizing
df_coph <- data.frame(
  Theory = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_theory)),
  Experiment = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_exp))
) %>%
  group_by(Theory, Experiment) %>%
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = 'drop') # 各座標の重複数をカウント

my_txt<-paste("R=",sprintf("%.3f",actual_cor),sep="")

# 2. Plotting with ggscatter
# Bubble size and color intensity are log2-scaled to visualize the density of distance pairs
ggscatter(df_coph, x = "Theory", y = "Experiment",
          size = "count",           # Map count to dot size
          fill = "count",           # Map count to fill color
          color = "black",          # Fix border color to black
          shape = 21,               # Use filled circles with borders
          alpha= 0.8,
          xlab = "Cophenetic distance (Theory)",
          ylab = "Cophenetic distance (Experiment)",
          title = "Cophenetic Correlation (Log-scaled Bubble Size)",
          ylim=c(0,3)) +
  # Apply log2 transformation to size and color to handle the wide range of counts
  scale_size_continuous(trans = "log2", range = c(1, 12), name = "Count (log2)") +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Greys", trans = "log2", direction = 1, name = "Count (log2)")+
  annotate("text", x = 1, y = 2.7, label = my_txt,)

Sys.time()
```

```{r,fig.width=4,fig.height=3,dpi=300}
ma_df_integrated <- left_join(ma_df_integrated, ma_tmp2, by = "carbon2")


# ==========================================
# 2. Data wrangling: define three pair-type groups with "Between" as reference
# ==========================================
ma_plot_df <- ma_df_integrated %>%
  mutate(
    pair_type = case_when(
      cluster1_new == "Cluster 1" & cluster2_new == "Cluster 1" ~ "Cluster 1", # Both in Cluster 1
      cluster1_new == "Cluster 2" & cluster2_new == "Cluster 2" ~ "Cluster 2", # Both in Cluster 2
      TRUE                                                      ~ "Between"   # All other (cross-cluster) pairs
    )
  ) %>%
  # Fix factor level order for plotting and testing: Cluster 1, Cluster 2, Between
  mutate(pair_type = factor(pair_type, levels = c("Cluster 1", "Cluster 2", "Between")))


# ==========================================
# 3. Visualization and statistical testing
# ==========================================
# Draw a boxplot of LMM-corrected MA correlations (correlation)
p_ma_integrated <- ggboxplot(
  ma_plot_df,
  x = "pair_type", 
  y = "correlation_rsdl",
  ylab = "Residual correlation [-]", # consistent with previous MA axis label
  xlab = "",
  add = "jitter", 
  add.params = list(alpha = 0.4, size = 1.5), 
  theme = theme_pubr(base_size = 20)
) +
  font("xy.text", size = 18) +
  font("ylab", size = 18) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-0.4, 1.0, by = 0.4), limits = c(-0.4, 1.3)) +
  # Add pairwise Wilcoxon tests against "Between" as the reference group
  stat_pwc(
    method = "wilcox.test",
    ref.group = "Between",      
    p.adjust.method = "BH",     
    label = "p.adj.signif",     
    tip.length = 0,
    bracket.nudge.y = 0.05, 
    hide.ns = TRUE              
  )

print(p_ma_integrated)


# ==========================================
# 4. Print detailed statistical results to the console (for verification)
# ==========================================
ma_stat_test <- ma_plot_df %>%
  wilcox_test(
    formula = correlation ~ pair_type,
    ref.group = "Between",
    p.adjust.method = "BH"
  )
print("Adjusted p-values from pairwise Wilcoxon tests against 'Between' (MA dataset, LMM corrected):")
print(ma_stat_test)

Sys.time()
```

### 10.2.14 PCA
```{r,fig.height=2.5,fig.width=2.5, dpi=300}
# Define common carbon sources between MA and ECOR
my_carbons<-ma_carbons[ma_carbons %in% ecor_carbons]
my_carbons<-my_carbons[order(my_carbons)]

# A (ECOR)
A_mat<-gr_ecor_df %>%
  select(strain,carbon,mu_max_allrep) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon,values_from = mu_max_allrep)
my_rows<-paste("ECOR",A_mat$strain,sep="_")
A_mat<-A_mat %>% select(my_carbons) %>% as.matrix()
rownames(A_mat)<-my_rows

# B (MA)
B_mat <- res_df_rs_allrep %>%
  rename(carbon = carbon_source) %>% 
  mutate(name = str_c(str_replace(lineage, "lineage", "L"), "@R", sprintf("%02d", round))) %>%
  select(name, carbon, residual) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon, values_from = residual) %>%
  column_to_rownames("name") %>%
  select(all_of(my_carbons)) %>%
  as.matrix()

# 1. Normalization
A_scaled <- scale(A_mat) # ECOR
B_scaled <- scale(B_mat) # MA

# 2. Extract principal components of (co-)variation across carbon sources
## 2.1. PCA for dataset B
pca_B <- prcomp(B_scaled, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)
## 2.2. PCA for dataset A
pca_A <- prcomp(A_scaled, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)

# 3. Calc. variance explained
## 3.1. for dataset B 
var_B_own <- pca_B$sdev^2 / sum(pca_B$sdev^2) # ratio of total variance
cum_B_own <- cumsum(var_B_own) # cumulative variance
## 3.2. for dataset A
var_A_own <- pca_A$sdev^2 / sum(pca_A$sdev^2)
cum_A_own <- cumsum(var_A_own)

# 4. Generate a dataframe for visualization
pca_summary <- data.frame(
  PC = 1:length(var_B_own),
  Variance = var_B_own,
  Cumulative = cum_B_own
)

# 5. Project A onto the principal component space of B
# Apply the principal component axis (rotation matrix) of B to A_scaled
# A_projected represents principal score (coordinates) of A in B's PC space.
A_projected <- scale(A_mat,center = pca_B$center,scale = pca_B$scale) %*% pca_B$rotation
var_A_on_B <- apply(A_projected, 2, var)
var_explained_A_on_B <- var_A_on_B / sum(var_A_on_B)
cum_A_on_B <- cumsum(var_explained_A_on_B)

# 6. Generate a dataframe for visualization
pca_compare <- data.frame(
  PC = rep(1:length(var_B_own), 2),
  Variance = c(var_B_own, var_explained_A_on_B),
  Cumulative = c(cum_B_own, cum_A_on_B),
  Type = rep(c("MA", "ECOR"), each = length(var_B_own))
)

# dataset B: MA
fviz_pca_biplot(pca_B, repel = TRUE, col.var = "red", col.ind = "grey50",labelsize = 2,arrowsize=0.3)+
  theme_pubr()
# dataset A: ECOR
fviz_pca_biplot(pca_A, repel = TRUE, col.var = "red", col.ind = "grey50",labelsize = 2,arrowsize=0.3)+
  theme_pubr()


#
pc_map<-data.frame(
  PC1=c(pca_B$x[,1],A_projected[,1]),
  PC2=c(pca_B$x[,2],A_projected[,2]),
  PC3=c(pca_B$x[,3],A_projected[,3]),
  Type=c(rep("MA",nrow(pca_B$x)),rep("ECOR",nrow(A_projected))),
  Name=c(rownames(pca_B$x),rownames(A_projected))
)
ggscatter(pc_map[pc_map$Type=="MA",],x="PC1",y="PC2",
          # repel = TRUE,label = "Name",font.label = c(6),
          color="#00BFC4",legend.title="",alpha=0.9)



# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Proposed null model: within-strain permutation of carbon source labels
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

n_sim <- 1000
n_col <- length(my_carbons)
n_row <- nrow(A_mat)

sim_results_perm <- matrix(NA, nrow = n_sim, ncol = n_col)

set.seed(123) 

for (i in 1:n_sim) {
  # 1. Randomly shuffle carbon source values (columns) within each strain (row).
  #    This preserves the marginal variance of each carbon source while
  #    destroying the cross-carbon correlation structure.
  A_perm_mat <- t(apply(A_mat, 1, sample))
  colnames(A_perm_mat) <- colnames(A_mat)
  
  # 2. Standardize using the PCA center and scale parameters from dataset B (MA)
  A_perm_scaled <- scale(A_perm_mat, center = pca_B$center, scale = pca_B$scale)
  
  # 3. Project onto the principal component space (rotation matrix) of dataset B (MA)
  A_perm_proj <- A_perm_scaled %*% pca_B$rotation
  
  # 4. Compute cumulative variance explained across PCs
  vars_perm <- apply(A_perm_proj, 2, var)
  sim_results_perm[i, ] <- cumsum(vars_perm) / sum(vars_perm)
}

# 5. Summarize permutation null statistics: mean, 2.5th, and 97.5th percentiles
stats_permAontoB_df <- data.frame(
  PC = 1:n_col,
  Mean = colMeans(sim_results_perm),
  Lower = apply(sim_results_perm, 2, quantile, probs = 0.025),
  Upper = apply(sim_results_perm, 2, quantile, probs = 0.975)
)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Update plot: overlay the permutation null distribution
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
ggline(pca_compare, x = "PC", y = "Cumulative", color = "Type",
       numeric.x.axis = TRUE,
       xlab = "Principal Component of MA", 
       ylab = "Cumulative fraction of \n variance explained",
       legend.title="",
       ylim = c(0, 1.1)) +
  geom_line(data = stats_permAontoB_df, aes(x = PC, y = Mean), color = "gray20", size = 1) +
  geom_ribbon(data = stats_permAontoB_df, aes(x = PC, y = NULL, ymin = Lower, ymax = Upper), alpha = 0.2, fill = "black") +
  geom_point(data = stats_permAontoB_df, aes(x = PC, y = Mean), inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "gray20", size = 2) +
  theme_pubr()



Sys.time()
```
## 10.3. Log-transformed LMM without ancestor normalization (Four reps)
### 10.3.1 Fit LMM
```{r}
my_df<-gr_ma_df %>%
  select(lineage,Anc,round,Abb,mu_max_allrep) %>%
  rename(founder=Anc,carbon_source=Abb,growth_allrep=mu_max_allrep) %>%
  filter(round>0) %>%
  mutate(log_growth_allrep = log(growth_allrep)) # Add natural log transformation

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Fit random-slope model and extract summary statistics and slopes
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model: log_growth_allrep ~ round + founder + (1 + round | lineage)
# `(1 + round | lineage)` estimates random intercepts and random slopes
# for `round` for each lineage.

fit_random_slope_log_lmm_allrep <- function(df) {
  cs_name <- unique(df$carbon_source)
  
  # 1. Fit LMM (fall back to `lm` on convergence error)
  fit <- tryCatch({
    lmer(log_growth_allrep ~ round + founder + (1 + round | lineage), data = df)
  }, error = function(e) NULL)
  
  # Handle singular fit or convergence failure
  if (is.null(fit) || isSingular(fit)) {
    # If random slopes cannot be estimated, fall back to a fixed-effects
    # `lm` with lineage × round interactio
    fit_lm <- lm(log_growth_allrep ~ round * factor(lineage) + founder, data = df)
    
    # Extract per-lineage slopes from `lm` (main effect of `round` + interaction term)
    coefs <- summary(fit_lm)$coefficients
    base_slope <- coefs["round", "Estimate"]
    
    slopes_df <- tibble(lineage = paste0("lineage", 1:12)) %>%
      mutate(
        random_slope = map_dbl(lineage, function(l) {
          term <- paste0("round:factor(lineage)", l)
          if (term %in% rownames(coefs)) base_slope + coefs[term, "Estimate"] else base_slope
        })
      )
    
    res_df <- df %>% mutate(residual = residuals(fit_lm))
    var_slope <- var(slopes_df$random_slope)
    p_val_slope <- NA_real_ # Skip likelihood-ratio test for `lm` fallback
    
    # Approximate R² for `lm` fallback
    r2_cond <- cor(df$log_growth_allrep, predict(fit_lm))^2
    r2_marg <- NA_real_ # Not separable for `lm` with interactions
    
    
  } else {
    # Normal fit: extract random effects (Random Slopes)
    ranef_res <- ranef(fit)$lineage
    # Add the overall fixed-effect slope (β₁) and the lineage-specific
    # deviation (b_j) to obtain the effective slope for each lineage.
    fix_slope <- fixef(fit)["round"]
    
    slopes_df <- ranef_res %>%
      rownames_to_column("lineage") %>%
      mutate(random_slope = fix_slope + round) %>%
      select(lineage, random_slope)
    
    res_df <- df %>% mutate(residual = residuals(fit))
    
    # Variance of the random slope effect (variability in evolutionary
    # trends across lineages): σ²_slope
    vc <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(fit))
    var_slope <- vc %>% filter(grp == "lineage", var1 == "round") %>% pull(vcov)
    if (length(var_slope) == 0) var_slope <- 0
    
    # Test significance of random slopes via Likelihood Ratio Test
    # against a random-intercept-only model
    fit_null <- lmer(log_growth_allrep ~ round + founder + (1 | lineage), data = df, REML = FALSE)
    fit_full <- lmer(log_growth_allrep ~ round + founder + (1 + round | lineage), data = df, REML = FALSE)
    lrt <- anova(fit_null, fit_full)
    p_val_slope <- lrt$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2]
    
    # Approximate R² from `lmer`
    pred_cond <- predict(fit)                    # Fixed effects + random effects
    pred_marg <- predict(fit, re.form = NA)      # Fixed effects only
    
    r2_cond <- cor(df$log_growth_allrep, pred_cond)^2   # Approximate Conditional R²
    r2_marg <- cor(df$log_growth_allrep, pred_marg)^2   # Approximate Marginal R²
    
  }
  
  return(list(
    res_df = res_df,
    slopes_df = slopes_df %>% mutate(carbon_source = cs_name),
    var_summary = tibble(
      carbon_source = cs_name, 
      var_slope = var_slope, 
      p_val_slope = p_val_slope,
      r2_cond = r2_cond,  
      r2_marg = r2_marg   
      )
  ))
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Apply to all carbon sources at once
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
log_lmm_results_allrep <- my_df %>%
  split(.$carbon_source) %>%
  purrr::map(fit_random_slope_log_lmm_allrep)

# A. Reconstruct the residual data frame
log_res_df_rs_allrep <- map_dfr(log_lmm_results_allrep, ~ .x$res_df)
# 1. Build new residual matrix
log_res_matrix_rs_allrep <- log_res_df_rs_allrep %>%
  mutate(sample_id = paste(lineage, round, sep = "_")) %>%
  select(sample_id, carbon_source, residual) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon_source, values_from = residual) %>%
  column_to_rownames("sample_id")

# 2. Compute residual correlation matrix (Spearman)
log_res_corr_rs_allrep <- Hmisc::rcorr(as.matrix(log_res_matrix_rs_allrep), type = "spearman")
corr_matrix_log_residual_rs_allrep <- log_res_corr_rs_allrep$r



# B. Extract the matrix of evolutionary rates (slopes b_{jk})
#    for each carbon source × lineage
log_slopes_df_all_allrep <- map_dfr(log_lmm_results_allrep, ~ .x$slopes_df)

log_slope_matrix_allrep <- log_slopes_df_all_allrep %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon_source, values_from = random_slope) %>%
  column_to_rownames("lineage")

# C. Variance summary of evolutionary trajectory divergence
#    (variability in slopes across lineages) for each carbon source
var_summary_df <- map_dfr(log_lmm_results_allrep, ~ .x$var_summary)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Inspect analysis results and output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# ① Check whether the divergence in evolutionary trends across lineages
#   (variance of random slopes) is significant for each carbon source
cat("=== Summary of evolutionary slope variance (variability) per carbon source ===\n")
print(head(var_summary_df))
print(var_summary_df,n=22)

# ② Correlation analysis of per-lineage evolutionary slope vectors
#   (12 lineages × ~30 carbon sources)
#   (Do lineages that decline on one carbon source tend to
#    decline/increase on another?)）
log_slope_corr_allrep <- rcorr(as.matrix(log_slope_matrix_allrep), type = "spearman")
corr_matrix_log_slope_allrep <- log_slope_corr_allrep$r
p_matrix_log_slope_allrep    <- log_slope_corr_allrep$P
Sys.time()
```

### 10.3.4 Correlation analysis using cosine similarity
```{r}
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Inter-carbon-source correlation via cosine similarity of residual vectors
# (alternative to Spearman correlation)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# `log_res_matrix_rs_allrep` is a (sample_id × carbon source) matrix.
# Cosine similarity between carbon sources is computed column-wise
# (equivalent to operating on the transposed matrix).

# Scale the residual matrix (column-wise z-score) before computing cosine similarity.
# Note: scaling is optional; residuals are already close to zero mean,
# so this step may be omitted.
log_res_matrix_scaled <- scale(log_res_matrix_rs_allrep)

# Cosine similarity matrix (carbon source × carbon source)
cos_sim_matrix_residual_allrep <- coop::cosine(log_res_matrix_scaled)

# Comparison with the Spearman correlation matrix
cos_sim_df <- cos_sim_matrix_residual_allrep %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("carbon1") %>%
  pivot_longer(-carbon1, names_to = "carbon2", values_to = "cos_sim")

spearman_df <- corr_matrix_log_residual_rs_allrep %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("carbon1") %>%
  pivot_longer(-carbon1, names_to = "carbon2", values_to = "spearman_r")

comparison_df <- left_join(cos_sim_df, spearman_df, by = c("carbon1", "carbon2")) %>%
  filter(carbon1 > carbon2)

# Check agreement between the two measures
cor.test(comparison_df$cos_sim, comparison_df$spearman_r, method = "spearman")
```

### 10.3.6 Lag-1 autocorrelation of residual change vectors
```{r}
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Compute the change vector Δϵ for each lineage and step (round-to-round)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
delta_df <- log_res_df_rs_allrep %>%
  select(lineage, founder, round, carbon_source, residual) %>%
  arrange(lineage, carbon_source, round) %>%
  group_by(lineage, founder, carbon_source) %>%
  mutate(delta_res = residual - lag(residual)) %>% # Round-to-round change: Δϵ_t = ϵ_t − ϵ_{t−4}
  filter(!is.na(delta_res)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Helper function to compute cosine similarity
calc_cosine <- function(v1, v2) {
  sum(v1 * v2) / (sqrt(sum(v1^2)) * sqrt(sum(v2^2)))
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Cosine similarity for consecutive step pairs within the same lineage (Observed)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Reshape change vectors per lineage and round into wide format
delta_wide <- delta_df %>%
  mutate(step = paste0(round - 4, "to", round)) %>% 
  select(lineage, founder, step, carbon_source, delta_res) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon_source, values_from = delta_res)

# Extract consecutive step pairs (e.g., "4to8" and "8to12") and compute cosine similarity
steps <- unique(delta_wide$step)
# Set step ordering: "4to8", "8to12", "12to16", "16to20", "20to24", "24to28"
step_pairs <- tibble(
  step1 = steps[-length(steps)],
  step2 = steps[-1]
)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Cosine similarity for consecutive step pairs within the same lineage (Observed)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
obs_results <- delta_wide %>%
  group_by(lineage, founder) %>%
  nest() %>%
  mutate(cosine_sims = purrr::map(data, function(df_lineage) {
    step_pairs %>%
      rowwise() %>%
      mutate(cos_sim = {
        v1 <- df_lineage %>% filter(step == step1) %>% select(-step) %>% unlist()
        v2 <- df_lineage %>% filter(step == step2) %>% select(-step) %>% unlist()
        if (length(v1) > 0 && length(v2) > 0) calc_cosine(v1, v2) else NA_real_
      })
  })) %>%
  select(-data) %>%
  unnest(cosine_sims) %>%
  filter(!is.na(cos_sim))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Generate null model (cosine similarity from cross-lineage shuffling)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
set.seed(42)
n_perm <- 1000

null_cos_sims <- numeric(n_perm)

for (i in 1:n_perm) {
  # Randomly select two distinct lineages and compute cosine similarity
  # for a random consecutive step pair
  l1 <- sample(unique(delta_wide$lineage), 1)
  l2 <- sample(setdiff(unique(delta_wide$lineage), l1), 1)
  
  pair_idx <- sample(seq_len(nrow(step_pairs)), 1)
  s1 <- step_pairs$step1[pair_idx]
  s2 <- step_pairs$step2[pair_idx]
  
  v1 <- delta_wide %>% filter(lineage == l1, step == s1) %>% select(-lineage, -founder, -step) %>% unlist()
  v2 <- delta_wide %>% filter(lineage == l2, step == s2) %>% select(-lineage, -founder, -step) %>% unlist()
  
  if (length(v1) > 0 && length(v2) > 0) {
    null_cos_sims[i] <- calc_cosine(v1, v2)
  }
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Statistical test (Observed vs. Null)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Wilcoxon rank-sum test
test_res <- wilcox.test(obs_results$cos_sim, null_cos_sims, alternative = "two.sided")

cat("=== Analysis results ===\n")
cat("Mean cosine similarity of observed values:", mean(obs_results$cos_sim), "\n")
cat("Mean cosine similarity of null model (shuffled):", mean(null_cos_sims), "\n")
cat("Wilcoxon p-value:", test_res$p.value, "\n")

cat("SD of observed values:", sd(obs_results$cos_sim), "\n")
cat("SE of observed values:", sd(obs_results$cos_sim) / sqrt(nrow(obs_results)), "\n")
cat("n of observed values:", nrow(obs_results), "\n")
Sys.time()
```

```{r,fig.width=4,fig.height=3,dpi=300}
# 1. Clustering based on experimental evolutionary distances
# Define the number of theoretical clusters (k)
k_val <- 2

dist_exp<-ma_dist_matrix_log_lmmrs_allrep
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method)
cluster_exp    <- cutree(hc_exp, k = k_val)

# Create a mapping table for carbon sources and their assigned clusters
my_tmp<-data.frame(carbon=names(cluster_exp),exp=cluster_exp)
carbon_clust_tbl<-my_tmp
my_tmp1<-my_tmp %>% rename(carbon1=carbon,exp1=exp)
my_tmp2<-my_tmp %>% rename(carbon2=carbon,exp2=exp)

# Print carbon sources belonging to each cluster for inspection
for(i in 1:k_val){
  paste("cluster ",i,": ",paste(my_tmp[my_tmp$exp==i,]$carbon,collapse = ","),sep="") %>% print()
}

# 2. Data Integration
# Focus on unique pairs (upper triangle) and join with cluster assignments
my_map<-carbon_pairs_all %>%
  select(carbon1,carbon2,key,category1,category2,pair_category,category_col)
my_dist_df<-ma_pair_log_lmmrs_allrep %>%
  left_join(my_tmp1,by="carbon1") %>%
  left_join(my_tmp2,by="carbon2") %>%
  filter(key=="upper")

my_clstrs<-seq(1,k_val)

# ==========================================
# 3. Reshape data: automatically assign cluster numbers based on Upper Glycolysis count
# ==========================================
# Count the number of Upper Glycolysis carbon sources within each cluster
# based on the raw assignment (exp = 1, exp = 2, etc.)
cluster_counts <- my_dist_df %>%
  mutate(pair_type_raw = case_when(
    exp1 == 1 & exp2 == 1 ~ "C1",
    exp1 == 2 & exp2 == 2 ~ "C2",
    TRUE                  ~ "Between"
  )) %>%
  # Retain within-cluster pairs only and tally Upper Glycolysis counts per cluster
  filter(pair_type_raw %in% c("C1", "C2")) %>%
  group_by(pair_type_raw) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(upper_glyco_count = sum(pair_category == "Upper Glycolysis", na.rm = TRUE))

# Identify the original cluster label containing more Upper Glycolysis carbon sources
# (ties are broken in favour of the original C1)
target_raw_c1 <- cluster_counts$pair_type_raw[which.max(cluster_counts$upper_glyco_count)]

# Reassign cluster labels so that the cluster with more Upper Glycolysis
# carbon sources becomes Cluster 1
plot_df <- my_dist_df %>%
  mutate(
    pair_type = case_when(
      exp1 == 1 & exp2 == 1 ~ if_else(target_raw_c1 == "C1", "Cluster 1", "Cluster 2"),
      exp1 == 2 & exp2 == 2 ~ if_else(target_raw_c1 == "C2", "Cluster 1", "Cluster 2"),
      TRUE                  ~ "Between"
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(pair_type = factor(pair_type, levels = c("Cluster 1", "Cluster 2", "Between")))

# Report which original cluster was assigned as the new Cluster 1
print(paste("Cluster with more Upper Glycolysis carbon sources assigned as 'Cluster 1'. Original cluster:", target_raw_c1))


# ==========================================
# 4. Visualization and statistical testing
# ==========================================
# Embed wilcox.test directly within ggboxplot to reliably avoid mapping errors
p_integrated <- ggboxplot(
  plot_df,
  x = "pair_type", 
  y = "correlation_rsdl",
  ylab = "Residual correlation [-]", 
  xlab = "",
  add = "jitter", 
  add.params = list(alpha = 0.4, size = 1.5), 
  theme = theme_pubr(base_size = 20)
) +
  font("xy.text", size = 18) +
  font("ylab", size = 18) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-0.4, 1.0, by = 0.4), limits = c(-0.4, 1.3)) +
  stat_pwc(
    method = "wilcox.test",
    ref.group = "Between",      
    p.adjust.method = "BH",     
    label = "p.adj.signif",     
    tip.length = 0,
    bracket.nudge.y = 0.05, 
    hide.ns = TRUE              
  )

print(p_integrated)


# ==========================================
# 5. Detailed statistical output (for inspection)
# ==========================================
stat_test <- plot_df %>%
  wilcox_test(
    formula = correlation_rsdl ~ pair_type,
    ref.group = "Between",
    p.adjust.method = "BH"
  )
print("Detailed adjusted p-values compared to Between:")
print(stat_test)

# Extract a mapping table of carbon sources to their new cluster labels (Cluster 1 / 2)
# from plot_df. Note: this carries forward the cluster definition corrected by
# Upper Glycolysis count.
cbnclust_tbl_marsdlbased_allrep <- plot_df %>%
  # Build the mapping from carbon1 and carbon2 so that each carbon source
  # appears as a separate row
  select(carbon = carbon1, pair_type) %>%
  bind_rows(select(plot_df, carbon = carbon2, pair_type)) %>%
  filter(pair_type %in% c("Cluster 1", "Cluster 2")) %>%
  distinct(carbon, pair_type)


Sys.time()
```

```{r, fig.width=1.5,fig.height=3.5,dpi=300}

# Flux-based distance and Phenotypic distance from Growth rates
dist_exp<-as.dist(1 - ma_matrix_log_lmmrs_allrep)
my_ins<-rownames(ma_matrix_log_lmmrs_allrep)
dist_theory<-mean_carbon_dist_matrix[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------ cosine distance


# Hierarchical clustering using Ward's D2 method
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = cl_method)
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method)

dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# 2. Untangle: Optimize the layout of the two dendrograms to minimize crossings
# Maintaining the topology while rotating branches for better visualization
dl <- dendlist(dend_theory, dend_exp)
dl_untangled <- dendextend::untangle(dl, method = "step2side")

dend_p <- dl_untangled[[1]] # Optimized FBA-based dendrogram
dend_t <- dl_untangled[[2]] # Optimized Growth-based dendrogram


# 3. Create color vectors based on labels
# Retrieve current label order from the left (FBA) dendrogram
current_labels_p <- labels(dend_p)
# Map categories and colors to the current labels
groups_p <- carbon_labels_ordered_cos$Category[match(current_labels_p, carbon_labels_ordered_cos$label)]
col_vector_p <- carbon_labels_ordered_cos$Category_col[match(current_labels_p, carbon_labels_ordered_cos$label)]

# 4. Set label colors
dend_p <- dend_p %>% set("labels_colors", col_vector_p)

# Match Growth-based tree labels with the FBA-based tree's color vector
dend_t <- dend_t %>% 
  set("labels_colors", col_vector_p[match(labels(dend_t), current_labels_p)])

# 5. Draw Tanglegram
# Visualizing the structural similarity between metabolic theory and growth phenotype
tanglegram(dend_p, dend_t,
           common_subtrees_color_lines = FALSE, 
           highlight_distinct_edges = FALSE,
           highlight_branches_lwd = FALSE,
           color_lines = col_vector_p, 
           main_left = "Flux",
           main_right = "Growth",
           lab.cex = 1,
           lwd=2,
           columns_width = c(4, 1.5, 4),
           margin_inner = 3.5,
           margin_outer = 0.5,
           axes = FALSE)


# 6. Permutation Test for Entanglement Score
# Lower entanglement indicates higher structural similarity
actual_ent <- entanglement(dl_untangled) # Entanglement score after untangling

print(Sys.time())
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- if_else(iteration_scale=="large",1000,10)
perm_ent <- numeric(n_perm)

# Fixed theory-based labels
labels_theory <- labels(dend_p)

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # Copy the experimental dendrogram and shuffle labels
  shuffled_dend <- dend_t
  labels(shuffled_dend) <- sample(labels_theory)
  
  # Calculate entanglement for the shuffled pair after untangling
  perm_dends <- dendlist(dend_p, shuffled_dend) %>% 
    dendextend::untangle(method = "step2side")
  perm_ent[i] <- entanglement(perm_dends)
  
  # Progress monitoring
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# 7. Calculate P-value
# P-value = Probability that random entanglement is lower than the observed value
p_val_ent <- sum(perm_ent <= actual_ent) / n_perm

# 8. Visualization of results
hist(perm_ent, main="Permutation Test for Entanglement", 
     xlab="Entanglement Score", xlim=c(0, 1))
abline(v = actual_ent, col = "red", lwd = 2)
cat(sprintf("Actual Entanglement: %.3f\nP-value: %.4f\n", actual_ent, p_val_ent))

Sys.time()
```
##### 10.3.11.1.2 Cophenetic correlation with permutation test (Fig. 5f)
```{r}
# 1. Prepare distance matrices and initial dendrograms
dist_exp<-as.dist(1 - ma_matrix_log_lmmrs_allrep)
my_ins<-rownames(ma_matrix_log_lmmrs_allrep)

# Flux-based metabolic distance
dist_theory<-mean_carbon_dist_matrix[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------ cosine distance

# Hierarchical clustering
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = cl_method)
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method)

dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# Calculate observed Cophenetic correlation (Spearman)
# This measures how well the tree structure reflects the original distance matrix
actual_cor <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_exp, method = "spearman")

# --- Permutation Test for Cophenetic Correlation ---
print(Sys.time())
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- 1000
perm_results <- data.frame(cor = numeric(n_perm))

# Get original labels (strain names) from the experimental distance matrix
exp_labels <- rownames(as.matrix(dist_exp))

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # 1. Shuffle labels while keeping the underlying matrix structure intact
  dist_shuffled <- dist_exp
  shuffled_labels <- sample(exp_labels)
  
  # Convert to matrix to reassign shuffled names
  temp_mat <- as.matrix(dist_shuffled)
  rownames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  colnames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  
  # 2. Reconstruct dendrogram from the shuffled distance matrix
  hc_shuffled <- hclust(as.dist(temp_mat), method = cl_method)
  dend_shuffled <- as.dendrogram(hc_shuffled)
  
  # 3. Calculate and store the correlation for this permutation
  perm_results$cor[i] <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_shuffled, method = "spearman")
  
  # Progress monitoring
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# --- Statistical Evaluation ---
# P-value: Proportion of permutations where correlation is equal to or greater than observed
p_val_cor <- sum(perm_results$cor >= actual_cor) / n_perm

cat("【Analysis Results】\n")
cat(sprintf("Cophenetic Cor (Spearman): %.3f (p = %.4f)\n", actual_cor, p_val_cor))

# --- Visualization: Cophenetic Correlation Bubble Plot ---
# 1. Prepare data and count overlapping points (ties) for bubble sizing
df_coph <- data.frame(
  Theory = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_theory)),
  Experiment = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_exp))
) %>%
  group_by(Theory, Experiment) %>%
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = 'drop') # 各座標の重複数をカウント

my_txt<-paste("R=",sprintf("%.3f",actual_cor),sep="")

# 2. Plotting with ggscatter
# Bubble size and color intensity are log2-scaled to visualize the density of distance pairs
ggscatter(df_coph, x = "Theory", y = "Experiment",
          size = "count",           # Map count to dot size
          fill = "count",           # Map count to fill color
          color = "black",          # Fix border color to black
          shape = 21,               # Use filled circles with borders
          alpha= 0.8,
          xlab = "Cophenetic distance (Theory)",
          ylab = "Cophenetic distance (Experiment)",
          title = "Cophenetic Correlation (Log-scaled Bubble Size)",
          ylim=c(0,3)) +
  # Apply log2 transformation to size and color to handle the wide range of counts
  scale_size_continuous(trans = "log2", range = c(1, 12), name = "Count (log2)") +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Greys", trans = "log2", direction = 1, name = "Count (log2)")+
  annotate("text", x = 1, y = 2.7, label = my_txt,)

Sys.time()
```

```{r, fig.width=1.5,fig.height=3.5,dpi=300}
  labels(shuffled_dend) <- sample(labels_theory)
  
  # Calculate entanglement for the shuffled pair after untangling
  perm_dends <- dendlist(dend_p, shuffled_dend) %>% 
    dendextend::untangle(method = "step2side")
  perm_ent[i] <- entanglement(perm_dends)
  
  # Progress monitoring
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# 7. Calculate P-value
# P-value = Probability that random entanglement is lower than the observed value
p_val_ent <- sum(perm_ent <= actual_ent) / n_perm

# 8. Visualization of results
hist(perm_ent, main="Permutation Test for Entanglement", 
     xlab="Entanglement Score", xlim=c(0, 1))
abline(v = actual_ent, col = "red", lwd = 2)
cat(sprintf("Actual Entanglement: %.3f\nP-value: %.4f\n", actual_ent, p_val_ent))

Sys.time()
```
##### 10.3.11.2.2 Cophenetic correlation with permutation test (Fig. S10d)
```{r}
# 1. Prepare distance matrices and initial dendrograms
dist_exp<-as.dist(1 - ma_matrix_log_lmmrs_allrep)
my_ins<-rownames(ma_matrix_log_lmmrs_allrep)
dist_theory<-dist_theory<-carbon_matrix_70gem[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------ 70 GEMs

# Hierarchical clustering
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = cl_method)
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = cl_method)

dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# Calculate observed Cophenetic correlation (Spearman)
# This measures how well the tree structure reflects the original distance matrix
actual_cor <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_exp, method = "spearman")

# --- Permutation Test for Cophenetic Correlation ---
print(Sys.time())
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- 1000
perm_results <- data.frame(cor = numeric(n_perm))

# Get original labels (strain names) from the experimental distance matrix
exp_labels <- rownames(as.matrix(dist_exp))

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # 1. Shuffle labels while keeping the underlying matrix structure intact
  dist_shuffled <- dist_exp
  shuffled_labels <- sample(exp_labels)
  
  # Convert to matrix to reassign shuffled names
  temp_mat <- as.matrix(dist_shuffled)
  rownames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  colnames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  
  # 2. Reconstruct dendrogram from the shuffled distance matrix
  hc_shuffled <- hclust(as.dist(temp_mat), method = cl_method)
  dend_shuffled <- as.dendrogram(hc_shuffled)
  
  # 3. Calculate and store the correlation for this permutation
  perm_results$cor[i] <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_shuffled, method = "spearman")
  
  # Progress monitoring
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# --- Statistical Evaluation ---
# P-value: Proportion of permutations where correlation is equal to or greater than observed
p_val_cor <- sum(perm_results$cor >= actual_cor) / n_perm

cat("【Analysis Results】\n")
cat(sprintf("Cophenetic Cor (Spearman): %.3f (p = %.4f)\n", actual_cor, p_val_cor))

# --- Visualization: Cophenetic Correlation Bubble Plot ---
# 1. Prepare data and count overlapping points (ties) for bubble sizing
df_coph <- data.frame(
  Theory = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_theory)),
  Experiment = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_exp))
) %>%
  group_by(Theory, Experiment) %>%
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = 'drop') # 各座標の重複数をカウント

my_txt<-paste("R=",sprintf("%.3f",actual_cor),sep="")

# 2. Plotting with ggscatter
# Bubble size and color intensity are log2-scaled to visualize the density of distance pairs
ggscatter(df_coph, x = "Theory", y = "Experiment",
          size = "count",           # Map count to dot size
          fill = "count",           # Map count to fill color
          color = "black",          # Fix border color to black
          shape = 21,               # Use filled circles with borders
          alpha= 0.8,
          xlab = "Cophenetic distance (Theory)",
          ylab = "Cophenetic distance (Experiment)",
          title = "Cophenetic Correlation (Log-scaled Bubble Size)",
          ylim=c(0,3)) +
  # Apply log2 transformation to size and color to handle the wide range of counts
  scale_size_continuous(trans = "log2", range = c(1, 12), name = "Count (log2)") +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Greys", trans = "log2", direction = 1, name = "Count (log2)")+
  annotate("text", x = 1, y = 2.7, label = my_txt,)

Sys.time()
```

### 10.3.14 Residual correlation of MA across clusters defined by other dataset
#### 10.3.14.1 defined by ECOR
```{r,fig.width=4,fig.height=3,dpi=300}
# Extract unique pairs (upper triangle) from the MA experimental data
ma_df_integrated <- ma_pair_log_lmmrs_allrep[ma_pair_log_lmmrs_allrep$key == "upper", ]

# Join the new cluster definition determined from ECOR analysis to the MA data
ma_tmp1 <- cbnclust_tbl_ecorbased_allrep %>% rename(carbon1 = carbon, cluster1_new = pair_type)
ma_tmp2 <- cbnclust_tbl_ecorbased_allrep %>% rename(carbon2 = carbon, cluster2_new = pair_type)

ma_df_integrated <- left_join(ma_df_integrated, ma_tmp1, by = "carbon1")
ma_df_integrated <- left_join(ma_df_integrated, ma_tmp2, by = "carbon2")


# ==========================================
# 2. Reshape data: define three groups with "Between" as the common reference
# ==========================================
ma_plot_df <- ma_df_integrated %>%
  mutate(
    pair_type = case_when(
      cluster1_new == "Cluster 1" & cluster2_new == "Cluster 1" ~ "Cluster 1", # Both carbon sources in Cluster 1
      cluster1_new == "Cluster 2" & cluster2_new == "Cluster 2" ~ "Cluster 2", # Both carbon sources in Cluster 2
      TRUE                                                      ~ "Between"   # All other pairs (cross-cluster, etc.)
    )
  ) %>%
  # Fix the display and test order to "Cluster 1, Cluster 2, Between"
  mutate(pair_type = factor(pair_type, levels = c("Cluster 1", "Cluster 2", "Between")))


# ==========================================
# 3. Visualization and statistical testing
# ==========================================
# Draw a boxplot using the residual correlation coefficients from the MA data
p_ma_integrated <- ggboxplot(
  ma_plot_df,
  x = "pair_type", 
  y = "correlation_rsdl",
  ylab = "Evolutionary correlation [-]", 
  xlab = "",
  add = "jitter", 
  add.params = list(alpha = 0.4, size = 1.5), 
  theme = theme_pubr(base_size = 20)
) +
  font("xy.text", size = 18) +
  font("ylab", size = 18) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-0.4, 1.0, by = 0.4), limits = c(-0.4, 1.3)) +
  # Automatically add Wilcoxon tests against "Between" as the reference group
  stat_pwc(
    method = "wilcox.test",
    ref.group = "Between",      
    p.adjust.method = "BH",     
    label = "p.adj.signif",     
    tip.length = 0,
    bracket.nudge.y = 0.05, 
    hide.ns = TRUE              
  )

print(p_ma_integrated)


# ==========================================
# 4. Detailed statistical output (for inspection)
# ==========================================
ma_stat_test <- ma_plot_df %>%
  wilcox_test(
    formula = correlation_rsdl ~ pair_type,
    ref.group = "Between",
    p.adjust.method = "BH"
  )
print("Detailed adjusted p-values compared to Between (MA dataset):")
print(ma_stat_test)

Sys.time()
```

### 10.3.15 PCA
#### 10.3.15.1  ECOR projected onto residual MA space (Fig. 5j)
```{r,fig.height=3,fig.width=3, dpi=300}

# Define common carbon sources between MA and ECOR
my_carbons<-ma_carbons[ma_carbons %in% ecor_carbons]
my_carbons<-my_carbons[order(my_carbons)]

# A (ECOR)
A_mat<-gr_ecor_df %>%
  select(strain,carbon,mu_max_allrep) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon,values_from = mu_max_allrep)
my_rows<-paste("ECOR",A_mat$strain,sep="_")
A_mat<-A_mat %>% select(my_carbons) %>% as.matrix()
rownames(A_mat)<-my_rows

# B (MA)
B_mat <- log_res_df_rs_allrep %>%
  rename(carbon = carbon_source) %>% 
  mutate(name = str_c(str_replace(lineage, "lineage", "L"), "@R", sprintf("%02d", round))) %>%
  select(name, carbon, residual) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon, values_from = residual) %>%
  column_to_rownames("name") %>%
  select(all_of(my_carbons)) %>%
  as.matrix()

# 1. Normalization
A_scaled <- scale(A_mat) # ECOR
B_scaled <- scale(B_mat) # MA

# 2. Extract principal components of (co-)variation across carbon sources
## 2.1. PCA for dataset B
pca_B <- prcomp(B_scaled, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)
## 2.2. PCA for dataset A
pca_A <- prcomp(A_scaled, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)

# 3. Calc. variance explained
## 3.1. for dataset B 
var_B_own <- pca_B$sdev^2 / sum(pca_B$sdev^2) # ratio of total variance
cum_B_own <- cumsum(var_B_own) # cumulative variance
## 3.2. for dataset A
var_A_own <- pca_A$sdev^2 / sum(pca_A$sdev^2)
cum_A_own <- cumsum(var_A_own)

# 4. Generate a dataframe for visualization
pca_summary <- data.frame(
  PC = 1:length(var_B_own),
  Variance = var_B_own,
  Cumulative = cum_B_own
)

# 5. Project A onto the principal component space of B
# Apply the principal component axis (rotation matrix) of B to A_scaled
# A_projected represents principal score (coordinates) of A in B's PC space.
A_projected <- scale(A_mat,center = pca_B$center,scale = pca_B$scale) %*% pca_B$rotation
var_A_on_B <- apply(A_projected, 2, var)
var_explained_A_on_B <- var_A_on_B / sum(var_A_on_B)
cum_A_on_B <- cumsum(var_explained_A_on_B)

# 6. Generate a dataframe for visualization
pca_compare <- data.frame(
  PC = rep(1:length(var_B_own), 2),
  Variance = c(var_B_own, var_explained_A_on_B),
  Cumulative = c(cum_B_own, cum_A_on_B),
  Type = rep(c("MA", "ECOR"), each = length(var_B_own))
)

# dataset B: MA
fviz_pca_biplot(pca_B, repel = TRUE, col.var = "red", col.ind = "grey50",labelsize = 2,arrowsize=0.3)+
  theme_pubr()
# dataset A: ECOR
fviz_pca_biplot(pca_A, repel = TRUE, col.var = "red", col.ind = "grey50",labelsize = 2,arrowsize=0.3)+
  theme_pubr()


#
pc_map<-data.frame(
  PC1=c(pca_B$x[,1],A_projected[,1]),
  PC2=c(pca_B$x[,2],A_projected[,2]),
  PC3=c(pca_B$x[,3],A_projected[,3]),
  Type=c(rep("MA",nrow(pca_B$x)),rep("ECOR",nrow(A_projected))),
  Name=c(rownames(pca_B$x),rownames(A_projected))
)
ggscatter(pc_map[pc_map$Type=="MA",],x="PC1",y="PC2",
          # repel = TRUE,label = "Name",font.label = c(6),
          color="#00BFC4",legend.title="",alpha=0.9)



# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Proposed null model: within-strain permutation of carbon source labels
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------


n_sim <- 1000
n_col <- length(my_carbons)
n_row <- nrow(A_mat)

sim_results_perm <- matrix(NA, nrow = n_sim, ncol = n_col)

set.seed(123) # 再現性の確保

for (i in 1:n_sim) {
  # 1. Randomly shuffle carbon source values (columns) within each strain (row).
  #    This preserves the marginal variance of each carbon source while
  #    destroying the cross-carbon correlation structure.
  A_perm_mat <- t(apply(A_mat, 1, sample))
  colnames(A_perm_mat) <- colnames(A_mat)
  
  # 2. Standardize using the PCA center and scale parameters from dataset B (MA)
  A_perm_scaled <- scale(A_perm_mat, center = pca_B$center, scale = pca_B$scale)
  
  # 3. Project onto the principal component space (rotation matrix) of dataset B (MA)
  A_perm_proj <- A_perm_scaled %*% pca_B$rotation
  
  # 4. Compute cumulative variance explained across PCs
  vars_perm <- apply(A_perm_proj, 2, var)
  sim_results_perm[i, ] <- cumsum(vars_perm) / sum(vars_perm)
}

# 5. Summarize permutation null statistics: mean, 2.5th, and 97.5th percentiles
stats_permAontoB_df <- data.frame(
  PC = 1:n_col,
  Mean = colMeans(sim_results_perm),
  Lower = apply(sim_results_perm, 2, quantile, probs = 0.025),
  Upper = apply(sim_results_perm, 2, quantile, probs = 0.975)
)

ggline(pca_compare, x = "PC", y = "Cumulative", color = "Type",
       numeric.x.axis = TRUE,
       xlab = "Principal Component of MA", 
       ylab = "Cumulative fraction of \n variance explained",
       legend.title="",
       ylim = c(0, 1.1)) +
  geom_line(data = stats_permAontoB_df, aes(x = PC, y = Mean), color = "gray20", size = 1) +
  geom_ribbon(data = stats_permAontoB_df, aes(x = PC, y = NULL, ymin = Lower, ymax = Upper), alpha = 0.2, fill = "black") +
  geom_point(data = stats_permAontoB_df, aes(x = PC, y = Mean), inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "gray20", size = 2) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = get_breaks(from=0,to=1,by=0.2))+
  theme_pubr()



Sys.time()
```

```{r}
# 1. Run Spearman correlation analysis for each carbon source
cor_results <- my_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(precul_od) & !is.na(residual)) %>% 
  group_by(carbon_source) %>%
  summarise(
    res = list(if(n() >= 3) cor.test(precul_od, residual, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE) else NULL)
  ) %>%
  filter(!map_lgl(res, is.null)) %>% 
  mutate(
    rho = map_dbl(res, ~ .x$estimate),
    p_value = map_dbl(res, ~ .x$p.value)
  ) %>%
  select(-res)

# 2. Correct p-values using the Benjamini–Hochberg method
cor_results <- cor_results %>%
  mutate(p_adj = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH"))


# 3. Extract significant results (e.g., adjusted p-value < 0.05)
significant_results <- cor_results %>%
  filter(p_adj < 0.05) %>%
  arrange(p_adj)

# Check results (return a message if no significant correlations are found)
if (nrow(significant_results) == 0) {
  message("No carbon sources with significant correlation found after Benjamini–Hochberg correction.")
} else {
  print(significant_results)
}
```

## X.1 ECOR projected onto MA space
```{r,fig.height=2.5,fig.width=2.5, dpi=300}
# Define common carbon sources between MA and ECOR
carbons_ecorma_common<-ma_carbons[ma_carbons %in% ecor_carbons]
carbons_ecorma_common<-carbons_ecorma_common[order(carbons_ecorma_common)]

# A (ECOR)
gr_ecor_com_mat<-gr_ecor_df %>%
  select(strain,carbon,mu_max) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon,values_from = mu_max)
my_rows<-paste("ECOR",gr_ecor_com_mat$strain,sep="_")
gr_ecor_com_mat<-gr_ecor_com_mat %>% select(carbons_ecorma_common) %>% as.matrix()
rownames(gr_ecor_com_mat)<-my_rows
A_mat<-gr_ecor_com_mat

# B (MA)
## Anc
gr_ma_anc_df<-gr_ma_df[gr_ma_df$round==0,] %>% distinct(carbon,.keep_all = TRUE) %>% select(lineage,round,carbon,rel_mu_max)
gr_ma_anc_df$name<-"MA_Anc@0"
## Offspring
gr_ma_offsp_df<-gr_ma_df[gr_ma_df$round!=0,] %>% select(lineage,round,carbon,rel_mu_max)
gr_ma_offsp_df$name<-paste(gr_ma_offsp_df$lineage,sprintf("%02d", gr_ma_offsp_df$round),sep="@R")
## Anc & Offspring
gr_ma_com_mat<-bind_rows(gr_ma_anc_df,gr_ma_offsp_df) %>% select(name,carbon,rel_mu_max)
gr_ma_com_mat<-gr_ma_com_mat%>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon,values_from = rel_mu_max)
my_rows<-gr_ma_com_mat$name
my_rows<-my_rows %>% str_replace_all(pattern = "lineage",replacement = "L")
gr_ma_com_mat<-gr_ma_com_mat %>% select(carbons_ecorma_common) %>% as.matrix()
rownames(gr_ma_com_mat)<-my_rows
B_mat<-gr_ma_com_mat


# 1. Normalization
A_scaled <- scale(A_mat) # ECOR
B_scaled <- scale(B_mat) # MA

# 2. Extract principal components of (co-)variation across carbon sources
## 2.1. PCA for dataset B
pca_B <- prcomp(B_scaled, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)
## 2.2. PCA for dataset A
pca_A <- prcomp(A_scaled, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)

# 3. Calc. variance explained
## 3.1. for dataset B 
var_B_own <- pca_B$sdev^2 / sum(pca_B$sdev^2) # ratio of total variance
cum_B_own <- cumsum(var_B_own) # cumulative variance
## 3.2. for dataset A
var_A_own <- pca_A$sdev^2 / sum(pca_A$sdev^2)
cum_A_own <- cumsum(var_A_own)

# 4. Generate a dataframe for visualization
pca_summary <- data.frame(
  PC = 1:length(var_B_own),
  Variance = var_B_own,
  Cumulative = cum_B_own
)

# 5. Project A onto the principal component space of B
# Apply the principal component axis (rotation matrix) of B to A_scaled
# A_projected represents principal score (coordinates) of A in B's PC space.
A_projected <- scale(A_mat,center = pca_B$center,scale = pca_B$scale) %*% pca_B$rotation
var_A_on_B <- apply(A_projected, 2, var)
var_explained_A_on_B <- var_A_on_B / sum(var_A_on_B)
cum_A_on_B <- cumsum(var_explained_A_on_B)

# 6. Generate a dataframe for visualization
pca_compare <- data.frame(
  PC = rep(1:length(var_B_own), 2),
  Variance = c(var_B_own, var_explained_A_on_B),
  Cumulative = c(cum_B_own, cum_A_on_B),
  Type = rep(c("MA", "ECOR"), each = length(var_B_own))
)

# dataset B: MA
fviz_pca_biplot(pca_B, repel = TRUE, col.var = "red", col.ind = "grey50",labelsize = 2,arrowsize=0.3)+
  theme_pubr()
# dataset A: ECOR
fviz_pca_biplot(pca_A, repel = TRUE, col.var = "red", col.ind = "grey50",labelsize = 2,arrowsize=0.3)+
  theme_pubr()


#
pc_map<-data.frame(
  PC1=c(pca_B$x[,1],A_projected[,1]),
  PC2=c(pca_B$x[,2],A_projected[,2]),
  PC3=c(pca_B$x[,3],A_projected[,3]),
  Type=c(rep("MA",nrow(pca_B$x)),rep("ECOR",nrow(A_projected))),
  Name=c(rownames(pca_B$x),rownames(A_projected))
)
ggscatter(pc_map[pc_map$Type=="MA",],x="PC1",y="PC2",
          # repel = TRUE,label = "Name",font.label = c(6),
          color="#00BFC4",legend.title="",alpha=0.9)



# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Proposed null model: within-strain permutation of carbon source labels
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

n_sim <- 1000
n_col <- length(carbons_ecorma_common)
n_row <- nrow(A_mat)

sim_results_perm <- matrix(NA, nrow = n_sim, ncol = n_col)

set.seed(123)

for (i in 1:n_sim) {
  # 1. Randomly shuffle carbon source values (columns) within each strain (row).
  #    This preserves the marginal variance of each carbon source while
  #    destroying the cross-carbon correlation structure.
  A_perm_mat <- t(apply(A_mat, 1, sample))
  colnames(A_perm_mat) <- colnames(A_mat)
  
  # 2. Standardize using the PCA center and scale parameters from dataset B (MA)
  A_perm_scaled <- scale(A_perm_mat, center = pca_B$center, scale = pca_B$scale)
  
  # 3. Project onto the principal component space (rotation matrix) of dataset B (MA)
  A_perm_proj <- A_perm_scaled %*% pca_B$rotation
  
  # 4. Compute cumulative variance explained across PCs
  vars_perm <- apply(A_perm_proj, 2, var)
  sim_results_perm[i, ] <- cumsum(vars_perm) / sum(vars_perm)
}

# 5. Summarize permutation null statistics: mean, 2.5th, and 97.5th percentiles
stats_permAontoB_df <- data.frame(
  PC = 1:n_col,
  Mean = colMeans(sim_results_perm),
  Lower = apply(sim_results_perm, 2, quantile, probs = 0.025),
  Upper = apply(sim_results_perm, 2, quantile, probs = 0.975)
)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Update plot: overlay the permutation null distribution
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
ggline(pca_compare, x = "PC", y = "Cumulative", color = "Type",
       numeric.x.axis = TRUE,
       xlab = "Principal Component of MA", 
       ylab = "Cumulative fraction of \n variance explained",
       legend.title="",
       ylim = c(0, 1.1)) +
  geom_line(data = stats_permAontoB_df, aes(x = PC, y = Mean), color = "gray20", size = 1) +
  geom_ribbon(data = stats_permAontoB_df, aes(x = PC, y = NULL, ymin = Lower, ymax = Upper), alpha = 0.2, fill = "black") +
  geom_point(data = stats_permAontoB_df, aes(x = PC, y = Mean), inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "gray20", size = 2) +
  theme_pubr()



Sys.time()
```

## X.5 Growth rate vs. PC1 for Revision
```{r,fig.height=2.5,fig.width=2.5}
# Define common carbon sources between MA and ECOR
carbons_ecorma_common<-ma_carbons[ma_carbons %in% ecor_carbons]
carbons_ecorma_common<-carbons_ecorma_common[order(carbons_ecorma_common)]

# A (ECOR)
gr_ecor_com_mat<-gr_ecor_df %>%
  select(strain,carbon,mu_max) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon,values_from = mu_max)
my_rows<-paste("ECOR",gr_ecor_com_mat$strain,sep="_")
gr_ecor_com_mat<-gr_ecor_com_mat %>% select(carbons_ecorma_common) %>% as.matrix()
rownames(gr_ecor_com_mat)<-my_rows
A_mat<-gr_ecor_com_mat

# B (MA)
## Anc
gr_ma_anc_df<-gr_ma_df[gr_ma_df$round==0,] %>% distinct(carbon,.keep_all = TRUE) %>% select(lineage,round,carbon,rel_mu_max)
gr_ma_anc_df$name<-"MA_Anc@0"
## Offspring
gr_ma_offsp_df<-gr_ma_df[gr_ma_df$round!=0,] %>% select(lineage,round,carbon,rel_mu_max)
gr_ma_offsp_df$name<-paste(gr_ma_offsp_df$lineage,sprintf("%02d", gr_ma_offsp_df$round),sep="@R")
## Anc & Offspring
gr_ma_com_mat<-bind_rows(gr_ma_anc_df,gr_ma_offsp_df) %>% select(name,carbon,rel_mu_max)
gr_ma_com_mat<-gr_ma_com_mat%>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon,values_from = rel_mu_max)
my_rows<-gr_ma_com_mat$name
my_rows<-my_rows %>% str_replace_all(pattern = "lineage",replacement = "L")
gr_ma_com_mat<-gr_ma_com_mat %>% select(carbons_ecorma_common) %>% as.matrix()
rownames(gr_ma_com_mat)<-my_rows
B_mat<-gr_ma_com_mat


# 1. Normalization
A_scaled <- scale(A_mat) # ECOR
B_scaled <- scale(B_mat) # MA

# 2. Extract principal components of (co-)variation across carbon sources
## 2.1. PCA for dataset B
pca_B <- prcomp(B_scaled, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)
## 2.2. PCA for dataset A
pca_A <- prcomp(A_scaled, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Extract PC scores and compute mean growth rates
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Dataset A (ECOR)
# Mean growth rate of each strain across the common carbon sources (row-wise mean)
mean_growth_A <- rowMeans(A_mat, na.rm = TRUE)
# PC1 and PC2 scores (projections onto the first and second principal components)
pc1_score_A <- pca_A$x[, "PC1"]
pc2_score_A <- pca_A$x[, "PC2"]

# Correlation tests: PC scores vs. mean growth rate (ECOR)
cor_test_A1 <- cor.test(mean_growth_A, pc1_score_A)
cat("--- ECOR (Dataset A) : PC1 vs Mean Growth Rate ---\n")
print(cor_test_A1)

cor_test_A2 <- cor.test(mean_growth_A, pc2_score_A)
cat("--- ECOR (Dataset A) : PC2 vs Mean Growth Rate ---\n")
print(cor_test_A2)


# Dataset B (MA)
# Mean relative growth rate of each strain across the common carbon sources (row-wise mean)
mean_growth_B <- rowMeans(B_mat, na.rm = TRUE)
# PC1 and PC2 scores (projections onto the first and second principal components)
pc1_score_B <- pca_B$x[, "PC1"]
pc2_score_B <- pca_B$x[, "PC2"]

# Correlation tests: PC scores vs. mean growth rate (MA)
cor_test_B1 <- cor.test(mean_growth_B, pc1_score_B)
cat("\n--- MA (Dataset B) : PC1 vs Mean Growth Rate ---\n")
print(cor_test_B1)

cor_test_B2 <- cor.test(mean_growth_B, pc2_score_B)
cat("\n--- MA (Dataset B) : PC2 vs Mean Growth Rate ---\n")
print(cor_test_B2)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Scatter plot visualization (ggplot2)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Assemble data frames for plotting
df_A <- data.frame(
  Strain = rownames(A_mat),
  Mean_Growth = mean_growth_A,
  PC1 = pc1_score_A,
  Dataset = "ECOR (A)"
)

df_B <- data.frame(
  Strain = rownames(B_mat),
  Mean_Growth = mean_growth_B,
  PC1 = pc1_score_B,
  Dataset = "MA (B)"
)

df_combined <- bind_rows(df_A, df_B)

ggplot(df_combined, aes(x = PC1, y = Mean_Growth)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "darkred", se = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~ Dataset, scales = "free") +
  labs(
    title = "Correlation between PC1 Score and Mean Growth Rate",
    x = "PC1 Score",
    y = "Mean Growth Rate (Across Common Carbons)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


Sys.time()
```
